（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. M. REGISTRY No. S n. D. 849 F/52 Date 31-2-41）

Special Branch Station. File No. Date July 30, 1941

SUBJECT: "THE GLOBE" - Application for registration with the Shanghai Municipal Police.

"THE GLOBE," published by the Globe Publishing Co., a subsidiary of Messrs. Max Noessler & Co., is a monthly magazine in the English language intended to bring to the notice of the English reading Shanghai public the economic strength of the Axis powers, particularly German. The alleged proprietor and Chief Editor, Eduard ORENAUS and Rudolf SOMMER respectively, are both Germans. ORENAUS, a resident of Shanghai for over seventeen years is the proprietor of Max Noessler & Co., while SOMMER, who arrived in Shanghai from the United States in April of this year, declares himself to be a free-lance journalist.

The magazine itself is simply pro-German propaganda intended for consumption among English reading peoples. The majority of articles appearing therein are translations from German or German-controlled publications in Europe.

ORENAUS is responsible, according to his own statement, for the publishing of the magazine and should registration of the magazine be approved, the certificate should be made out in his name. SOMMER translates the articles from the German language and plays a minor part in the publication.

Despite the fact that both ORENAUS and SOMMER deny that "THE GLOBE" is subsidized by Nazi Party funds, the belief is held that the German Press Attache's office is the organ responsible for this paper.

A.G. (Special Branch).
（签名：Ja. Rees）

主题：“环球”（THE GLOBE）- 向上海公共租界工部局警务处申请注册。

“环球”由麦克斯·诺斯勒公司 (Max Noessler & Co.) 的子公司环球出版公司 (Globe Publishing Co.) 出版，是一份英文月刊，旨在向阅读英文的上海公众展示轴心国，特别是德国的经济实力。据称业主兼主编分别为爱德华·奥雷诺斯 (Eduard ORENAUS) 和鲁道夫·索默 (Rudolf SOMMER)，两人均为德国人。奥雷诺斯在上海居住已超过十七年，是麦克斯·诺斯勒公司的业主，而索默于今年四月从美国抵达上海，自称是自由撰稿记者。

该杂志本身仅仅是面向英语读者的亲德宣传品。其中刊登的大部分文章是从德国或欧洲受德国控制的出版物翻译而来的。

根据奥雷诺斯自己的说法，他负责杂志的出版工作，如果杂志注册获得批准，证书应以他的名义开具。索默负责将文章从德语翻译成英语，在出版工作中扮演次要角色。

尽管奥雷诺斯和索默都否认“环球”接受纳粹党资金的资助，但人们认为德国新闻参赞办公室是负责该报纸的机构。

Forwarded herewith is an application from Mr. J.M. Zakheim, a Soviet citizen, for the registration of "Our Epoch," a foreign language newspaper in Russian, to be published twice daily, morning and evening editions.

The applicant is editor and publisher of "The Epoch," a weekly illustrated magazine in Russian, and "Shih Tai" (时代), a Chinese edition of "The Epoch," and he is also the publisher of the "Daily War News."

Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date November 11, 1941.
SUBJECT: Der Kreis - German Monthly -
Application for Registration with S.M.P.
Attached herewith is the application form for
registration with the S.M.P. in respect of a German
language monthly publication to be called "DER KREIS"
(German for "Circle"). The object of the journal
is to awaken an interest in art in local refugee circles.
The publication will print only articles dealing with
art subjects and will have no political leanings and no
editorial policy.
The publisher of "Der Kreis" will be Bruno
Löwenberg, German Jewish Refugee, born December 16,
1890 in Stettin and residing at 5 Yang Terrace. Bruno
Löwenberg is the owner of the "Lion Book Shop" at 238
Moulmein Road. This store also conducts a lending
library and seems to be a fairly sound business. He
is the publication's main financial backer.
The editors of "Der Kreis" will be:-
Wolfgang Fränkel, German Jewish Refugee, born on
October 10, 1897 in Berlin; arrived in Shanghai in
May 1939. He is a musician and is employed with the
S.M.C. Municipal Orchestra.
and
Friedrich Karp, Austrian Jewish Refugee, born
September 15, 1901 in Vienna; arrived in Shanghai
on December 31, 1938. He is an accountant in the
employ of Messrs. Turner, Sturrock & Brown at 9 Ave.
Edward VII. Friedrich Karp is also a dillettante
novelist and art critic.
（批：Registry Prepare Certificate 11. 11. 41 [签名]）

SUBJECT: "SHANGHAI WOCHE" - German Weekly -
Application for Registration with S.M.P.

Attached herewith is the application form for
registration with the S.M.P. in respect of a German
language weekly publication to be called "SHANGHAI WOCHE"
(German for "Shanghai Weekly"). The proposed publication
will be unpolitical, dealing mostly with various
recreational subjects.

The publisher of the "Shanghai Woche" will be
Wolfgang FISCHER, German Jewish Refugee, residing at
26, Studley Avenue. In March 1939, Wolfgang Fischer
obtained Registration Certificate No. F-63 in respect
of a similar publication entitled "Shanghai Rundschau"
and in September 1940 he was issued with a Certificate
(F-89) in respect of "The 8 Uhr Abendblatt" a German
language daily evening paper. Both these papers are not
appearing at present.

Wolfgang Fischer has only some $500.00 with
which to start the publication. He is, however, a
veteran newspaperman and has a great circle of friends
in local refugee circles, who may assist him in establi-
shing his weekly. Fischer is a World War I Invalid,
in which he lost his right arm.

The paper will be printed by the "Mercury Press"
and sell at 30 cents per copy.

The publisher has been warned that, provided
permission is granted by the S.M.P., he has to submit
each publication to the Special Branch.

EVENING ECHO
NOV 21 1939

Big-Scale Contest
For Writers

Essays, Novels, Plays,
Songs And Ditties
Are Invited

China's literary talents will have an opportunity to display their wares in a large-scale contest in the writing of essays, novels, stage and screen plays, songs and ditties which has been announced by the "Ksing Kien Monthly," a local Chinese publication.

The competition, in which attractive cash prizes are offered, is said to be in connection with the movement for national reconstruction and Asiatic regeneration, with the establishment of peace in Asia as the basis.

According to the rules, each essay should contain not more than 5,000 words and based on these four points: (1) That China's present political, economic and social system is in a precarious state; (2) That a new ideology for the nation and a new order in the Far East should be established; (3) That the Communist and other doctrines have failed to improve the lot of the people; and (4) That geographical, historical and racial factors make the establishment of a new order in the Far East imperative. The best dissertation will be awarded a prize of $2,000, with minor prizes for nine others.

Novel On Life In China

For the novel, with a maximum of 30,000 words, real and actual life in present-day China should be depicted. First prize for this type of work is also $2,000.

As regards the stage or screen play, which should be written for a two-hour performance, a sum of $1,500 is offered for the first prize. The moving factors of current affairs in this country should be played up and given stress in the plot.

The song or ditty should treat of the ideal of Asiatic regeneration and the cause of national reconstruction, and should be as short as possible. $500 is to be awarded to the first-prize winner.

The contest will be closed at midnight, January 31, 1940 and the results will be announced publicly on May 1, 1940. Under tentative arrangements, it has been learnt that authors of the winning manuscripts will be entitled to a royalty of 30 per cent. of the proceeds realised from the sale of their works to be published in book form. They will also be published in the "Hsin Kien Monthly" and other magazines, it is stated.

Manuscripts should be addressed to Hsin China Box 1768.
page_data.zh:
EVENING ECHO
1939年11月21日

大规模征文比赛
面向作家

征集散文、小说、剧本、
歌曲和小调

据当地中文出版物《兴建月刊》（Ksing Kien Monthly）宣布，中国的文学人才将有机会在一次大规模的散文、小说、舞台剧和电影剧本、歌曲和小调创作比赛中展示他们的才华。

据悉，这次比赛提供诱人的现金奖励，与以亚洲和平为基础的国家重建和亚洲复兴运动有关。

根据规则，每篇散文不得超过5000字，并基于以下四点：(1) 中国目前的政治、经济和社会制度处于危险状态；(2) 应建立新的国家意识形态和远东新秩序；(3) 共产主义和其他学说未能改善人民的命运；(4) 地理、历史和种族因素使得建立远东新秩序成为当务之急。最佳论文将获得2000美元奖金，另有九篇获小额奖金。

关于中国生活的小说

小说字数上限为30000字，应描绘当今中国的真实生活。此类作品的一等奖也为2000美元。

至于舞台剧或电影剧本，应按两小时的演出时长编写，一等奖金额为1500美元。剧情应突出并强调本国当前时事的推动因素。

歌曲或小调应涉及亚洲复兴的理想和国家重建的事业，并应尽可能简短。一等奖获得者将获得500美元。

比赛将于1940年1月31日午夜截止，结果将于1940年5月1日公布。据初步安排，获悉获奖作品的作者有权获得其作品以书籍形式出版所得收益的30%作为版税。据悉，这些作品还将在《兴建月刊》和其他杂志上发表。

稿件请寄至 Hsin China Box 1768。

EVENING ECHO
01762'
FEB 1 6 1939

CRIME-RIDDEN SHANGHAI

THE approach of the old Chinese New Year, now known as the Spring Festival, is generally accompanied by an increase of crime. It is the most important day settlement day of the year and consequently many are forced to dishonest, to say nothing of desperate, remedies in order to meet their commitments.

Nowadays there are many factors contributing to an exacerbation of crime; some of them are political and are concerned with the current hostilities, while others may be described as economic. Scarcely a day passes without at least one—and generally several—armed robberies, hold-ups and shootings, which are keeping both the Settlement and the Concession police extremely busy.

There is much want in this city and those who are hungry become desperate, committing acts in their extremity which would never occur in more normal times. Together with the tens of thousands of refugees now being harboured in Shanghai have come many criminal characters, while there is reason to believe that not a few guerillas as well as soldiers who were formerly fighting with the Chinese armies, but who have been cut off from their units, have been forced through privation to seek a means of keeping body and soul together by joining the ranks of Shanghai's underworld.

It can be easily understood that, owing to the severe fighting in the areas surrounding Shanghai large quantities of firearms have found their way into the city, many of which were doubtless picked up from the corpses of dead soldiers, and these have found their way, together with large quantities of small-arms ammunition, into the hands of gangsters. Periods of warfare are the cause of large numbers of men becoming familiar with the use of firearms and the development of a psychosis which holds life cheap, so that they will take desperate risks with their own in the hope of securing a few dollars. It was only a day or two ago that a gangster met his death at the hands of the Settlement police in a running street fight after he had attempted to rob a blind fortune-teller.

Such men can be hired for a few dollars to commit political assassinations and many such have occurred in recent months, chiefly of those who have accepted office under the Ta Tao Government.

Assassinations perpetrated by crazed fanatics for political reasons are despicable enough, but it is impossible to find words to express sufficient contempt for those who commit such acts for money.

This city has always been a happy hunting ground for gamblers who have never found any lack of amenities for indulging their weakness, and present conditions lend themselves to an increase of such activities. "Easy money" invariably attracts large numbers of the worst elements with the result that even the fortunate minority who leave a "gambling-joint" with more in their pockets than when they entered are by no means sure of getting their cash or their persons safely home.

Allegations have been made of failure of the various authorities responsible for the maintenance of law and order to co-operate, but such are the present abnormal conditions in and around Shanghai that it is surprising that such a large percentage of those committing offences against the law are brought so swiftly to justice.

《晚声报》
01762'
1939年2月16日

罪恶滋生的上海

旧历新年（现称春节）的临近，通常伴随着犯罪率的上升。这是一年中最重要的结算日，因此许多人为了履行债务承诺，被迫采取不诚实的手段，更不用说铤而走险的极端措施了。

如今，有许多因素导致犯罪加剧；其中一些是政治性的，与当前的敌对行动有关，而另一些则可归结为经济因素。几乎每一天都至少发生一起——通常是多起——武装抢劫、拦路劫持和枪击事件，这使得租界警务处和法租界巡捕房都极度忙碌。

这座城市中存在大量的贫困现象，饥饿的人会变得绝望，在走投无路之际做出在较正常时期绝不会发生的举动。随着目前上海收容的数以万计的难民而来的，还有许多犯罪分子；同时有理由相信，不少游击队员以及此前曾在中国军队中作战但与部队失散的士兵，也因生活所迫，不得不加入上海黑社会的行列，以求维持生计。

不难理解，由于上海周边地区战事激烈，大量枪支流入本市，其中许多无疑是从阵亡士兵的尸体上捡拾而来，这些枪支连同大量轻武器弹药一起，落入了帮派分子手中。战争时期使得大量人员熟悉枪支的使用，并滋生出一种视生命如草芥的病态心理，以至于他们为了获取几美元，不惜拿自己的生命去冒极大的风险。就在前一两天，一名帮派分子在试图抢劫一位盲人算命先生后，在与租界警察的街头追逐搏斗中被击毙。

只需几美元便可雇佣此类人员实施政治暗杀，近几个月已发生多起此类事件，受害者主要是那些在“大道政府”任职的人员。

出于政治原因由疯狂 fanatic 实施的暗杀固然卑鄙，但对于那些为金钱而实施此类行为的人，任何言语都无法表达足够的蔑视。

这座城市历来是赌徒们的乐园，他们从不缺乏满足其嗜好的便利条件，而目前的局势助长了此类活动的增加。“快钱” invariably 吸引着大量最恶劣的分子，其结果是，即使是那些离开“赌窟”时口袋里比进去时更多的少数幸运儿，也绝无把握能平安带着现金或人身安全回家。

有人指责负责维护治安的各当局之间缺乏合作，但鉴于上海及其周边地区目前异常的状况，令人惊讶的是，如此高比例的违法者能被如此迅速地绳之以法。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

DEC 15 1938

Reporter Awarded $94.18
Judgment Against “Echo”

In the British Supreme Court this morning, Mr. K. M. Steiner, local reporter, was awarded a judgment for $94.18 in his suit against the Shanghai Evening Echo. The sum represents salaries due for services between November 5 and 19.

Judge Sir Alan Mossop, who handed down the judgment, also ordered the defendant to pay court costs amounting to $11.26 and $20 attorney’s fee.

Mr. Steiner, now working on a morning newspaper here, testified when cross-examined by his lawyer, Dr. Piero Terni, that he joined the Echo with the understanding that he would write headlines for telegrams and take charge of the local “coverage.” It turned out to be a much heavier work, he declared, as he had to handle the whole paper.

Working conditions on the paper were poor, the offices being not heated, he stated. When he asked for a stove, the Echo publisher is said to have offered to give him a coat—an old one.

On further questioning, Mr. Steiner declared that another reason for his resignation from the paper was his belief that the Echo was receiving subsidies from the Japanese or the “Ta Tao Government,” the latter apparently referring to the “City Government of Greater Shanghai.” He admitted, however, that this was but a hearsay.

After further deliberation, Judge Sir Alan delivered the judgment.

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
DEC 16 1938
Journalist's Claim
Against Publisher
Mr. L. F. Fearon Sued in
H.M. Supreme Court; Story
Of Impossible Conditions

Stating that the conditions under which he was supposed to work were impossible, thus forcing him to resign his position, a Shanghai journalist, Mr. Kurt Steiner, appeared as plaintiff in H.M. Supreme Court yesterday before Judge P. Grant Jones when he brought a claim against Mr. L. F. Fearon, publisher of the "Evening Echo," for $94.18, being 12 days' salary, and court costs.

Defendant did not appear in court and plaintiff, represented by Dr. P. V. E. Terni, told the court how he met Mr. Fearon in June before the original publication of the "Evening Echo." At the end of October, he stated, he received a telephone call from Mr. Fearon asking witness to meet him at the offices of the newspaper in the Central Arcade.

Defendant then offered him a position on the publication to write headings—"Which are usually most misleading" remarked the Judge—and cover the city news. Witness began work on November 3, the arrangement being that he should receive $250 as salary for the first month. He ceased to work for the newspaper on November 15.

Inadequate

During the time of his employment, witness stated that he informed Mr. Fearon of the inadequacy of the editorial offices there being only three typewriters for a staff of five. "When I joined" he continued "I discovered I was running the paper." There was no telephone in the office, merely an extension from the "China Press." It was impossible to carry on as the office was not heated and was dangerous to the employees, he added.

Due to irregular payments to the printers of the "Evening Echo," witness continued, the publication often appeared on the streets late and defendant had admitted that he was in arrears regarding payments to the printers, who were the International Corporation, printers of the "China Press."

On November 15 witness went to the business offices of the newspaper and typed a letter to Mr. Fearon resigning his position and asking for the salary due to him. In a telephone conversation defendant promised to pay the money on the following day. On November 17 another letter was sent and a reply was received stating that the money would be paid when the "Evening Echo's" account would be credited with expected funds.

Plaintiff added that it was impossible to assume responsibility for the [□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□]

1938年12月16日

记者起诉出版商
L. F. Fearon 先生被诉至英国在华最高法院；
关于无法工作之条件的陈述

上海记者 Kurt Steiner 先生昨日作为原告出现在英国在华最高法院 P. Grant Jones 法官面前，起诉《晚声报》（Evening Echo）出版商 L. F. Fearon 先生，索赔 94.18 美元（即12天的薪水）及诉讼费用。Steiner 先生称，他被迫辞职是因为其受雇工作的条件根本无法实现。

被告未出庭。由原告代理人 P. V. E. Terni 博士向法庭陈述，原告于《晚声报》正式创刊前的六月结识了 Fearon 先生。原告称，十月底，他接到 Fearon 先生的电话，要求证人在中央商场（Central Arcade）的报社办公室与其会面。

被告随后向原告提供在该出版物任职的机会，负责撰写标题——法官评论道“标题通常最具误导性”——并报道本市新闻。证人于11月3日开始工作，约定首月薪水为 250 美元。他于11月15日停止为该报工作。

条件不足

证人称，在受雇期间，他曾向 Fearon 先生指出编辑室条件简陋，五名职员仅有三台打字机。他继续说道：“当我入职时，我发现实际上是我一个人在操办这份报纸。”办公室内没有电话，仅有一部从《大陆报》（China Press）分出的分机。他补充说，由于办公室没有供暖，且对员工存在危险，工作无法继续进行。

证人继续称，由于《晚声报》未能按时向印刷商付款，该报经常延迟上市。被告已承认拖欠印刷商款项，这些印刷商是国际公司（International Corporation），即《大陆报》的印刷商。

11月15日，证人前往该报的业务办公室，给 Fearon 先生打了一封辞职信，并要求支付欠薪。在一次电话交谈中，被告承诺次日付款。11月17日，证人又发出一封信，收到回复称，待《晚声报》账户收到预期资金后，将支付款项。

原告补充说，不可能为 [□□□…] 承担责任

D 9.4.50'

EVENING ECHO

ENTER: THE EVENING ECHO

THE EVENING ECHO makes its first appearance today and we trust that those Shanghailanders who scan its modest four pages for the first time will remember that the acorn came before the oak.

We also derive considerable solace and encouragement from the reflection that the great James Gordon Bennett, founder of the New York Herald, started his paper (for which he charged one cent) in a cellar and was editor, publisher, printer, reporter and salesman.

He was frequently compelled in the last capacity to combine it with that of fistic handyman, as a number of his readers were unable to appreciate his frequent very outspoken and pungent comments concerning their real or fancied moral obliquities. These encounters in the journalistic cause usually occurred in the streets, so Bennett gained plenty of free publicity.

We trust, however, that we shall be spared this last, but not least, important phase of his many-sided activities.

Bennett fixed the policy of his paper from the very beginning and adhered to it to the day of his death. It was as follows:

“We shall support no party, be the agent of no faction or coterie, and care nothing for any election, or any candidate from president down to constable.”

We cannot do better than attempt a modest emulation of this policy.

We propose strictly to eschew all political matters, but shall not hesitate to take a strong view, when we consider it necessary, on matters concerning the public welfare of this city, among whose residents we trust we shall have a steadily increasing number of readers.

We were born in difficult times and no part of the world is now free from anxiety. He would be a bold man who ventured to predict what lies in store for the human race during the next few years or even months.

Here, for the past ten months, we have been in the midst of an undeclared war, with its inevitable concomitants of trade paralysis and uncertainty, but Shanghai has weathered many crises in the past, always shewing marvellous powers of resiliency and recuperation, and history has an uncanny habit of repeating itself.

Wars do not last forever and sooner or later the fabric of our commerce will again be found licking its wounds and those wounds will not prove fatal; they will, as always in the past, heal.

We have endeavoured to attune the rates of the EVENING ECHO to the times and are confident that they will make their appeal to the Shanghai public.

We trust that we may merit the very encouraging support which we have so far been accorded, both from those who have already enrolled themselves as subscribers, and from advertisers.

晚聲報

登场：《晚声报》

《晚声报》今日首次面世，我们希望那些第一次翻阅这 modest 四版内容的上海老居民们能记住，橡树源于橡果。

我们也从以下反思中获得极大的慰藉和鼓励：伟大的《纽约先驱报》创始人詹姆斯·戈登·贝内特（James Gordon Bennett）是在地下室创办他的报纸的（售价一美分），并且身兼编辑、出版人、印刷工、记者和销售员数职。

在担任销售员这一角色时，他经常被迫兼任拳脚打手，因为他的一些读者无法欣赏他对他们真实或想象中的道德败坏行为所发表的频繁、非常直率且辛辣的评论。这些为了新闻事业而发生的冲突通常发生在街头，因此贝内特获得了大量的免费宣传。

然而，我们希望不必经历他多方面活动中这最后但并非最不重要的阶段。

贝内特从一开始就确定了其报纸的方针，并坚持至死。方针如下：

“我们不支持任何政党，不做任何派系或小团体的代理人，不关心任何选举，也不关心从总统到巡捕的任何候选人。”

我们若能 modestly 效仿这一方针，便再好不过了。

我们提议严格回避所有政治事务，但在我们认为必要时，对于关乎本市公共福利的事项，我们将毫不犹豫地采取强硬立场；在我们希望读者群稳步增长的居民中，我们将致力于此。

我们诞生于艰难时期，如今世界没有一个地方免于焦虑。若是有人敢于预测未来几年甚至几个月人类将面临何种命运，那他必定是个大胆的人。

在这里，过去十个月我们一直处于一场未宣战的战争之中，随之而来的是贸易瘫痪和不确定性，但上海在过去曾渡过许多危机，总是展现出惊人的韧性和恢复力，而历史有着令人不安的重演习惯。

战争不会永远持续，迟早我们的商业结构会再次舔舐伤口，而这些伤口将被证明并非致命；它们将像过去一样愈合。

我们已努力使《晚声报》的价格适应时局，并相信这将吸引上海公众。

我们希望自己能配得上迄今为止获得的令人鼓舞的支持，这些支持既来自已登记订阅的读者，也来自广告商。

归档
DR 116

Dear Mr. Tabrum,

I am enclosing herewith a translation of
the brief item which appeared in the Japanese owned Sin
Shun Pao on October 21.

"The China Weekly Review which was bought over by
the Chungking Government printed in its last week's
issue an article entitled "Inside Nanking" which
not only defamed the government, but falsely re-
ported the facts. It is hoped that authorities will
give the paper a warning or a sanction."

The allegation that the China Weekly Review
has been "bought over" by Chungking is of course false. The
article which we published in our issue of October 18th on
page 191 "Inside Nanking" was actually written by a man who
is connected with the Nanking Government, hence presumably
is familiar with the situation.

With best wishes, I am,

Very truly yours,

J.B. Powell

page_data.en:
At 7.15.p.m. on 23.10.1941 Mr.J.B.Powell,
American Citizen, Editor of the China Weekly Review
of 160 Avenue Edward VII, came to station accompanied
by C.D.C. 62 (Crime Branch Headquarters and temporarily
acting as Mr.Powell's bodyguard) and C.P.C. 304 (C).
C.P.C.304 also brought to station one potato masher
type hand grenade which has been placed in safety
pending disposal on 24.10.1941.

Mr. Powell informed detectives that he left
his office at approximately 6.45.p.m. 23.10.1941 and
proceeded East on Avenue Edward VII turning North on
Szechuen Road. He walked on the west side pavement
of Szechuen Road and from a reconstruction was
about two to three feet from the building line.
Between Nos. 133 and 149 Szechuen Road there is a
lane protected by iron gates. As Mr.Powell was
passing this he was struck fairly forcibly on the
left upper arm by something which struck the corner
stone of No.149 about four feet away. The object was
obviously hard and fairly heavy and Mr.Powell invest-
igated. He discovered something wrapped in newspaper
which felt like a potato masher hand grenade.

Mr. Powell had been followed at a distance of
about 6 feet by his bodyguard, C.D.C.62, who upon
seeing the object strike Mr.Powell and thereafter
fall to the ground assisted in the investigation
and then turned about to see who threw the missile.
No suspect could be seen this section of the road being
at that time practically deserted. This C.D.C.then
called C.P.C.304 on duty at No.70 Szechuen Road who
upon arrival at the scene further examined the hand
page_data.zh:
1941年10月23日下午7时15分，美国公民、爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）160号《密勒氏评论报》（China Weekly Review）编辑J.B.鲍威尔（J.B. Powell）先生，在刑事部总部警员C.D.C. 62（临时担任鲍威尔先生的保镖）和巡捕C.P.C. 304 (C)的陪同下来到警局。C.P.C. 304还向警局提交了一枚土豆捣碎器型手榴弹，该手榴弹已处于安全状态，待1941年10月24日处置。

鲍威尔先生告知侦探，他于1941年10月23日下午6时45分左右离开办公室，沿爱多亚路向东行进，随后在四川路向北转弯。他走在四川路西侧的人行道上，根据现场重建，距离建筑红线约两至三英尺。在四川路133号至149号之间有一条由铁门保护的弄堂。当鲍威尔先生经过此处时，他的左上臂被某物相当用力地击中，该物体随后击中了约四英尺外的149号角石。该物体显然坚硬且相当沉重，鲍威尔先生随即进行了查看。他发现了一个用报纸包裹的东西，手感像是一枚土豆捣碎器型手榴弹。

鲍威尔先生身后约6英尺处跟着他的保镖C.D.C. 62，后者在看到物体击中鲍威尔先生并随后掉落在地后，协助进行了调查，然后转身查看是谁投掷了该投射物。由于该路段当时几乎空无一人，未能看到任何嫌疑人。随后，这名C.D.C.呼叫了在四川路70号执勤的C.P.C. 304，后者到达现场后进一步检查了这枚手

page_data.en:
3098/41.
1/3.

grenade and picking same up brought same to station.
Upon receipt of this report Officer I/c. Station,
D.O. "A" Division, D.C. (Divisions) and Mr.J.A.Collins,
U.S. Vice-Consul, were informed by D.I.Moir, Sen.Det/I/c.
Accompanied by complainant, C.D.C.62 and C.P.C.304
the scene of crime was visited and the crime reconstructed
It is found that the door of Imperial Chemical
Industries Building, 133 Szechuen Road, recesses from
the building line to the extent of 6 feet. The main
door was open and S.P.W. 172 was on duty in the main
hall but not actually at the door. This door is 55
feet from the point where the grenade struck complt.
It appears that complainant was practically in the
centre of the gateway to the lane dividing the above
building from No.149 Szechuen Road and was about
three feet from the building line. The grenade struck
him on the left upper arm (the arm nearest the wall)
and then carried forward striking the ground at the foot
of the building about four feet in front.
C.P.W. 1164 on duty in the aforementioned lane
was in his hut at the time and knew nothing of the
affair until informed by Police.
Both Mr. Powell and C.D.C.62 state that they saw
page_data.zh:
3098/41.
1/3.

榴弹，将其捡起并带回警局。接到此报告后，分区督察莫尔（Moir，高级侦探/负责人）通知了警局负责人、“A”分区副督察、分区副督察（各分区）以及美国副领事J.A.柯林斯（J.A. Collins）先生。在报案人、C.D.C. 62和C.P.C. 304的陪同下，相关人员走访了犯罪现场并进行了案情重建。经查，四川路133号帝国化学工业公司大楼（Imperial Chemical Industries Building）的大门向内凹陷，距建筑红线6英尺。大门敞开，特别巡捕S.P.W. 172正在大厅执勤，但并未实际守在门口。该门距离手榴弹击中报案人的地点55英尺。看来，报案人当时几乎正处在分隔上述大楼与四川路149号的弄堂入口中央，距离建筑红线约三英尺。手榴弹击中了他的左上臂（靠近墙壁的手臂），然后向前飞去，击中了前方约四英尺处的建筑物底部地面。

当时在上述弄堂内执勤的巡捕C.P.W. 1164正身处其岗亭内，直到警方告知后才知晓此事。
鲍威尔先生和C.D.C. 62均表示，他们看到

page_data.en:
3038/41.
1/4.

no-one moving in the immediate vicinity and no-one whom
they might consider suspicious.
On the roadway opposite to the spot where the
grenade struck Mr.Powell there was a motor truck Lic.
No.17274. This was drawn up near the curb and near a
S.P.Co. pole. From the reconstruction it appeared
impossible that anyone using the truck as cover could
have thrown the grenade to reach the spot where it struck
Mr.Powell.
There are three possibilities (1) One that it was
thrown at Mr.Powell from the front. This can be ruled
out as Mr.Powell would have seen the assailant. (2) that
it was thrown from above, namely, from one of the windows
of No.149 Szechuan Road and (3) that it was thrown from
behind which theory Mr.Powell believes the most likely.
In such a case the thrower would have been in rear of
C.D.C.62 and it is possible that he used the recess at
the main door of No.133 Szechuan Road to hide in and to
protect him from any possible blast. No-one having been
seen to move from the scene it is possible that the man
remained hidden or entered the offices unseen by the
S.P.V. on duty.
D.S.I.Chase, C.D.S.118 and C.D.C.132 made enquiries
page_data.zh:
3038/41.
1/4.

附近没有任何人移动，也没有发现任何可疑人员。
在手榴弹击中鲍威尔先生地点的对面道路上，停着一辆车牌号为17274的卡车。该车停靠在路边，靠近一根上海电力公司（S.P.Co.）的电杆。根据现场重建，任何人利用卡车作为掩护投掷手榴弹以击中鲍威尔先生所在地点似乎是不可能的。
存在三种可能性：(1) 从正面朝鲍威尔先生投掷。这一点可以排除，因为鲍威尔先生会看到袭击者。(2) 从上方投掷，即从四川路149号的其中一扇窗户投下；(3) 从背后投掷，鲍威尔先生认为这一理论最有可能。如果是这种情况，投掷者将位于C.D.C. 62的身后，他可能利用四川路133号大门处的凹进空间进行藏身，并保护自己免受可能的爆炸冲击。由于无人被看到从现场移动，此人可能一直藏匿，或在当值的特别巡捕（S.P.V.）未察觉的情况下进入了办公室。
副侦探长蔡斯（Chase）、刑事部警员C.D.S. 118和C.D.C. 132进行了询问

page_data.en:
3098/41.

1/5.

in the vicinity of the scene of crime but no witnesses
could be located. As stated this section of Szechuen Road
was very deserted at the time of detectives' visit and
Mr.Powell stated that it was about the same when the
incident occurred.

Mr.Powell stated that he has not recently received
any threats but on the 22.10.1941 an article appeared
in the Sing Shan Pao (新申报) Pro- Nanking Daily
newspaper, which criticised an article appearing in last
week's issue of the China Weekly Review and claiming that
a strong protest would be lodged. Mr.Powell thought that
the attempted bombing might be the protest referred to.

The grenade was wrapped in paper from the Sin Wan Pao
dated 19.9.1941 which throws no light on the case.

A small sketch plan is attached showing the scene
of crime.

R.M.瑞
Sen.Det.I/c.

鲍威尔先生表示，他最近未收到任何威胁，但在1941年10月22日，亲南京日报《新申报》（Sing Shan Pao）上刊登了一篇文章，批评了上周《密勒氏评论报》上刊登的一篇文章，并声称将提出强烈抗议。鲍威尔先生认为，此次未遂的炸弹袭击可能就是所指的抗议行为。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
JUL 1 1941.

（批：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
D.8149 F.23
1 - 7-41）

American Weekly's
Issues Seized by
Municipal Police

The Shanghai Municipal Police having confiscated all issues of the "China Weekly Review" dated June 21, Lieut.-Col. Kimio Akiyama, local Japanese Army spokesman, yesterday called on Maj. K. M. ... Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, to protest the publication in the weekly newspaper of an article of a derogatory nature to the Japanese military, it was learned, says Denki.

Lieut.-Col. Akiyama, it was understood, emphasized that such articles must not be tolerated.

With the American-owned weekly giving prominence to articles of an extreme anti-Japanese nature, the Shanghai Municipal Police naturally asked the United States Consul-General to take appropriate steps for stopping it is allowed by law.

It was understood, however, that the U.S. Consular authorities said the weekly was not registered as the United States Consulate-General, hence no confiscatory action by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

While action by the U.S. authorities here toward Mr. J. B. Powell, editor and publisher of the "China Weekly Review," may be expected, negotiations between the Japanese and American authorities could be arranged for articles appearing if occasion requires.

Statement by Mr. Powell

Mr. Powell yesterday told the "North-China Daily News" that he had learned from the Municipal Police that about 30 copies of his weekly had been seized by them. He denied the allegation that the journal was not registered with the United States Consulate-General here. The "China Weekly Review" had been registered annually for a period of 25 years except for a brief period. It is registered under the name of the Millard Publishing Co., he said.

The Japanese objection was chiefly to an article which appeared in the weekly's issue of a member of the staff. The allegations came from two copies of "Asahi Shimbun" and a story in the "New York Times." It charged originally by two Japanese officers, Col. ... and Lieut.-Col. ... who claimed that the article was libelous. They demanded an apology and retraction. Mr. Powell refused to comply with their demands, stating that the article was based on facts and that he would not apologize for publishing the truth. He further stated that the Japanese authorities had no right to interfere with the editorial policy of an American-owned publication. The matter was then referred to the United States Consulate-General for settlement.

《字林西报》
1941年7月1日

（批注：上海公共租界工部局警务处
档案室
D.8149 F.23
1 - 7-41）

美资周刊
遭工部局警务处
查扣

据《电报》获悉，上海公共租界工部局警务处没收了所有6月21日出版的《密勒氏评论报》后，日本陆军当地发言人秋山大佐（Lieut.-Col. Kimio Akiyama，音译）昨日拜访了上海公共租界工部局警务处处长K. M. ...少校（Maj. K. M. ...），就该周刊刊登一篇对日军具有贬损性质的文章提出抗议。

据悉，秋山大佐强调，此类文章绝不能容忍。

鉴于这家美资周刊显著刊登极具反日性质的文章，上海公共租界工部局警务处自然要求美国总领事馆采取适当措施予以制止，只要法律允许。

然而，据了解，美国领事当局表示，该周刊并未在美国总领事馆注册，因此上海公共租界工部局警务处无权采取没收行动。

虽然预计此地美国当局会对《密勒氏评论报》编辑兼出版人J. B.鲍威尔先生采取行动，但如果需要，日美当局可就刊登的文章安排谈判。

鲍威尔先生的声明

鲍威尔先生昨日告诉《字林西报》，他从工部局警务处得知，其周刊约有30本被警方查扣。他否认了该期刊未在此地美国总领事馆注册的说法。他说，《密勒氏评论报》除短暂时期外，已连续25年每年进行注册。该刊是以密勒出版公司（Millard Publishing Co.）的名义注册的。

日方的异议主要针对该周刊某期上刊登的一篇由 staff member（职员/撰稿人）撰写的文章。指控依据来自两份《朝日新闻》和《纽约时报》的一则报道。最初由两名日本军官，...上校和...中校提出指控，他们声称该文章构成诽谤。他们要求道歉并撤回文章。鲍威尔先生拒绝满足他们的要求，称该文章基于事实，他不会为公布真相而道歉。他进一步表示，日本当局无权干涉美资出版物的编辑方针。此事随后被提交给美国总领事馆解决。

CHINA PRESS
JUL 1 1941

Weekly Review
Article Draws
Nippon Protest

Lieut. Col. Kunio Akimoto, chief Japanese Army spokesman, yesterday called on Major E. M. Powell, Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, to protest against the publication of an article in the China Weekly Review dated June 21, 1941.

The complaint, it was reported, was based on an article entitled "Mackenzie is largest ship Japan along the path of empire—foreign adventures." Lieut.-Col. Akimoto's protest, that all copies of the Weekly Review were seized by the Settlement police from the news-stands here. The seizure was halted by a protest to the Shanghai Municipal Council by Mr. J. B. Powell, editor of the publication.

Contacted by The China Press last night, Mr. Powell said that the article in question was based on information taken from two articles in the Time Magazine, an article in Life Magazine, and also a series of articles published in the New York Herald Tribune. Mr. Powell stated that he could not see any justification of the Japanese protest as the articles previously had appeared in widely circulated magazines and newspapers in the United States, to which the Japanese apparently had not made any complaint. The re-printing of the articles here, Mr. Powell said, according to Mr. Powell were not intended and absolutely could not be regarded as insulting to the Japanese Armed Forces or Japanese Military Publicity which was alleged in the Japanese complaint.

《大美晚报》
1941年7月1日

《评论报》文章
引发日本抗议

日本陆军首席发言人秋元邦夫中佐（Lieut. Col. Kunio Akimoto，音译）昨日拜访上海公共租界工部局警务处处长E. M.鲍威尔（E. M. Powell，原文如此，应为Bourne之误）少校，抗议1941年6月21日出版的《密勒氏评论报》中刊登的一篇文章。

据报道，投诉基于一篇题为“麦肯齐号是日本沿着帝国之路——外国冒险中最大的船只”的文章。秋元中佐提出抗议后，租界警察从这里的报摊上收缴了所有《评论报》副本。此次收缴因该出版物编辑J. B.鲍威尔先生向上海公共租界工部局提出抗议而停止。

《大美晚报》昨晚联系鲍威尔先生时，他表示有关文章是基于《时代》杂志的两篇文章、《生活》杂志的一篇文章以及《纽约先驱论坛报》发表的一系列文章中的信息。鲍威尔先生表示，他看不出日本抗议有任何正当理由，因为这些文章此前已出现在美国广泛发行的杂志和报纸上，而日本方面显然并未对此提出任何投诉。鲍威尔先生说，在此重印这些文章并非有意，且绝对不能被视为对日本武装部队或日本军事宣传的侮辱，而这正是日本投诉中所指控的内容。

URGENT.

Council Chamber.

ADMINISTRATION BUILDING

Shanghai, 28th June, 19 41.

The Commissioner of Police:

China Weekly Review.

I wrote to you this morning expressing my approval
of your action in suppressing the sale of to-day's issue of
the China Weekly Review. I further stated that I proposed
to arrange for a discussion in Council as to the desirability
of suspending the newspaper in question.

Immediately after I had sent this letter to you
I received a telephone message from the American Consul-General
stating that the newspaper in question is registered at the
American Consulate-General, and requesting me to cancel the
order for suppression of the sale of the issue in question.

In order to make my own position clear I must record
that I expressly asked the American Consul-General last week
whether the paper was registered at the American Consulate,
and he informed me that it was not. The American Consul-
General now tells me that he was misinformed at the time when
he replied to my question.

In view of the American Consul-General's request,
and the question of extraterritorial jurisdiction involved,
will you please at once cancel the order for suppression of
the sale of the newspaper in question.

Secretary & Commissioner General.

DB.

URGENT.
Council Chamber.
ADMINISTRATION BUILDING
Shanghai, 28th June, 19 41.

The Commissioner of Police:

China Weekly Review.

I refer to page 112 of the issue of the China
Weekly Review of to-day's date, to which I drew your attention
this morning. I note that you have ordered the immediate
seizure of all copies. I entirely agree.

On June 24 I wrote to the Editor drawing his
attention to the undesirable nature of an article appearing
in the previous issue which dealt with Colonel Hashimoto.
This article contained derogatory references to the Imperial
Family of Japan. The caption under the photograph on
page 112 of to-day's issue invites the attention of readers
to the previous article against which the Council protested.
In my opinion the publication of this caption warrants the
Council in suspending forthwith the publication of the
China Weekly Review.

Only one question causes me difficulty. I have
just received a letter from Mr. J.B. Powell, a copy of which
I enclose. You will note that this letter is dated
June 27, 1941, and that in it Mr. Powell states that he
has only just received my letter of June 24. In my opinion
this is no excuse. I find that my letter was in fact
delivered on the morning of June 26. There should be some
machinery to secure that letters addressed to the Editors
of newspapers are opened and dealt with without delay.
Moreover, even if Mr. Powell only received my letter
yesterday, it should still have been practicable for him
to take steps to suppress to-day's issue or at least tender
immediate apologies to the Council.

《密勒氏评论报》。

我提及今日出版的《密勒氏评论报》第112页，今晨我曾提请阁下注意该页内容。我注意到阁下已下令立即查扣所有副本。我完全同意。

6月24日，我致函编辑，提请其注意上一期刊登的一篇关于桥本欣五郎大佐（Colonel Hashimoto）的文章性质不良。该文章包含对日本皇室的贬损性提及。今日一期第112页照片下的说明文字，意在引导读者关注工部局曾提出抗议的前述文章。在我看来，刊登此说明文字足以让工部局有理由立即暂停《密勒氏评论报》的出版。

只有一个问题令我感到为难。我刚刚收到鲍威尔先生（Mr. J.B. Powell）的来信，随函附上副本。请注意，此信日期为1941年6月27日，鲍威尔先生在信中称他刚刚收到我6月24日的去信。在我看来，这并非借口。经查，我的信件实际上已于6月26日上午送达。应当建立某种机制，以确保寄给报纸编辑的信件能被及时开启和处理。此外，即使鲍威尔先生昨天才收到我的信件，他本应仍有可能采取措施禁止今日一期的发行，或至少向工部局立即致歉。

THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW

160 Avenue Edward VII,
Shanghai, June 27, 1941.

Mr. G.G. Phillips,
Secretary & Commissioner General,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Administration Building,
209 Kiangse Road,
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Phillips,

I am just in receipt of your letter of
June 24th referring to an article which we published in our
issue of June 21st referring to two well known Japanese, Col.
Kingoro Hashimoto of the Japanese Army, and Toshio Shiratori
who is an advisor to the Tokyo Foreign Office.

This article was a condensation of three
articles which previously appeared in well known journals in
the United States, TIME, ASIA and the NEW YORK TIMES. One of
the articles in TIME was a summary of a series which previously
had been syndicated all over the United States by Wilfrid
Fleisher former Editor of the Japan Advertiser, and corres-
pondent for the New York Herald-Tribune in Tokyo for many
years.

Since the article we published was a conden-
sation of articles previously published in reputable journals
in the United States, which had been distributed here as well
as in Japan several weeks and months ago, I had no idea that
the reprinting of the articles here would cause any complica-
tions, particularly in view of the fact that the activities of
the two Japanese officers referred to are quite well known
and a matter of general knowledge both in Japan and the United
States. In the case of one of the men, other members of the
organization with which he is connected have been prosecuted
in the courts of Japan.

In reading over the article as it appeared in
our paper, I see that we perhaps did not make it sufficiently
clear that it was a re-print and not an original article. The
inscription under the picture of Col. Hashimoto stated it was
from Time Magazine, but we also should have indicated the
original source in the text of the article.

I assume that the Japanese complaint was based
on a reference to the Emperor of Japan which appeared in the
second column of the article. This text was reproduced from
the article in ASIA Magazine. In reproducing it, we obviously
had no intention of publishing anything that might be considered
disrespectful of H.E. the Emperor of Japan.

I admit there might be a difference of opinion
on the matter of publishing such articles in Shanghai, but it
appears to the writer that the best way to combat such influences
as displayed by these Japanese officials, is to make the matter
page_data.zh:
《密勒氏评论报》

上海爱多亚路160号，
1941年6月27日。

致 G.G. 菲利普斯先生，
秘书兼总办，
上海公共租界工部局，
行政大厦，
江西路209号，
上海。

亲爱的菲利普斯先生：

我刚收到您6月24日的来信，信中提及我们在6月21日一期中刊登的一篇关于两位知名日本人——日本陆军桥本欣五郎大佐和东京外务省顾问白鸟敏夫（Toshio Shiratori）——的文章。

这篇文章是对此前刊登在美国知名期刊《时代》（TIME）、《亚洲》（ASIA）和《纽约时报》（NEW YORK TIMES）上的三篇文章的摘要。其中《时代》杂志的一篇文章是对一系列文章的总结，这些文章此前由前《日本广知报》（Japan Advertiser）编辑、多年担任《纽约先驱论坛报》驻东京记者的威尔弗里德·弗莱舍尔（Wilfrid Fleisher）在美国各地联合刊发。

由于我们发表的文章是此前在美国信誉良好的期刊上发表的文章的摘要，而这些文章在数周乃至数月前已在包括日本在内的各地分发，我未曾想到在此重印这些文章会引起任何纠纷，特别是鉴于文中提到的两名日本军官的活动在日本和美国均为众所周知的事实。就其中一人而言，与其所属组织有关的其他成员已在日本法院被起诉。

在重读刊登在我报上的这篇文章时，我发现我们或许没有足够清楚地表明这是一篇重印文章而非原创文章。桥本大佐照片下的说明文字指出其源自《时代》杂志，但我们也应在文章正文中注明原始出处。

我推测日方的投诉是基于文章第二栏中出现的一处对日本天皇的提及。这段文字转载自《亚洲》杂志的文章。在转载时，我们显然无意刊登任何可能被视为对日本天皇陛下不敬的内容。

我承认，对于在上海刊登此类文章可能存在不同意见，但在笔者看来，对抗这些日本官员所表现出的此类影响的最佳方式是使此事

page_data.en:
2.

public. I am sure that if certain Japanese officers and
politicians were advocating war against Great Britain you
would also agree that their activities should be exposed in
no uncertain manner, otherwise more serious developments
might occur.

I wish to thank you for bringing the matter to
my attention. I have cautioned our staff against re-printing
articles referring to Japan which have appeared in newspapers
in the United States or Great Britain, without clearly indica-
ting the source of the information.

With best wishes, I am,

Very truly yours,

J.B. Powell.
page_data.zh:
2.

公开化。我相信，如果某些日本军官和政治家正在鼓吹对英国开战，您也会同意应当毫不含糊地揭露他们的活动，否则可能会发生更严重的事态。

感谢您提请我注意此事。我已告诫我方员工，在未清楚标明信息来源的情况下，不得重印出现在美国或英国报纸上涉及日本的 Article。

顺致最良好的祝愿，

您真诚的，

J.B. 鲍威尔。

D.C.(C.& S.B.)
June 28, 1941.
Sir,
China Weekly Review - Objectionable matter
in issue of June 21, 1941.

In connection with the article on Col. Kingoro
Hashimoto appearing in the June 21 issue of the China
Weekly Review, C.D.I. Tabrum, accompanied by D.S.I. Young,
visited Mr. Powell in his office at 5 p.m. June 27, 1941,
and pointed out to him the objections to his article from
a police point of view, and impressed on him the fact
that apart from the risk of suspension he incurred in
publishing such matter it was not beyond the possibility
that more drastic action might be taken by others.

At the commencement of the interview Mr. Powell
thumped his desk and shouted that the substance of the
article had appeared in the American magazines "Time" and
"Asia", concluding by asking "What are you going to do
about it ?" Thereafter he adopted a very reasonable
attitude and stated the matter had appeared on page 37
of the April 21, 1941, issue of "Time", on page 27 of the
December 2, 1940, issue of "Time" and on page 522 of the
October issue of "Asia", and offered these magazines for
examination.

He was then asked for a copy of the issue of the
China Weekly Review for June 28, and this was perused by
detectives who voiced objections to those expressions
marked in red on pages 101, 106, 107 and 112. Mr. Powell
was asked if he could obliterate the text objected to,
but replied that the paper was already printed and as
copies had already been sent out to distributors, it was
too late.

He then stated he had already received a letter from
the Secretary & Commissioner General and had been
page_data.zh:
D.C.(C.& S.B.)
1941年6月28日。
先生，
《密勒氏评论报》 - 1941年6月21日一期中的不良内容。

关于《密勒氏评论报》6月21日一期中刊登的关于桥本欣五郎大佐的文章，特高课督察塔布鲁姆在侦探督察杨（Young）的陪同下，于1941年6月27日下午5时在其办公室拜访了鲍威尔先生，并向他指出从警方角度来看其文章存在的问题，并向他强调，除了因刊登此类内容而面临的停刊风险外，其他人还可能采取更严厉的行动。

会谈开始时，鲍威尔先生捶打桌子并大喊，称文章的实质内容已出现在美国杂志《时代》和《亚洲》上，最后问道：“你们打算对此做什么？”此后，他采取了非常理性的态度，并称该内容出现在1941年4月21日一期《时代》杂志的第37页、1940年12月2日一期《时代》杂志的第27页以及10月份一期《亚洲》杂志的第522页，并提供这些杂志供查阅。

Sir,
China weekly Review - Objectionable matter
in issue of June 21, 1941.

In connection with the article on Col. Kingoro
Hashimoto appearing in the June 21 issue of the China
weekly Review, C.D.I. Tabrum, accompanied by D.S.I. Young,
visited Mr. Powell in his office at 5 p.m. June 27, 1941,
and pointed out to him the objections to his article from
a police point of view, and impressed on him the fact
that apart from the risk of suspension he incurred in
publishing such matter it was not beyond the possibility
that more drastic action might be taken by others.

At the commencement of the interview Mr. Powell
thumped his desk and shouted that the substance of the
article had appeared in the American magazines "Time" and
"Asia", concluding by asking "What are you going to do
about it ?" Thereafter he adopted a very reasonable
attitude and stated the matter had appeared on page 37
of the April 21, 1941, issue of "Time", on page 27 of the
December 2, 1940, issue of "Time" and on page 522 of the
October issue of "Asia", and offered these magazines for
examination.

He was then asked for a copy of the issue of the
China Weekly Review for June 28, and this was perused by
detectives who voiced objections to those expressions
marked in red on pages 101, 106, 107 and 112. Mr. Powell
was asked if he could obliterate the text objected to,
but replied that the paper was already printed and as
copies had already been sent out to distributors, it was
too late.

He then stated he had already received a letter
from the Secretary & Commissioner General and had been

Shanghai, June 27, 1941.
C.P
This mail with my letter of
this morning. I wish it to come to
hand it sufficient to act on the
request made in the
G.G. Phillips, Esq.,
Secretary & Commissioner General,
Shanghai.
My dear Mr. Phillips,
I received your letter of June 24th, just after I sent
you another letter concerning the same matter.
In view of the seriousness of the offence, this case
cannot be dealt with in the same way as other anti-Japanese
articles. We cannot remain indifferent to any derogatory
reference to our Imperial Family, and this particular case is
the worst in these days. The question whether the article was
an original, a reprint, or a digest is irrelevant in this case.
What we are concerned with are the offending character of this
article and that such an article was published and is being
allowed to circulate in Shanghai where utmost discretion and
restraint are needed to preserve tranquility, and, last but not
least, that the Settlement authorities do not seem to fully
understand the endeavours we have been exercising to induce the
Japanese newspapers to comply with their requests, either by
friendly talks, or, if absolutely necessary, by recourse to
legal authority.
While appreciating the trouble you have taken to warn
the editor against a repetition, I would like to request you
further to advise him to redeem on his own accord all the copies
still on sale, or if he does not accede to your advice, to take
some other possible means, such as the suppression of the sale
of this particular issue.
I have learned with great pleasure that you share my
views regarding the undesirable nature of such an article.
As the article in question is of an exceptionally offending
nature and might have harmful effects upon the Japanese com-
munity, here and elsewhere once it becomes known to them I

亲爱的菲利普斯先生：
我在寄给您另一封关于同一事项的信件后，收到了您6月24日的来信。
鉴于违规行为的严重性，此案不能以处理其他反日文章的方式处理。对于任何贬损我国皇室的内容，我们不能置之不理，而本案是近期最恶劣的一起。文章是原创、转载还是摘要，在此案中无关紧要。我们要关注的是该文章的冒犯性质，以及此类文章得以出版并在上海流通，而在上海需要极度的谨慎和克制以维持安宁；最后但同样重要的是，租界当局似乎并未充分理解我们一直在努力通过友好交谈，或在绝对必要时诉诸法律权威，促使日本报纸遵守其要求所付出的努力。
虽然感谢您费心警告编辑不得重犯，但我还想请您进一步建议他主动收回所有仍在销售的副本，或者如果他不接受您的建议，则采取其他可能的措施，例如禁止销售这一特定期号。
得知您也认为此类文章性质不良，我不胜欣慰。由于涉案文章具有格外严重的冒犯性质，一旦为日本侨民所知，可能会对本地及其他地方的日本社群产生有害影响，我

160, Avenue Edouard VII,
Shanghai.

Sir,

The Council's attention has been drawn to an article published at page 85 of the issue of the China Weekly Review dated June 21, 1941.

It would seem clear that the article in question is calculated to arouse resentment among the Japanese community and therefore is detrimental to the interests of the International Settlement.

I feel sure that you will agree with me that in the peculiar conditions which exist in Shanghai, any article which tends to inflame the feelings of any particular national community is contrary to the general interest.

While I must draw your attention to the Council's established policy of suspending the sale in the Settlement of any newspaper which publishes matter which, in the Council's opinion, tends to disturb peace and good order, I would prefer that you should rather regard this letter as an appeal to you to avoid the publication of any matter calculated to arouse the resentment of any body of nationals in the Settlement.

（印：RECEIVED 25 JUN 1941 CHINESE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL）
（批：The article in question has been noted. A.）

I am, Sir,
Your obedient Servant,

G. Godfrey Phillips

JAPANESE EMBASSY IN CHINA.
Shanghai, June 23rd, 1941.

My dear Mr. Phillips,

I beg to draw your attention to an article published on
page 83 of the June 21st issue of the China Weekly Review. You
will notice that the article contains utterly false and most
derogatory references to our Imperial Family.

You will be informed that some time ago our Consul-
General requested the Chairman of the Municipal Council to take
steps against the "Parade" which also contained slanderous
remarks regarding our Imperial Family. I need not dwell upon
how inimical these articles are to friendly relations between
various communities here, but I would like to remind you how
sensitive our people are toward any reference to our Imperial Family.

Apart from the legal question of the right of the
Municipal Council to control the publication in the International
Settlement, or of the extraterritorial character of the weekly
magazine in question, I am convinced that something can be done
regarding such a publication for the greater cause of tranquility
in this international community.

I should be very grateful if you would find it possible
to take a statesmanlike view of the situation, and adopt any
measure that may effectively withhold the above-mentioned issue
of the magazine from circulation and warn the editor against a
repetition.

I remain,

THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW
June 22, 1940

Closed Gambling Dens Rumored to
Reopen on Payment of $100,000 Each

THE long-discussed closure of gambling houses in the “bad-lands” district was finally put into effect on the night of Saturday, June 15—but when the excitement had died down it was discovered that those responsible for the closing act had overlooked two important places: the palatial China Club at 29 Tifeng Road and Farrens, 325 Great Western Road.

There were two explanations regarding the failure of the Japanese authorities to close the China Club—that it serves as headquarters for Wang Ching-wei politicians when they are in Shanghai; that the proprietors of the China Club paid somebody the sum of $100,000.

Failure of the Japanese to close Farrens, which also is located in territory controlled by the Japanese army was due, according to rumor, to the fact that the resort is patronized largely by foreigners and allegedly has some form of foreign protection. Of the two proprietors of Farrens, E. T. Riley, local slot-machine “king,” is either an American or a Briton, while his partner, Joe Farren is a Hungarian. It was reported that Mr. Farren and a foreign attorney visited a high Japanese official, who provided him with a special license to continue in operation despite the closing order which affected the other resorts. Messrs. Riley and Farren are the only foreigners who have “muscled-in” on the gambling business since the Japanese occupied this area.

Since one gambling and opium-smoking joint, known as “Honeymoon,” located at 42 Great Western Road, had already closed due to lack of patronage, the number affected by the latest shut down was nine, aside from a number of small places catering to coolies in Jessfield village.

Various rumors have been in circulation regarding the circumstances surrounding the Japanese action in closing the bad-lands resorts, the most significant being that the order to close originated in Tokyo and was conveyed to the Japanese military authorities here by special messenger, who arrived by plane from the Japanese Capital. The report that the Japanese authorities contemplated this action appeared in The Review on June 8 along with a list of the places to be closed and three “favored” places which were to be permitted to operate. Of the three (see Page 54, issue of June 8) only one, The China Club, has remained open. As stated in a previous reference to the China Club, it was regarded as successor to the Asia Club, which operated inside the International Settlement for more than a year without interference on the part of the police authorities—on the ground that it had Japanese protection. This however, was denied by the Japanese consular authorities, and the place closed after their attention had been called to the situation.

A special circumstance in connection with the closure action on the night of June 15, was the commandeering of all pistols in the possession of the gangsters who have provided “protection” to the various places. It was rumored that there were more than 2,000 of these armed gangsters, many of whom operated as robbers and hold-up men in their off-hours when they were not busy protecting gambling houses.

According to information provided by an assistant in one of the houses, the military police seized all of the pistols in the possession of the joints on the early morning of Sunday, June 16, following which the closure orders were issued. According to a report in The China Press derived from police circles, many of the resorts were visited by contingents of Japanese Gendarmes, who impressed upon the proprietors the fact that the orders were genuine and were not an attempt to collect back “taxes” as had occurred when previous closure orders had been issued. The impression prevails, however, that the closures are to be temporary and that all places may reopen shortly, as evidenced in the fact that the China Club and Farrens have been permitted to remain open. The proprietors of some of the closed resorts alleged that they had been informed—secretly—that they might be permitted to reopen, provided they handed over the sum of $100,000. As the officials refused to give any assurances of future protection, even though the $100,000 was paid over, the proprietors, following a conference, decided to remain closed for the present.

Correction

The China Weekly Review received a communication on Thursday of this week, too late for publication in full in this issue, stating that an article published in our issue of June 15, (Page 89) was incorrect. The article referred to the opening of a gambling house, which allegedly had Japanese protection, at No. 52 Yates Road. Mr. T. Torikawa, who signed the letter alleged that our article was incorrect and that the so-called “Finance Investigation Society” is a social club. The S. M. P. have maintained a cordon about the premises at 52 Yates Road for several days.

《密勒氏评论报》
1940年6月22日

传闻每家缴纳10万美元后，已关闭的赌场将重新开业

关于在“坏地段”（bad-lands）区域关闭赌馆的长期讨论，终于在6月15日星期六晚间付诸实施——但当喧嚣平息后，人们发现负责执行关闭行动的人遗漏了两个重要场所：位于提丰路29号的豪华“中国总会”（China Club），以及位于大西路325号的“法伦斯”（Farrens）。

关于日本当局未能关闭“中国总会”的原因有两种解释：一是该处在汪精卫派政客在上海期间充当其总部；二是“中国总会”的业主向某人支付了10万美元。

据传言，日本人未能关闭同样位于日军控制区域内的“法伦斯”，是因为该娱乐场所主要受外国人光顾，且据称拥有某种形式的外国保护。“法伦斯”的两名业主中，当地老虎机“大王” E. T. 莱利（E. T. Riley）不是美国人就是英国人，而其合伙人乔·法伦（Joe Farren）是匈牙利人。据报道，法伦先生与一名外籍律师拜访了一位日本高官，后者为其提供了特别许可证，使其尽管受到影响其他场所的关闭令限制，仍可继续营业。莱利先生和法伦先生是自日本人占领该地区以来，唯一“强行介入”赌博业务的外国人。

由于一家名为“蜜月”（Honeymoon）、位于大西路42号的赌博兼鸦片烟馆已因缺乏客源而关闭，因此受最新关闭行动影响的场所共有九家，此外还有杰司菲尔德村（Jessfield village）一些服务于苦力的小场所。

关于日本当局关闭“坏地段”娱乐场所的背景，各种谣言流传甚广，其中最为显著的说法是，关闭命令源自东京，并由一名从日本首都乘飞机抵达的特使传达给驻沪日本军事当局。《评论报》曾在6月8日刊登了日本当局考虑采取此行动的报道，并列出了拟关闭的场所名单以及三家被允许运营的“受优待”场所。在这三家中（参见6月8日一期第54页），只有“中国总会”一家仍然开放。正如前文提及“中国总会”时所述，它被视为“亚洲总会”（Asia Club）的继任者，后者在国际公共租界内运营了一年多而未受警方干涉——理由是它拥有日本人的保护。然而，这一说法遭到日本领事当局的否认，在该情况引起其注意后，该场所即被关闭。

6月15日晚关闭行动中的一个特殊情况是，没收了为各个场所提供“保护”的帮派分子所持有的所有手枪。据传这类武装帮派分子超过2000人，其中许多人在不忙于保护赌场的闲暇时间从事抢劫和持械拦路犯罪。

根据某家赌场一名助手提供的信息，宪兵队于6月16日星期日清晨没收了各赌场持有的所有手枪，随后发布了关闭令。据《字林西报》从警界获得的报道，大批日本宪兵走访了许多娱乐场所，向业主强调命令是真实的，并非像以前发布关闭令时那样试图收取回溯性“税款”。然而，普遍的印象是，这些关闭将是暂时的，所有场所可能很快重新开业，“中国总会”和“法伦斯”被允许继续营业的事实便证明了这一点。一些已关闭娱乐场所的业主声称，他们接到秘密通知——只要缴纳10万美元，即可获准重新开业。由于官员们拒绝提供任何未来保护的保证，即使支付了10万美元也无济于事，业主们在开会后决定暂时保持关闭状态。

更正

《密勒氏评论报》于本周四收到一封来信，因时间太晚无法在本期全文刊登，信中称本刊6月15日一期（第89页）发表的一篇文章有误。该文章提及在叶茨路52号开设了一家据称受日本人保护的赌场。签署该信的 T. 鸟川（T. Torikawa）先生声称，我方文章不实，所谓的“财务调查社”实为一个社交俱乐部。上海公共租界警务处已在叶茨路52号的 premises 周围设立警戒线数日。

Another Japanese Sponsored Gambling House Opened
in Settlement
-------------------------

The Editor,
The China Weekly Review.
Present.                                June 19, 1940

Sir,
    With considerable astonishment we learned, in your
issue of June 15, under the caption "ANOTHER JAPANESE
SPONSORED GAMBLING HOUSE OPENED IN SETTLEMENT" you
stated that the group of Chinese claiming the protection
of the Japanese and the new regime had opened a gambling
house at 82 Yates Road, the house bearing the sign
"Finance Investigation Society."
    You added that "Trucks were observed unloading
roulette wheels and other gambling paraphernalia in the
compound."
    As the news is entirely unfounded, incorrect and
published by you in spite of the fact that it had been
established as a social club, we now insist that you
immediately publish any authority or evidence in your
possession to corroborate your libellous statements,
which are deeply resented and indignantly repudiated.
    We demand a full retraction and apology in your next
issue, failing which we regret that we shall be compelled
to have recourse to a Court of Law. Members and officials

June 20, 1940.

Mr. Y. Torikawa,
c/o Finance Investigation Society,
(Sino-Japanese Commercial Association),
No. 82 Yates Road,
Shanghai, China.

Dear Mr. Torikawa:

We just received your letter of June 19th.,
referring to a report published in our paper last week re-
ferring to the opening of an alleged Japanese sponsored
gambling house at your address.

Since our paper is already made up, it will
be impossible for us to publish the complete text of your
letter this week. We shall however, publish a summary of it
and will try to use it in full next week.

The information upon which our article was
based was derived from an article bearing on the same subject
which previously had appeared in the Shanghai Evening Post &
Mercury.

We also had been informed from other sources
that the police had established a cordon about the house at
82 Yates Road, because of their alleged knowledge that a
gambling house was to be opened on the premises.

The report was also prevalent in other circles
that such an institution was to be opened there.

Perhaps you can inform me why the police re-
garded it as necessary to establish a cordon about your premises
in case nothing illegal was to be conducted on the premises? We
obviously have no desire to publish articles which are not
correct, hence we would appreciate it if you could supply us in
writing with further information on the subject.

Very truly yours,

J.B. Powell

亲爱的鸟川先生：

我们刚刚收到阁下6月19日的来信，提及上周本报发表的一篇关于在阁下地址开设一家据称由日本人支持的赌场的报道。

由于本报版面已排定，本周无法刊登阁下来信的全文。不过，我们将刊登摘要，并争取在下周全文刊登。

我方文章所依据的信息来源于此前刊登在《上海晚报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）上的一篇关于同一主题的文章。

我们也从其他渠道获悉，警方已在叶茨路82号的房屋周围设立警戒线，原因是他们据称得知该处将开设一家赌场。

在其他圈子中，也普遍流传着将在该处开设此类机构的说法。

也许阁下可以告知我，如果该处不进行任何非法活动，警方为何认为有必要在阁下 premises 周围设立警戒线？我们显然无意发表不正确的文章，因此，若阁下能书面提供有关此事的进一步信息，我们将不胜感激。

您真诚的，

J.B. 鲍威尔

Japanese call to see Editor of China
Weekly Review.

At 3.25p.m. 17/6/40 a telephone message was
received from F.P/S Richardson to the effect that
he had been informed by one of the staff of the China
Weekly Review that 4 Japanese had just called to see
the editor of said paper, but had left when told
he was out. They had departed in a westerly direction
along Av. Ed. VII in a m/car Lic. No. 10272.

C.D.S. 312 and the undersigned attended and
learned from Mr. J.B. Powell (American) that at about
2.50p.m. even date three Japanese and one Chinese
interpreter attended the office and asked to see
the editor. One of the Japanese held a rolled up
copy of the China Weekly Review in his hand. When
told the editor was not in the party held a few
moments discussion in Japanese and then left saying
that they would call again at 4p.m. A coolie employed
at above premises followed the party and saw them get
into a dark red closed car, Lic. No. 10272, in which were
3 more Japanese and depart in a westerly direction
along Av. Ed. VII.

Enquiries at Traffic Office elicited that the
m/car used is registered in the name of Robert Lee, 150,
Edinburgh Rd.

日本人要求会见《密勒氏评论报》编辑。

1940年6月17日下午3时25分，收到来自法捕房/警司 Richardson 的电话留言，称据《密勒氏评论报》一名工作人员告知，有4名日本人刚才前来拜访该报编辑，但得知其外出后离去。他们乘坐一辆车牌号为 10272 的机动车，沿爱多亚路向西驶离。

刑事侦缉处第312号警员及本人前往现场，并从 J.B. Powell 先生（美国人）处获悉，当日下午约2时50分，三名日本人和一名中国翻译来到办事处，要求见编辑。其中一名日本人手中拿着一卷《密勒氏评论报》。当被告知编辑不在时，这群人用日语简短讨论了几句，然后离开，并称将于下午4时再来。上述 premises 雇用的一名苦力跟随这群人，看见他们进入一辆深红色封闭式轿车，车牌号为 10272，车内另有3名日本人，随后沿爱多亚路向西驶离。

devoted to economics, finance, Sino-American and Inter-
national politics, its capital is G$50,000.00, whilst

Special Branch Station. File No. Date February 26, 1942

SUBJECT: SHANGHAI HERALD - Request from Guenther
LENHARDT, Editor-in-Chief, for return of
Registration Certificate No. F. 143.

With reference to the contents of the attached
letter dated February 24, 1942 I have to report
that Certificate No. F. 143 in respect of Shanghai
Herald was cancelled on October 23, 1941 as per the
contents of Police report dated October 23, 1941
(attached).

Since the receipt of the current letter I have
made three appointments for Mr. Philip KOHN, Mr.
Guenther LENHARDT and Mr. H. SELIG to meet me in
Headquarters to discuss the present status of
Shanghai Herald. Its owner is KOHN, its editor is
LENHARDT and its Assistant Editor is SELIG. Despite
the appointments made, however, I have been unable to
get these three individuals together at one time
but another attempt is being made for Saturday
morning, February 28, 1942 when efforts will be
made to secure full details of the new publication.

It is learned, however, that KOHN, the owner,
is financing the new venture with capital not
exceeding $3,000.00, a sum, that at the present time
seems insufficient to conduct a daily newspaper.
In this connection I would respectfully draw your
attention to the contents of the attached file and
the continual source of trouble which previous
editions of the paper in question gave the Police.
In view of the fact that Certificate No. F. 143,
in respect of Shanghai Herald, has been cancelled, it
would appear that the question of returning the

THE SHANGHAI HERALD
P.O.Box 1035

Shanghai, February 24th, 1942.

（印：SHANGHAI Municipal Police S. B. D. No. S. B. D. 8149 E/143 Date 17 - 3 - 42）

To the Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police,
Foochow Road,
Local.

Dear Sir,

cancelling my application of November 29th 1941 and referring to my letter of October 11th 1941, I herewith beg to inform you, that the Shanghai Herald will appear again as daily evening paper as from the 28th of this month. The paper will contain the reports of the news agencies Domei, Transocean, Tass, Havas and Reuter as well as the official announcements of the authorities in this city, local news and also non-political stories without any political tendency whatsoever.

With respect to above we have already informed Captain Inosuka of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party and we have been ordered to send him a copy of our issue each day as well as the translation in English of our first leading article. Certainly we shall also send to your office a copy each day.

Being unwell at present I beg you hand out the license of the Shanghai Herald (No.F.143), which you had received from Mr. Philip Kohn, moved by my application, on October 11th 1941, to my Assistant-Editor, Mr.H.Selig, who is bearer of this letter. Mr. H. Selig has the authority to confirm the receiving.

Thanking you in advance for your kindness,

I remain,

Yours respectfully
（签名：Gunther Lenhardt）
GUNTHER LENHARDT
Editor-In-Chief and owner
of the license of the
SHANGHAI HERALD

上海，1942年2月24日。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特务科 D. 编号 S. B. D. 8149 E/143 日期 42年3月17日）

致上海公共租界工部局警务处总监，
福州路，
本地。

尊敬的先生：

撤销我1941年11月29日的申请，并参照我1941年10月11日的信件，特此告知您，《上海导报》将从本月28日起重新作为每日晚报出版。该报将包含同盟社、跨洋社、塔斯社、哈瓦斯社和路透社的新闻机构报道，以及本市当局的官方公告、本地新闻，以及无任何政治倾向的非政治性故事。

关于上述事项，我们已通知日本海军特别陆战队 Inosuka 上尉，并奉命每天向他发送一份我们的刊物，以及我们首篇社论的英文译文。当然，我们也将每天向贵办公室发送一份副本。

由于目前身体不适，恳请您将《上海导报》的许可证（编号 F.143），即您于1941年10月11日应我的申请从 Philip Kohn 先生处收到的许可证，交给本信持有人、我的助理编辑 H. Selig 先生。H. Selig 先生有权确认收讫。

提前感谢您的好意，

此致

敬礼
（签名：Gunther Lenhardt）
GUNTHER LENHARDT

Special Branch Station. File No. Date October 23, 1941

SUBJECT: SHANGHAI HERALD - Registration Certificate
F. 143 returned.

"Shanghai Herald" has not appeared
since October 10, 1941 and the owner and publisher
of this journal informs me that owing to certain
financial difficulties future publication is, at
the moment, doubtful. The owner, Philipp KOHN,
states that the Chief Editor Guenther LENHARDT is
now no longer in his employ and has no connection
with any publication controlled by by KOHN.

In these circumstances - change of
editor and cessation of publication - I called for
the return of the registration certificate and attach
herewith Certificate F. 143 in respect of this
paper.

In view of the trouble the Police have
had at various times in the past with the management
of this publication, might I respectfully suggest
that this certificate be cancelled?

（批：yes.）
（批：&ll 23.10.41.）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY No. S. 8 8149 F.143 Date 18-8-41）

Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date August 15, 1941

SUBJECT: The Shanghai Herald - Communication from
I. C. Committee.

With reference to the attached
communication dated July 29, 1941 from Mr.
P. KOMOR, Hon. Secretary of the I. C. organization,
I have to confirm that the issue by the I.C.
Committee of Identification Cards for Jewish
refugees has been of the greatest assistance
to the Police since the inception of this registration
system. Its value to the Police was deemed to
be of such worth that in the summer of 1939 the
Municipal Police official seal was affixed to
public notices emanating from the I.C. Committee
advising refugees of the necessity of registering
without delay and securing Identification Cards.

The article to which Mr. KOMOR refers
appeared in The Shanghai Herald of July 27, 1941
and it is more or less an editorial comment on
a report that appeared in the July issue of the
Japanese sponsored magazine "Asiana," entitled
"New York Jewess Studies Refugees." Miss Laura
MARGOLIES, American Jewess, an employee of the
American Joint Relief Committee which disburses
funds for the upkeep of local Jewish refugees,
arrived in Shanghai some three months ago for
the ostensible purpose of studying the refugee
problem in Shanghai and endeavouring to assist
refugees in re-emigrating to the United States.
Miss Margolies who left Shanghai for
Manila on August 15, 1941 via Manila in the ss.

（批：D.C. (COMMS) I）

关于附上的由国际组织名誉秘书 P. 科莫尔 (P. KOMOR) 先生于1941年7月29日发出的公函，我必须确认，自该注册制度实施以来，国际委员会为犹太难民签发身份证对警方提供了极大的帮助。其对于警方的价值被认为极高，以至于在1939年夏季，工部局警务处的官方印章被盖在国际委员会发布的公告上，建议难民立即注册并获取身份证。

科莫尔先生提到的文章刊登在1941年7月27日的《上海先驱报》上，它或多或少是对日本资助的杂志《亚细亚》(Asiana) 7月刊上一篇题为“纽约犹太女性研究难民”的报道所作的社论评论。劳拉·马戈利斯 (Laura MARGOLIES) 小姐，美国犹太女性，美国联合救济委员会 (American Joint Relief Committee) 的雇员，该委员会负责拨付资金以维持当地犹太难民的生活，大约三个月前抵达上海，表面目的是研究上海的难民问题，并努力协助难民再移民至美国。马戈利斯小姐于1941年8月15日乘轮船经马尼拉离开上海前往马尼拉 [原文如此]。

SUBJECT: 2

President Harrison has, according to the observations
of this office, failed to grasp the fundamentals
affecting the refugee problem in Shanghai - probably
because she has been in Shanghai for such a short
time - with the result that her sympathies are
entirely with the refugees and against the Committee
for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees in
Shanghai headed by Messrs. SPEELMAN, HAYIM, KANN, etc.

That there is dissatisfaction in the
local refugee camps is an admitted fact. There
always will be a minimum of unrest where several
thousand people are herded together in conditions
that savour of hardship but the utterances of Miss
Margolies only tend to increase the difficulties of
the authorities in caring for refugees instead
diminishing them.

In the article in "Asiana" Miss Margolies
is alleged to have been interviewed by reporters and
given statements that, to say the least, do not
reflect credit on the efforts of the Committee above
mentioned. Miss Margolies has told me that she
was misquoted, misunderstood and that she never has
committed herself to any definite statement on the
activities or policies of the Committee. That
may or may not be correct, but she is not believed
in circles that have access to real information
vis-a-vis refugee affairs.

And thus the editorial comment that
appears in The Shanghai Herald goes further with
the question without first taking the preliminary

主题：2

据本处观察，哈里森总统 [原文如此，应指前文之马戈利斯小姐，或OCR/原文错误] 未能掌握影响上海难民问题的基本要素——可能是因为她在上海的时间太短——结果导致她的同情心完全偏向难民，而反对由斯皮尔曼 (SPEELMAN)、哈伊姆 (HAYIM)、坎恩 (KANN) 等先生领导的上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会。

当地难民营中存在不满情绪是一个公认的事实。在数千人聚集在充满艰辛条件的地方时，总会存在最低限度的动荡，但马戈利斯小姐的言论只会增加当局照顾难民的困难，而不是减少这些困难。

在《亚细亚》杂志的文章中，据说马戈利斯小姐接受了记者采访，并发表了一些至少可以说不能为上述委员会的努力增光的声明。马戈利斯小姐告诉我，她被错误引用和误解，她从未就委员会的活动或政策做出任何明确的声明。这可能正确也可能不正确，但在那些能够获取有关难民事务真实信息的圈子里，人们并不相信她的说法。

因此，《上海先驱报》上出现的这篇社论评论在没有首先采取初步

整篇报纸文章的语气相当温和，但它无助于找到解决上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会面临的许多问题的方法，并倾向于使这本期刊的少数读者在观点上反委员会。

THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR THE
ORGANIZATION OF EUROPEAN IMMIGRANTS
IN CHINA

SHANGHAI. 29th July, 1941.

The Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

I beg to enclose a copy of "THE SHANGHAI
HERALD" of Sunday, 27th July, 1941, and draw your kind
attention to the article headed
"Das Shanghaier Emigrations-problem"
on the third page and especially to the last paragraph
but one where the author of the article says: "Wir brau-
chen keine Vermittlung zum deutschen Generalkonsulat,
wir brauchen keine "Kennkarten" und keine Bevormundung.
(We do not need any intermediary for the German Consulate
General, we do not need any "Cards of Identification" and
no guardians, either.)"

I would observe that these Cards of Identi-
fication are part of our registration system, whereby the
photo of the respective emigrant is attached to his card
in our index. This system was discussed and approved at
various meetings of the "I.C." Relief Fund, the Public
Health Department and the Police Department of the SMC.
I refer, in particular, to the minutes of the third and
fourth meeting of representatives of the above named bodies,
held on May 25th and June 22nd, 1939, respectively. In fact,
at that time a notice was issued drawing the attention of
the emigrants to the necessity of registering and obtaining
the Cards of Identification issued by this Organization. To
this notification, the seal of the Shanghai Municipal Police
was affixed. As a matter of fact, I consider it, especially
at present, of the utmost importance that the present form
of registration and issuance of Cards of Identification
should be continued and any opinion expressed to the con-
trary is, in my opinion, contrary to the public interest
and to the interest of the emigrants in particular.

Yours faithfully
Hon. Secretary.

我要指出，这些身份证是我们注册系统的一部分，即 respective emigrant [各别移民] 的照片附在我们索引中的卡片上。该系统已在工部局卫生处、警务处和“国际委员会”救济基金的多次会议上讨论并获得批准。我特别指的是上述机构代表分别于1939年5月25日和6月22日举行的第三次和第四次会议的会议纪要。事实上，当时发布了一则通知，提请移民注意注册并获取本组织签发的身份证的必要性。在该通知上，加盖了上海公共租界工部局警务处的印章。事实上，我认为，特别是在目前，继续目前的注册形式和签发身份证至关重要，任何表达相反意见的行为，在我看来，都违背公共利益，特别是违背移民的利益。

REPORT
Special Branch Station. File No. Date June 16, 1941
SUBJECT: "8-Uhr Abendblatt" and "The Shanghai Herald."
Letter dated June 5, 1941 from Mr. P. KOMOR.

The attached communication from Mr. Paul
KOMOR, in effect, refers to the contents of the
article appearing in "8-Uhr Abendblatt" marked in
blue pencil. This article, headed "A private
affair," gives a detailed report of the many
differences, mainly financial, that have existed
for a considerable time between the editor of
"8-Uhr Abendblatt" and the management of the
new publication "The Shanghai Herald." A
brief translation of this article is attached
hereto.

While it is not the policy of this office to
interfere with affairs involving financial matters
among the refugees, it does seem that the Police
were a little too hasty in issuing the registration
certificate for "The Shanghai Herald," the members
of whose management and editorial staff do not
inspire confidence in any shape or form. A
number of issues of the new paper have been perused
and the conclusion is reached that it does not
serve the aim for which it ostensibly commenced
business, i.e., to serve Jewish refugee interests.
It cannot possibly hope to compete with the better
known "Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" since it
is far too small an edition to include anything
but the briefest resume of news...

P. 科莫尔先生1941年6月5日的来信。

附上的保罗·科莫尔 (Paul KOMOR) 先生的公函，实际上是指用蓝铅笔标记的《八点晚报》上刊登的文章内容。这篇题为“私事”的文章详细报道了《八点晚报》编辑与新出版物《上海先驱报》管理层之间长期存在的许多分歧，主要是财务方面的分歧。该文章的简要译文附后。

虽然本处的政策是不干涉涉及难民之间财务事务的事情，但警方在签发《上海先驱报》注册证书时似乎有些过于仓促，其管理层和编辑部的成员在任何方面都无法令人产生信心。查阅了新报纸的几期后，得出的结论是，它并没有服务于其表面上开始运营的目的，即为犹太难民利益服务。它根本不可能希望与更知名的《上海晚邮报与水星报》(Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury) 竞争，因为它的版面太小，除了最简短的新闻摘要外，容纳不了任何其他内容...

TRANSLATION FROM GERMAN

RESUME OF "A PRIVATE AFFAIR."

Mr. Philip KOHN belongs to Class C of the immigrants, i.e.
he arrived here with US$800 and consequently did not have to
struggle as hard as we pioneers who went from boat to camp,
and then without support from anybody built an existence in
an alien city. To the surprise all Jewish newspapermen
KOHN suddenly began to publish Juedische Nachrichtenblatt,
a paper which due to financial losses had ceased publication.
This was done although the committees had promised us to
keep the paper down in return for which we allowed the various
committees and the Gemeinde free printing space for its
weekly notifications. In view of the fact that every advert
we lost meant a further blow to our already sorry financial
state, we were forced into an alliance with the illustrious
Mr. KOHN, which resulted in his and Guenther LENHARDT's
attempt to force me out of the business. Internal friction,
mismanagement, etc., resulted in my having to mortgage the
paper to KOHN who thus gained a controlling interest in the
enterprise.

Several weeks ago Kohn declared he was in financial
straits and on May 29 I was informed that 8 Uhr Abendblatt
would cease publication on May 31. According to the
agreement formed between Kohn and myself, it was specified
that should losses for a three-month period amount to more
than one-quarter of the running costs of the paper, publication
would cease. However a profit and loss account compiled
by me on April 4 clearly showed that the paper was making a
monthly profit of $750. Naturally I objected to Kohn's
decision. Nevertheless the unbelievable happened and 8 Uhr
Abendblatt stopped, the reason given being that the paper
did not comply with the standard needed for a modern political
newspaper. This statement was made notwithstanding the fact
that KOHN was partly responsible for the direction of the
page_data.zh:
德语译文

《一件私事》摘要。

菲利普·科恩（Philip KOHN）先生属于C类移民，即
他携带800美元抵达此地，因此不必像我们这些从船
上到营地、在无人支持的情况下在这座陌生城市建立
生计的先驱者那样艰难奋斗。令所有犹太报人惊讶的
是，科恩突然开始出版《犹太新闻报》（Juedische
Nachrichtenblatt），这是一份因财务亏损而停刊的
报纸。尽管各委员会曾承诺我们会压制该报，作为交
换，我们允许各委员会和犹太社区（Gemeinde）免费
刊登其每周通知，但科恩仍这样做。鉴于我们失去的
每一则广告都对我们原本就糟糕的财务状况造成进一
步打击，我们被迫与这位显赫的科恩先生结盟，结果
导致他和京特·伦哈特（Guenther LENHARDT）试图将
我排挤出业务领域。内部摩擦、管理不善等导致我不
得不将该报抵押给科恩，从而使他获得了企业的控股
权。

几周前，科恩声称他陷入财务困境，并于5月29日通
知我，《八点钟晚报》（8 Uhr Abendblatt）将于5月
31日停刊。根据科恩与我之间达成的协议，规定如果
三个月的损失超过报纸运营费用的四分之一，则停止
出版。然而，我在4月4日编制的损益表清楚地显示，
该报每月盈利750美元。我自然反对科恩的决定。然
而，不可思议的事情发生了，《八点钟晚报》停刊了，
给出的理由是该报不符合现代政治报纸所需的标准。
尽管科恩部分负责该报的

page_data.en:
2

paper.
In the meantime preparations were made to publish
a new and more expensive paper. These preparations were
made secretly. This was intended to be the last stab in
the back. The advertisers of 8 Uhr Abendblatt were
even won over.
The fact that I have for well over two years employed
and in early 1939 given private financial assistance to Mr.
Guenther LENHARDT, who used to display proudly a Nazi
Party badge in the Third Reich and never attached much value
to his real name of LEVY, did not stop him from double-crossing
me.
This unfair attempt to liquidate me will soon be heard
in the course of arbitration and I think it is only fair that
subscribers who have been fair to me for the past 27 months
should learn the details of this infamous plot.
page_data.zh:
2

导向，但仍作出了上述声明。
与此同时，秘密筹备出版一份新的、更昂贵的报纸。
这意在给予最后一击（背后捅刀）。《八点钟晚报》
的广告客户甚至也被争取过去。
事实上，我在两年多的时间里雇佣了京特·伦哈特
（Guenther LENHARDT）先生，并在1939年初给予他私
人财政援助，他曾自豪地在第三帝国佩戴纳粹党徽章，
并且从不重视他的真实姓名莱维（LEVY），但这并未
阻止他背叛我。
这种清算我的不公企图很快将在仲裁过程中被听闻，
我认为，让过去27个月里一直公平对待我的订户了解
这一臭名昭著阴谋的细节是公平的。

Forwarded herewith for re-registration

"The Call of the Ukraine" in the Ukranian language

Mr. John V. Sweet is a Ukranian, born in
the Harkov district of the Ukraine in 1897. He went

left for Harbin in 1922, and continued as a journalist

edited a Ukranian weekly called the "Manchurian Herald."

John V. Sweet 先生是乌克兰人，1897年出生于乌克兰哈尔科夫地区。他于1918年前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），并在那里担任记者直至1922年。1920年，他还出版了一份名为《日出》（The Sunrise）的半月刊杂志。他于1922年前往哈尔滨，继续担任记者和邮票商直至1932年。从1932年到1937年，他编辑了一份名为《满洲先驱报》（Manchurian Herald）的乌克兰文周刊。他于1941年7月22日抵达上海，在西摩路101号开设了一家邮票店。

IVAN V SWEET
John V. Sweet, Orthodox, borne on 27th April
1897 in Charkow Government, Kupiansky district.
Attended the school for priests in 1913, from
1913-1915 attended Charkow Seminary. In 1915
attended lectures of the Physical-Mathematic
Faculty of Charkow University.
In 1918 left for Far. East via Siberia.
In 1918-1922 resided in Vladivostock working
as journalist and publishing 2 fortnightly
magazines (1920-"The Sunrise").
From 1922 to 1941 resided in Harbin working
as journalist and stamp-dealer. From 19
edited Ukrainian Weekly "The Manchurian
Herald".
On 22nd July 1941 arrived to Shanghai
and opened own stamp-shop in the Seya
Road 101. Residence: 118, Route des Soeurs

SUBJECT: The Call of The Ukraine - Application for Registration

Attached is an application for registration received from Mr. S. Vasiliev (Ukrainian), editor of "The Call of The Ukraine," proposed semi-monthly magazine in English with editorial offices at Room 19, No. 305 Kungping Road.

The following is the history of Mr. S. Vasiliev and Dr. M. Milko (Ukrainian), proprietor and publisher, who resides at 515 Route Vallon, French Concession :-

（批：First visit to-day check and prepare certificate if nothing objectionable.）
（印：JUL 15 1941 SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：S. S. wish.）

Mr. Vasiliev :- "I was born on November 2nd, 1905 at Shepetivka Volhynia (Ukraine) and attended a secondary school (5 classes) there. In 1924 I fled to Poland and obtained a position as warehouse manager in Borislov. 1937 I left Borislov for Harbin. In September 1939, I came to Shanghai from Harbin. Since December 1939, I have been employed as a watchman for the Messageries Maritimes Building."

Dr. Milko :- "I was born in Harbin on the 12th October, 1903, graduated at the Secondary Commercial School until 1921. In July 1921, I went to Europe to improve my education and studied in the following cities: Prague, Halli, Berlin and Giessen. In 1929, I acquired a state examination. 1931 obtained a doctor's degree (Rer. Pol.) 1932 I returned to Harbin and in 1937 I came to Shanghai. Since September, 1939, I have been employed by the General Auto Service as a manager. I am married and have one daughter."

附件为收到《乌克兰的呼唤》编辑 S. Vasiliev 先生（乌克兰人）提交的注册申请，该刊拟为英文半月刊，编辑部设于公平路 305 号 19 室。

以下为 S. Vasiliev 先生及 M. Milko 博士（乌克兰人，业主兼出版人，居住于法租界华伦路 515 号）的经历：

（批注：今日首次走访，若无不妥则核查并准备证书。）
（印章：1941 年 7 月 15 日 特别处）

Vasiliev 先生：“我于 1905 年 11 月 2 日出生于沃里尼亚舍佩托夫卡（乌克兰），并在那里就读中学（5 个年级）。1924 年我逃往波兰，在鲍里斯拉夫获得仓库经理职位。1937 年我离开鲍里斯拉夫前往哈尔滨。1939 年 9 月，我从哈尔滨来到上海。自 1939 年 12 月以来，我一直受雇于东方汇理银行大楼担任看守。”

Milko 博士：“我于 1903 年 10 月 12 日出生于哈尔滨，1921 年毕业于商业中学。1921 年 7 月，我前往欧洲深造，曾在以下城市学习：布拉格、哈雷、柏林和吉森。1929 年，我通过了国家考试。1931 年获得博士学位（政治学博士 Rer. Pol.）1932 年我返回哈尔滨，1937 年来到上海。自 1939 年 9 月以来，我一直受雇于通用汽车服务公司担任经理。我已婚，育有一女。”

page_data.en:
I was born on 2. 11 1905 in Shepetivka
Volhynia (Ukraine).
graduate of Gimnasium (5 classes)
in Shepetivka.
1924 I fled to Polen. Was storage
warehouse manager in Borislav.
1937 I left Borislav and through
Gdynia and Suez arrived in Harbin.
September 1939 came from Harbin
to Shanghai.
Since December 1939 I am working
as watchman of the Messageries Maritimes
Building.

Shanghai
10/III 1941

S. Vasiliev.

1939 年 9 月从哈尔滨
来到上海。
