At 3.10 p.m. 11-11-41, the undersigned, in
company with C.D.S. 12 and C.D.C. 90, visited the Dah
Sing Lodging House, (大新旅館, No. 108 Hoopeh Road.
Discreet enquiries were made at the lodging house, but
this proved fruitless, as no supposed representatives of
the workers now on strike were located therein.

At 10.10 a.m. 12-11-41, a visit was again paid at
the "Shanghai Times" by C.D.C. 261 and D.S.I. Chia Shao
Chi, where they interviewed one Mr. Mo Yoh Vung (馬敬之)
chief staff of the Advertisement Department. It was
learnt from him that 25 coolies had joined the strike
since 5 a.m. 12-11-41.

However, it was further ascertained that as the
result of the employment of a number of casual foreign
and Chinese workers, the printing department started its
function and the papers for 12-11-41 were published, the
machinery having been repaired.

Mr. Mo further informed the undersigned that the
representatives had removed from the Dah Sing Lodging
House, 108 Hoopeh Road, to Room No. 608 of the Grand
Hotel, Yu Ya Ching Road.

REPORT ON STRIKE AT THE "SHANGHAI TIMES".
No. 160 Avenue Edward VII.

On the morning of the 11-11-41, information was
received that workers of the "Shanghai Times", situated
at No. 160 Avenue Edward VII, were on strike, some had
not been reported by the proprietor, Mr. E.A. Nottingham.

At 10.15 a.m. 12-11-41, acting on the strength
of the information received, C.D.S. 12 and the under-
signed visited the "Shanghai Times", where they interviewed
Mr. E.A. Nottingham. He supplied with detectives with
the following particulars:-

The printing department of the said newspaper
establishment consists of 95 workers, among whom 78 are
male, 2 female and 15 apprentices. On the 6-11-41,
they asked for an increase of wage varying from 70%
to 100% over the present H.C.L. Allowance, which had
recently been granted to employees of the "N.C.D.N".

This request was, however, not met with as the
proprietor, Mr. E.A. Nottingham, only granted them an
increase from 20% to 25%. As no satisfaction was
obtained from the proprietor, the 95 workers declared a
strike at about 7 p.m. on the 10-11-41.

Mr. E.A. Nottingham further stated that some
vital parts of the machinery had been taken away by the

1941年11月11日上午，接获情报称，位于爱多亚路160号的《字林西报》工人正在罢工，部分情况尚未由业主 E.A. Nottingham 先生报告。

1941年11月12日上午10:15，根据所获情报，刑事侦缉股第12组（C.D.S. 12）及签署人前往《字林西报》，会见了 E.A. Nottingham 先生。他向侦探提供了以下详情：

该报社的印刷部门由95名工人组成，其中男性78名，女性2名，学徒15名。1941年11月6日，他们要求在近期授予“N.C.D.N.”雇员的 H.C.L. 津贴基础上，加薪70%至100%不等。

然而，这一请求未获满足，因为业主 E.A. Nottingham 先生仅同意在现有基础上增加20%至25%。由于从业主处未得到满意答复，这95名工人于1941年11月10日晚上7点左右宣布罢工。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
NOV 15 1939
BIG-SCALE CONTEST
FOR WRITERS
Essays, Novels, Plays,
Songs And Ditties
Are Invited
China's literary talents will have
an opportunity to display their
wares in a large-scale contest in
the writing of essays, novels, stage
and screen plays, songs and ditties
which has been announced by the
"Ksing Kien Monthly," a local
Chinese publication.
The competition, in which
attractive cash prizes are offered,
is said to be in connection with
the movement for national recon-
struction and Asiatic regeneration,
with the establishment of peace in
Asia as the basis.
According to the rules, each
essay should contain not more
than 5,000 words and based on
these four points: (1) That China's
present political, economic and
social system is in a precarious
state; (2) That a new ideology for
the nation and a new order
in the Far East should be estab-
lished; (3) That the Communist
and other doctrines have failed to
improve the lot of the people; and
(4) That geographical, historical
and racial factors make the estab-
lishment of a new order in the
Far East imperative. The best
dissertation will be awarded a
prize of $2,000, with minor prizes
for nine others.
Novel on Life In China
For the novel, with a maximum
of 30,000 words, real and actual
life in present-day China should
be depicted. First prize for this
type of work is also $2,000.
As regards the stage or screen
play, which should be written for
a two-hour performance, a sum of
$1,500 is offered for the first prize.
The moving factors of current
affairs in this country should be
played up and given stress in the
plot.
The song or ditty should treat
of the ideal of Asiatic regeneration
and the cause of national recon-
struction, and should be as short
as possible. $500 is to be awarded to
the first-prize winner.
The contest will be closed at
midnight, January 31, 1940 and the
results will be announced publicly
on May 1, 1940. Under tentative
arrangements, it has been learnt
that authors of the winning manu-
scripts will be entitled to a royalty
of 30 per cent. of the proceeds
realized from the sale of their
works to be published in book
form. They will also be published
in the "Hsin Kien Monthly" and
other magazines, it is stated.
Manuscripts should be addressed
to Post Office Box 1708.
（批：lu also see on Kam
Shing chieu (S.B.)

1939年11月15日
大型征文比赛
面向作家
征集散文、小说、剧本、
歌曲和小调
据本地中文刊物《新建月刊》（Ksing Kien Monthly）宣布，中国的文学人才将有机会在一次大型比赛中展示他们的作品，比赛类别包括散文、小说、舞台剧和电影剧本、歌曲和小调。
据悉，这项提供诱人现金奖励的比赛，与以亚洲和平为基础的国家重建和亚洲复兴运动有关。
根据规则，每篇散文不得超过5000字，并基于以下四点：(1) 中国目前的政治、经济和社会制度处于危险状态；(2) 应建立新的国家意识形态和远东新秩序；(3) 共产主义和其他学说未能改善人民的命运；(4) 地理、历史和种族因素使得建立远东新秩序成为当务之急。最佳论文将获得2000美元奖金，另有九篇获得次要奖项。
关于中国生活的小说
小说类作品字数上限为30,000字，应描绘当今中国的真实生活。此类作品的一等奖也为2000美元。
至于舞台剧或电影剧本，应按两小时演出时长编写，一等奖金额为1500美元。
剧情应突出并强调本国当前时事的推动因素。
歌曲或小调应涉及亚洲复兴的理想和国家重建的事业，并应尽可能简短。一等奖获得者将获得500美元。
比赛将于1940年1月31日午夜截止，结果将于1940年5月1日公布。据初步安排，获悉获奖手稿的作者有权获得其作品出版成书后销售收益的30%作为版税。据说，这些作品还将在《新建月刊》（Hsin Kien Monthly）和其他杂志上发表。
手稿请寄至邮政信箱1708号。
（批注：lu 另见 Kam Shing chieu (特别处)
C. 6116. (特别处)
附言。）

Information of a proposed attack on
the offices of "Shopping News" by
Italian Marines

Sir,

At 7p.m. September 19, 1940, Mr. Don Chisholm,
American, publisher of Shopping News, Room 532
Hardoon Building, 233 Nanking Road, reported that
he had received information on two occasions to-day
(Sept. 19) that Italian Marines would probably pay
a visit to his office on Friday or Saturday morning
with intent of wrecking the place.

Mr. Chisholm emphasized that he was not asking
for Police protection as he was armed, but wished
to make an official report in the event of some of
the marines getting shot.

He did not disclose the source of his information
and stated that he had just simply been "tipped off".

There might be a certain amount of truth in
Chisholm's information, and that the affair has been
planned by the Italians in retaliation for some
derogatory article published in the Shopping News
concerning them.

There is no doubt that Chisholm will not
hesitate to shoot should the incident take place
and he be about at the time.

Police have been posted inside the building.

（印：INDEXED BY (S.B.) REGISTRY DATE 21/9/40 JSay）

拟袭击《购物新闻》报社的情报

先生，

1940年9月19日下午7时，《购物新闻》的美籍出版商 Don Chisholm 先生，
办公地点位于南京路233号哈同大楼（Hardoon Building）532室，
报告称他今天（9月19日）两次收到消息，
意大利海军陆战队可能会在周五或周六上午
造访他的办公室，意图捣毁该处。

Chisholm 先生强调，他并未请求警方保护，因为他持有武器，
但希望正式报案，以防万一有海军陆战队员被枪击。

他未透露消息来源，仅表示他是刚刚得到“通风报信”。

Chisholm 的情报可能有一定真实性，此事可能是意大利人
为报复《购物新闻》刊登的有关他们的贬损文章而策划的。

毫无疑问，如果事件发生且 Chisholm 当时在场，
他将毫不犹豫地开枪。

警方已部署在大楼内部。

S.5, Special Branch,
September 1, 1939.

"Shopping News" - Objectionable references to
Council Services.
------------------------------------

Acting upon the instructions of the Officer
i/c Special Branch ament the August 28th issue of
"Shopping News," and its objectionable references
to the S.M.C. services, Mr. E.F. Stanton, U.S.
Consulate-General, was interviewed on September 1st
when he was shown the attached clippings from the paper
in question.

Mr. Stanton stated that the "Shopping News"
was the type of yellow sheet to be ignored, unless the
editor publishes something to warrant prosecution,
any effort at suppression through the Consulate or
otherwise would, under existing circumstances, only be
tantamount to stirring up a wasps nest. He explained
that the article to which exception has been taken
could only be met by an official complaint from the
S.M.C. resulting in the despatch by the Consulate-
General of a letter to R.D. Chisholm, which in Mr. Stanton's
considered opinion would have no good effect.

It would appear that American newspapers enjoy
far greater licence than English newspapers, whilst
municipal government in the U.S.A. provides particularly
the entire copy for papers of Chisholm sheet's
category.

Certified true copy.
J. F. Lovell

S.5，特务科，
1939年9月1日。

“《购物新闻》”—— 对工部局服务的令人反感的提及。
------------------------------------

根据特务科主管警官关于8月28日出版的
“《购物新闻》”及其对工部局服务令人反感的提及的指示，
E.F. Stanton 先生（美国总领事馆）于9月1日接受了问询，
期间向他展示了所附的该报剪报。

Stanton 先生表示，“《购物新闻》”属于那种应予忽略的黄色小报，
除非编辑发表了足以起诉的内容，否则通过领事馆或其他途径
进行的任何压制努力，在现有情况下，无异于捅马蜂窝。他解释说，
对于受到非议的文章，唯一的应对方式是工部局提出正式投诉，
从而导致总领事馆向 R.D. Chisholm 发送一封信函，
而在 Stanton 先生看来，这不会产生任何良好效果。

看来，美国报纸享有的自由度远大于英国报纸，
而美国的市政府实际上特别为 Chisholm 这类小报
提供了全部的报道素材。

经核证无误副本。
J. F. Lovell

page_data.en:
Shopping News
August 28, 1939

CAT TAILS
WE join Judge Jones in jeers and hisses towards our local
Gas Company Tycoons. The spotlight of publicity should
be thrown full upon any corporation which, showing a fat profit,
whines for surcharges and unfair ways of mulcting the public,
while at the same time cuts the wages of their workers to a
point which almost forces them to steal for a bare living. And
wasn't it Gas Tycoon Carney who, at the last Ratepayers Meet-
ing, arose to shout abusive remarks at Ratepayer Stewart, while
the latter was pleading for economy in S.M.C. affairs? Orchids
to Judge Jones for his fair outspoken condemnation. This is
not an age of slavery, or a period when the Public will allow
a British or any other Corporation to pay starvation wages in
order to fatten their already bloated dividend checks. So help
us, if, and when, the Gas Company petitions for another sur-
charge we'll gladly head a delegation of hissers to scare the
Fatcats from the Public Trough.

WHILE the Council cannot afford to buy rice stocks to feed
our hungry populace they are prepared to provide a few
nice programs of Municipal music....providing the hungry
human has the money to pay admission to the Municipal Parks.
We don't know just how satisfying Maestro Paci's rendering
of Puccini's Operas are to a hungry stomach, but we doubt if
even our $240,000.00 Municipal Orchestra can produce enough
calories to satisfy a sparrows appetite.

SPEAKING about the high
cost of living our investiga-
tions have discovered some local
firms exhibiting an attitude of
generous sympathy towards
their employees, some a com-
plete indifference. For inst-
ance, we find the Asia Theatres
(who haven't yet increased
admissions) increasing the
wages of their Chinese em-
ployees by the munificent sum
of 10%, their foreign employees
by 15%. On the other hand we
find the Shanghai Power Com-
pany dishing out a 250% in-
crease to those of their em-
ployees entitled to home leave.
WHICH MAY EXPLAIN ONE
OF THE CAUSES FOR A
120.01% SURCHARGE NEXT
MONTH, a 25% increase to
locally employed Chinese and
foreigners alike. To our way
of reckoning a 40% increase
will just about let the average
wage earner break even.
page_data.zh:
《购物新闻》
1939年8月28日

猫尾巴
我们与琼斯法官一起，对我们当地的
煤气公司巨头发出嘘声和蔑视。聚光灯应该
完全照射在任何一家 corporation 身上，它们一方面展示着丰厚的利润，
一边哭诉要求附加费并以不公平的方式榨取公众钱财，
同时却将工人的工资削减到几乎迫使他们为了勉强糊口而去偷窃的地步。
难道不是那位煤气巨头 Carney，在上次的纳税人会议上，
当 Stewart 纳税人恳求在工部局事务中节约开支时，
起身对 Stewart 纳税人大声辱骂吗？向公正直言谴责的琼斯法官致敬。
这不是奴隶制的时代，也不是公众会允许英国或任何其他公司
支付饥饿工资以使其已经膨胀的分红支票更加肥厚的时期。
所以请帮助我们，如果，以及当，煤气公司申请另一项附加费时，
我们将欣然率领一群嘘声者代表团，将这些肥猫从公共食槽旁吓跑。

虽然工部局负担不起购买大米储备来喂养
我们饥饿的民众，但他们准备提供几场
不错的市政音乐节目……前提是饥饿的人
有钱支付进入市政公园的门票。我们不知道帕基大师演奏的
普契尼歌剧对饥饿的胃有多大满足感，但我们怀疑，
即使是我们价值240,000.00美元的市政管弦乐队，
也无法产生足够的卡路里来满足一只麻雀的食欲。

说到生活成本高昂，我们的调查
发现一些本地公司对员工表现出
慷慨的同情的态度，另一些则
完全漠不关心。例如，我们发现
亚洲大戏院（尚未提高入场费）
将其中国员工的工资提高了
10% 这一巨额数目，外籍员工
提高了 15%。另一方面，我们
发现上海电力公司向其有权享受
回国休假的员工发放了 250% 的
加薪。这或许可以解释下个月
120.01% 附加费的原因之一，
以及对本地雇佣的中国人和外国人
一律加薪 25%。按照我们的计算，
40% 的加薪刚好能让普通工薪阶层
收支平衡。

page_data.en:
Shanghai News
August 28, 1939

SO the Shanghai Municipal Council has again granted the
Shanghai Power Company permission to put Settlement users
of electricity thru' the wringers....this time for a surcharge
of 120.01%. In other words, this so called public utility is to
be allowed to collect it's charges upon what amounts practically
to a gold dollar basis. How is it possible for the S.P.C. to put
such a tremendous surcharge over on the public? Frankly, we
don't know, but we suggest you ask S.M.C. Chairman Cornell
Franklin, who, as attorney for the S.P.C. at an alleged retainer
of $50,000 a year, and as Chairman of the S.M.C. the official
body pledged to safeguard the interests of the general public,
should be in a position to know all the little intimate details.
INTERESTING IS THAT THE FRENCHTOWN POWER
COMPANY WHO HAVE THE SAME GENERAL OPERATING
COSTS TO MEET (BUT DON'T HAVE TO FEED GOLD
DOLLARS TO THE NEW YORK FATCATS) HAVE IN-
CREASED TO DATE ONLY FIFTEEN PERCENT.

SO the police in the Western District have now been ordered
by our wistful Willies in the Council to look the other way
if they notice any trouble, fill their ears with cotton so the
sound of shooting will listen like peas popping, and if they're
actually shot at to stand perfectly still so as not to spoil the
dear, darling Ta Tao gunmen's aim. Darn if we wouldn't like
to put those Pivot Boys and Messrs: Franklin, Mitchell, and
a few others out on Badland patrol....at 26 shillings a week.
We'll bet a million these gentry would scram so fast you could
play checkers on their shirt tails.

SO the S.M.C. and the F.M.C. have been doing everything in
their power to curb rice profiteering and relieve the des-
perate plight of the masses. As a result of these strenuous
efforts on the part of our authorities, local rice prices have
increased only THREE HUNDRED PERCENT. It looks almost
as though the rice profiteers had received assurance from high
places that the track was being cleared for them and the sky
was the limit. Recently, we called these rice profiteers and
their political protectors vultures....today we extend our
apologies to the vultures.

WHICH reminds us that with
the full permission of the
Council, the S.P.C. seems out
with a vengeance to get back
that mythical 60 million dollars
the Power Boys are alleged to
have paid the S.M.C.'s Treasury
for what was once an honest to
goodness publicly owned utility.
Now just whatever could have
become of that sixty million?
Bet "Fessy" knows, but like the
daisies, he won't tell.
page_data.zh:
上海新闻
1939年8月28日

看来，上海公共租界工部局再次批准上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company）对租界内的用电户进行盘剥……这次的附加费高达120.01%。换言之，这家所谓的公用事业机构被允许按照几乎等同于金本位美元的标准来收取费用。工部局怎么可能将如此巨额的附加费强加于公众？坦白说，我们不知道，但我们建议您去问问工部局主席康奈尔·富兰克林（Cornell Franklin）。他作为上海电力公司的法律顾问，据称年薪高达5万美元，同时又是工部局主席，而工部局是誓言保护广大公众利益的官方机构，因此他理应知晓所有细微的内情。有趣的是，法租界电力公司面临着大致相同的运营成本（但不必向纽约的那些肥头大耳者进贡金元），迄今为止仅增加了百分之十五。

看来，西区巡捕如今已接到我们工部局里那些多愁善感的“威利们”（Willies，指优柔寡断者）的命令：如果注意到任何麻烦，就视而不见；把耳朵塞上棉花，让枪声听起来像爆豆子一样轻微；如果真的遭到射击，就原地站立不动，以免干扰亲爱的、可爱的“大刀队”枪手的瞄准。真恨不得把那些“轴心男孩”（Pivot Boys，指亲日或摇摆不定者）以及富兰克林先生、米切尔先生和其他几位送到“恶地”（Badland，指混乱危险地区）去巡逻……周薪26先令。我敢打赌一百万，这些绅士逃窜的速度之快，你甚至可以在他们的燕尾服后摆上玩跳棋。

看来，工部局和公董局（F.M.C.，即法租界公董局）一直在竭尽全力遏制大米投机，缓解民众的绝望困境。在我们当局这些不懈努力的成果下，本地米价仅仅上涨了百分之三百。这看起来几乎就像是大米投机者已从高层得到保证，道路已为他们扫清，前途无限。最近，我们将这些大米投机者及其政治庇护者称为秃鹫……今天，我们要向秃鹫致歉。

page_data.en:
Shopping News
August 28, 1939

AFTER a week's survey of local police conditions, we find
that more than forty foreign officers have already forward-
ed in their resignations, that another seventy intend doing so.
There are probably many more members of our once brilliantly
organized police force who, fed up on the disgraceful treatment
dished out to them by the Council, intend sending in resigna-
tions. It may be the Council's sneaking desire to get rid of
these fine, well trained policeman, who have, over a period of
years, contributed their best efforts towards creating one of
the world's finest forces. The Council may feel that Russians
and Jewish Refugees will do for police replacements, and these
men need be paid less than a hundred local dollars a month.
The "economy" thus achieved by Councilman Mitchell and his
Staff Committee can be added to the already bloated salaries
of Councilman Mitchell's Pivot Boy Pets. By the way....we
hadn't noticed before that S. M. Counciler Mitchell lives in
Frenchtown and also has his offices in Frenchtown. He should
worry if we have Boy Scouts for police over here in the
Settlement.

TEN Percent Mills in his Olympian column last week made
news. Mills insists that a certain nite club off Settle-
ment Roads proposed having a nude floor show, was quickly
jumped upon by the S.M.P. who promised to immediately
barricade the entrance to the nite spot. If Ten Percent's yarn
is true, how come the police have power to barricade a strip-
tease yet can do nothing at all about blocking the entrances
to the gambling hells which are nightly ruining far more
Villagers than could a dozen strip tease acts.

IF, and when, the Council's Old Guard gets busted open like a
termite tasted log of rotten timber, it will be a direct
outcome of their own blind avarice and their increasing diligence
in safeguarding and increasing their own riches. The Council,
beside being a gathering of the people....says who?....is the
finest Big Business Club in town. Well represented are land-
lords, public utilities, shipping, insurance, banking and the
membership of the Shanghai Club. The first principle of justice
is that "No man shall be a judge in his own cause"....or are
we wrong?

SO the Council is to consider the Gas Company's application
for increased surcharges. That is, they will consider them
upon their return from summer recess. If, and when, they do
we want our four thousand readers to phone S. M. Chairman
Franklin and shout. Phooey! Remember Mr. Davis!

购物新闻
1939年8月28日

在对本地警务状况进行了一周的调查后，我们发现已有四十多名外籍警官递交了辞呈，另有七十人打算这样做。可能还有更多曾经组织严密、表现出色的警队成员，因受够了工部局给予他们的屈辱待遇，也打算递交辞呈。这也许是工部局暗中希望摆脱这些优秀且训练有素的警察，他们在过去多年中为打造世界一流的警队贡献了最大努力。工部局可能认为俄罗斯人和犹太难民足以替代警察，而且这些人的月薪不到一百元本地货币。米切尔议员及其_staff_委员会由此实现的“节约”，可以加在米切尔议员的“轴心男孩”宠儿们已经膨胀的薪水之上。顺便说一句……我们之前没注意到，工部局议员米切尔住在法租界，办公室也在法租界。如果我们这边租界里的警察由童子军来担任，他才该担心呢。

“百分之十”米尔斯（Ten Percent Mills）在他上周的专栏文章中制造了新闻。米尔斯坚称，某家位于租界道路之外的夜总会提议举办裸体歌舞表演，随即遭到上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的迅速打压，警方承诺立即封锁该娱乐场所的入口。如果“百分之十”的故事属实，那么为什么警方有权封锁脱衣舞表演，却对每晚毁掉比十几场脱衣舞表演多得多的村民生活的赌博窟窿束手无策，连入口都无法封锁？

如果，或者说当，工部局的“老卫队”像一根被白蚁蛀烂的朽木一样崩塌时，那将是他们盲目贪婪以及日益勤勉地保护和增加自身财富的直接后果。工部局，除了是人民的集会……谁说的？……它是城里最高级的商业俱乐部。地主、公用事业、航运、保险、银行业以及上海俱乐部的会员都在其中拥有充分的代表权。正义的第一原则是“任何人不得在自己的案件中担任法官”……还是说我们错了？

看来，工部局将要审议煤气公司增加附加费的申请。也就是说，他们将在夏季休会归来后予以审议。如果，或者说当他们审议时，我们希望我们的四千名读者致电工部局主席富兰克林并高喊：“呸！”记住戴维斯先生！

AUG 5 1933

Local Columnists to
Stage Grudge Fight

After much verbal battling,
Hal P. Mills, local columnist,
suddenly hurled a challenge at
the head of Don Chisholm, of
"Shopping News," to do battle
tonight with leather gloves in
the Auditorium programme at
the Fronton. The author of
"Cat Tails" heard the challenge
on the radio last night and
immediately telephoned his
acceptance, insisting that the
side-bet be raised from $150 to
$300, which was agreed to.
Thus tonight, boxing followers
will be treated to the spectacle
of two determined, but far from
fit, scribes going after each
other hammer and tongs for
three two-minute rounds or
less, in order to express for-
cibly their feelings towards
each other. Local charity will
receive the $600.

本地专栏作家
将上演宿怨对决

经过长时间的口舌之争，本地专栏作家哈尔·P·米尔斯（Hal P. Mills）突然向《购物新闻》的唐·奇泽姆（Don Chisholm）发起挑战，要求今晚在Fronton（前滩/回力球场）的礼堂节目中戴着皮手套进行搏斗。《猫尾巴》（Cat Tails）的作者昨晚通过收音机听到了这一挑战，并立即打电话表示接受，坚持将侧注从150美元提高到300美元，对方同意了。因此，今晚拳击爱好者将看到两位意志坚定但身体状况远非最佳的文人，为了有力地表达彼此间的感受，在三个两分钟的回合或更短时间内激烈互殴。所得600美元将捐赠给本地慈善机构。

DECEMBER 19, 1938
SHOPPING NEWS 314/-F-
12

MARCO PHOOEY
An Analysis of the Egg That Goldwyn Laid
By Martin Davies

Marco Polo was a Medieval traveler and adventurer. It took him three years to get from Venice to China and six hundred and sixty years to get to Hollywood, but boy it was worth it, because he hadn't seem anything in adventures till Sam Goldwyn took him around!

Now, I don't know a damn thing about projection or direction, folks, all I know is the silliest movie of the century when I see it. And "The Adventures of Marco Polo," produced (out of a silk hat after not enough practise) by Goldwyn, adapted (to the moron mind) by Robert Sherwood, directed (at the mewling masses) by Archie Mayo, is it, folks, is it. Historical extravaganza is how Mr. Goldwyn tags it, and at least it's extravagant, but not half as extravagant as you'll be if you buy tickets....

Let's have a glimpse of history first, so you'll know what it's all not about.

In 1260, Venetian Tycoons Nicolo and Maffeo Polo, father and uncle of Marco, were the first Europeans to tour China. In 1271 they went again taking Marco with them, aged 17. Marco studied Chinese and the local big shot Kublai Khan gave him a public service job. In 1286, "the lady Kucachin, a maiden of 17," had to be convoyed to Persia to marry the Persian khan. The latter's favorite wife, a Chinese, had died, requesting she be replaced by another Mongol goal. Kublai picked Kucachin, no relation to himself, for the honor and delegated the Polos to be chief bodyguards and guides.

War was on with southern China, the two-year trip was tough and most of the suite succumbed. But the Polos, who were tougher, survived, and, says the Encyclopedia Britannica, "so did the young lady, who had come to look on them with filial regard." Filial—get it? On Marco, too, now an old gent of thirty-four, she looked as upon her pappy, and neither the Encyc. nor

Marco's own book mentions anything about him having hot pants. When they finally reached Persia the king had died and still Marco didn't marry the gal. The king's son did, like a gent, since she'd come all that way. The Polos went home to Venice, and after fighting in the Venetian-Genoan war and writing his memoirs while in enemy stir, Marco copped off a home-town girl and sired three daughters.

That's history, and not even God can change it, only a Hollywood producer. Let's observe to what extent Mr. Goldwyn did rape it to get his tale....

In the opening scene (Venice) Tycoon Nicolo calls a fellow merchant his anemic cousin. Did they know about anemia in 1271? Nicolo's making the local importers' eyes pop with a lay-out of bangles and tiaras. He got them from China, he explains, where no European has ever gone. Well then, how'd he get them—by mail order? If some European could get there, envisions Nicolo with gleaming eye, such gimcracks as this could pull business for Polo Bros., Inc. And sonny-boy Marco, he cheers, is their man!

So Marco (Gary Cooper) sets out to bring back the sparklers his pop already has, and with him sets out one Binguccio (Ernest Truex), the "comic relief," which means it's a relief all comics aren't like him. (There's nothing funny about sore feet, Mr. Goldwyn—a murrain on you of bunions, ingrowing toenails and corns!) They're shipwrecked and hauled ashore sans luggage, yet don Venetian finery in Peking. After the shipwreck they meet a sandstorm and coax their horses to lie down so they can hide behind them, the nags luckily having gone to Hollywood Horse College to learn how to behave on the Goldwyn Gobi. And in less time than it takes to say a simple one-syllable

马可·呸
戈尔温产下的那颗蛋之分析
作者：马丁·戴维斯

马可·波罗是一位中世纪的旅行家和冒险家。他花了三年时间从威尼斯来到中国，又花了六百六十年才到达好莱坞，但伙计，这很值得，因为在山姆·戈尔温（Sam Goldwyn）带他四处游历之前，他根本没见识过什么是冒险！

现在，我对投影或导演一窍不通，朋友们，我只知道当我看到本世纪最愚蠢的电影时，我就认得它。而《马可·波罗历险记》，由戈尔温（从礼帽里变出来似的，因为练习不足）制作，由罗伯特·舍伍德（Robert Sherwood）改编（以适应低能儿的思维），由阿奇·梅奥（Archie Mayo）执导（针对哀鸣的大众），就是这样，朋友们，就是这样。戈尔温先生将其标签为“历史奇观”，至少它确实奢华，但如果你买票的话，你的破费会比这奢华得多……

让我们先瞥一眼历史，这样你就知道这部电影完全不是关于什么的。

1260年，威尼斯大亨尼科洛和马费奥·波罗，即马可的父亲和叔叔，是首批游览中国的欧洲人。1271年，他们再次前往，带上了17岁的马可。马可学习了中文，当地的大人物忽必烈汗给了他一份公职。1286年，“17岁的少女库卡钦女士”（Lady Kucachin）必须被护送至波斯，嫁给波斯汗。后者宠爱的中国妻子去世前请求由另一位蒙古姑娘取代。忽必烈挑选了与他无亲属关系的库卡钦承担此荣誉，并委派波罗家族担任首席保镖和向导。

当时正与中国南方交战，两年的旅程十分艰难，随行人员大多病死。但更为坚韧的波罗家族幸存下来，正如《大英百科全书》所说，“那位年轻女士也幸存下来，并对他们产生了子女般的敬意。”子女般——懂吗？对于当时已是34岁老人的马可，她也视如父亲，《百科全书》和马可自己的书都没有提到他有任何非分之想。当他们最终到达波斯时，国王已经去世，马可仍然没有娶这位姑娘。国王的儿子像个绅士一样娶了她，因为她远道而来。波罗家族回到了威尼斯，在参加威尼斯-热那亚战争并在敌方监狱中撰写回忆录之后，马可娶了一位本地姑娘，并育有三个女儿。

这就是历史，连上帝都无法改变它，只有好莱坞制片人可以。让我们看看戈尔温先生为了编造他的故事，在多大程度上强奸了历史……

在开场场景（威尼斯）中，大亨尼科洛称一位商人为他贫血的表弟。1271年的人知道贫血症吗？尼科洛正在用一批手镯和头饰让本地进口商目瞪口呆。他解释说这些来自中国，那里从未有欧洲人去过的地方。那么，他是怎么得到的——邮购吗？尼科洛眼中闪烁着光芒设想，如果有些欧洲人能去那里，像这样的廉价小饰品就能为波罗兄弟公司（Polo Bros., Inc.）带来生意。而宝贝儿子马可，他欢呼道，就是他们的人选！

于是马可（加里·库珀饰）出发去带回他老爸已经拥有的那些闪亮饰品，随行的还有宾古乔（Binguccio，欧内斯特·特鲁克斯饰），即“喜剧调剂”，这意味着其他喜剧演员不像他那样是一种解脱。（脚痛没什么好笑的，戈尔温先生——祝你长满鸡眼、嵌甲和老茧！）他们遭遇海难，被拖上岸时身无行李，却在北京穿上了威尼斯的华丽服饰。海难后，他们遇到了沙尘暴，并哄骗马匹躺下以便躲在后面，这些驽马幸好去过好莱坞马术学院，学习如何在戈尔温戈壁滩上表现。而在说出一个简单的单音节词所需的时间内……

SHOPPING NEWS
DECEMBER 19, 1938

MARCO PHOOEY
(Continued from Page 22)
word in the plural, our wanderers enter Peking, in fealthy rags.

Their first colorful glimpse of 13th Century China comes when they pause piously to listen to a Chinese (H. B. Warner and looking it) reading from the Bible in English to two Chinese tots. Don't forget that according to Mr. Goldwyn himself, no Christian has yet penetrated Old Cathay. Luckily, though, all 13th Century Chinese speak English, the Italians' native tongue. The Bible, you can see, is printed in Chinese, but Pappy is translating into English as he goes along, so the kiddies can understand. And this is a good place to throw in a comment by The New York Times: "Possibly one of the limiting factors has been the remarkable range of accents Mr. Goldwyn culled into the court of Kublai Khan. The Khan speaks with George Barbier's nasal Philadelphian, the Venetian Marco with Mr. Cooper's Montana drawl, the Saracen Ahmed with Basil Rathbone's clipped Londonese, the Princess Kucachin with Sigrid Gurie's Garboesque Norwegian, the servant Binguccio with Ernest Truex's Burbanked Kansas-Broadway. And we're not counting Binnie Barnes' Cockney, Stanley Fields' growling Pennsylvanian, Ferdinand Gottschalk's whatever-it-is."

Marco's Montana drawl interrupts cozily and finishes the Bible quotation and the Chinese is so impressed that he invites the weary travelers to dinner. They've got baggage on their backs now and they might change out of their feelth before dinner, but they don't. Their Chinese host says grace and then produces spaghetti, which the Italians have never seen and can't eat without drooling, and which is an old Chinese custom locally termed "spaghet'." Marco is so impressed that he puts some spaghet' in his wallet to take home and circulate among the wops. Now, I have had the mean nasty curiosity to look up spaghetti, and all I can find is that it was "originally peculiar to Italy," with no record of China discovering it first. As to China's sponsoring coal, the Greeks had coal in 371 B. C., while coal cinders were found in the ruins of Roman towns and forts in Britain which date to the Roman era there, and that was from 43 A. D. to the 5th Century.

The Chinese kids pull a Katzenjammer with gunpowder under the snoozing Binguccio and get good American spans on their cans from their pop; Marco puts some gunpowder in his wallet, and he and Bing are off for the Palace still in a cloud of feelth.

The soldier to whom Marco gives his letter of introduction can't read it but he speaks English all right. And so into the presence of the great Kublai Khan, who is a dead ringer for Belle Livingstone, in looks, manner and talk.

Bored with the Khan's impersonation, Marco wanders into the big shot's daughter's boodwah. (Everybody pops in and out of the Princess's precincts, she's got no privacy at all.) Kucachin gazes up inch by inch to see if her prince has come. It's only an American cowboy dressed like Columbus (yeah, he's had a bath at last) but she tumbles just the same. Too late, too late, she got engaged to the Persian king while in her cradle. Don't worry, folks, Mr. Goldwyn is here and everything'll turn out all right.

Back in the Khan's presence Marco goes Solomon and helps Kublai pick court attendants by asking each gal how many teeth a snapping turtle has and electing those that say they don't know. But the scene's historical value lies not in Marco's sappliance (I said sappliance), but in the fact that this is the most interesting bevy of beauty ever assembled in a 13th Century Chinese court. There is one modern Jap among them, one Swede, and the rest are Miss Kansas City, Miss Albany, Miss San Antonio, etc. The make-up man never even struck a stroke! According to Goldwyn history the Chinese people of the 13th Century were comprised of: (1) the Chinese (the majority of the army), (2) the Americans trying to look Chinese, and (3) the natives frankly American. Nobody tries to act Chinese; nobody's inscrutable. Nobody tries to pretend he's anything but himself, except Princess Kucachin trying to be Garbo and Kublai Khan Belle Livingstone.

The next time that Marco drifts back into the Princess's chambers without knocking he shows her how to kiss, as best the art had been developed in Venice in 1271. It wouldn't get by nowadays, not that puckering-up stuff. But anyway it's dynamite for getting the plot going, thank God. Ahminpresent Ahmed the Sinister Minister finds out and influences the Khan to send Marco on a mission whence he will Never Return. And sure enough, captured as spies, Marco and Bing are brought before the provincial ruler Kaidu (Ferdinand Gottschalk in pickaninny pigtails) and doomed to die.

But hold! Kaidu's wife (Binnie Barnes) thinks Marco's cute, and Kaidu spares him gladly because Kaidu's henpecked, his wife won't let him neck the serving-girl, and now's his chance! Marco must entertain Kaidu's frau or else be boiled in oil! And he doesn't want to, folks, even if she is a slinky blonde. He wants to be true to Kookie!

Meanwhile Kublai Khan marches off to conquer Japan, a nice tie-up with modern news interest. A typhoon swamps the Chinese army in the China sea and Ahmed grabs the throne and tells Kookie that she's his queen.

Cut back to Marco. Kaidu's wife's got him alone! She's climbing his frame, she's doing the Mae West crawl! She's backing him against the ropes, he's on his bicycle, folks, he doesn't want to smudge his love for Kookie, but neither does he want to be fried in deep fat. Aw-w-w-w—he's gonna give up, the coward. He's gonna betray the trust of that sweet little girl! But wait—wait, folks, what's this development? Hooray—Kaidu's wife only wants to rub noses! She's inscrutable! Marco won't have to be untrue to Kookie after all!

And look, look, what's this? A carrier hawk flapping over Kaidu's camp! They shoot it down and tied to its leg is a message. It's from the Princess but it doesn't say anything. She's got a finishing-school accent but she can't write. All it says is The Princess,. Her Mark, but Marco, who's a punster at heart, knows that means it's for him. And not only that, but he knows it means she's in danger, come at once. Oh now, Mr. Goldwyn, that's going too far. How does he know it doesn't just mean "Aunt Minnie Whangpoo was over for dinner and afterwards we all made fudge."

No matter what it says, Kaidu won't let him go. He's got to stay and rub noses with Kaidu's wife. Meanwhile — flash — the Khan returns home from the wars, a broken old man. He didn't get swamped in the China sea, only his army. And now—and now, heh heh—he must sign the polpers deeding his kingdom and daughter to Ahmed, or else the buzzards will be turned loose to eat poor Kookie who lies chained beneath their evil beaks!

What can a pappy do? He signs,

购物新闻
1938年12月19日

马可·波罗（Marco Phooey）
（接第22页）
用复数形式来说，我们的流浪者身着肮脏的破衣烂衫进入了北京。

他们对13世纪中国的第一次多彩一瞥，发生在他们虔诚地驻足聆听一名中国人（由H. B. Warner饰演，且形象相符）用英语向两名中国幼童朗读《圣经》之时。别忘了，据戈德温先生本人称，尚无基督徒涉足古老的中国。幸运的是，所有13世纪的中国人都会说英语，即意大利人的母语。你可以看到，《圣经》是用中文印刷的，但“老爹”一边读一边将其翻译成英语，以便孩子们能听懂。在此处不妨引用《纽约时报》的一条评论：“也许限制因素之一是戈德温先生在忽必烈汗宫廷中汇集的各种口音。汗王说着乔治·巴比尔（George Barbier）那带有鼻音的费城腔，威尼斯人马可说着库珀先生（Mr. Cooper）的蒙大拿拖长音，撒拉森人艾哈迈德说着巴西尔·拉斯伯恩（Basil Rathbone）干脆利落的伦敦腔，库卡钦公主说着西格丽德·古里（Sigrid Gurie）那种嘉宝式的挪威腔，仆人宾古乔说着欧内斯特·特鲁克斯（Ernest Truex）那种伯班克式的堪萨斯-百老汇混合腔。这还没算上宾妮·巴恩斯（Binnie Barnes）的 cockney 伦敦东区腔，斯坦利·菲尔兹（Stanley Fields）低沉的宾夕法尼亚腔，以及费迪南德·戈特沙尔克（Ferdinand Gottschalk）不管是什么腔。”

马可的蒙大拿拖长音亲切地打断了朗读，结束了《圣经》引文，那位中国人深受感动，邀请疲惫的旅人共进晚餐。他们现在背着行李，本可以在饭前换下身上的脏衣服，但他们没有。他们的中国东道主做了饭前祷告，然后端出了意大利面，这是意大利人从未见过、吃得口水直流的东西，而这在当地是一种被称为“spaghet'”的中国古老习俗。马可深受感动，把一些“spaghet'”放进钱包，打算带回家在意大利同胞中传阅。现在，我怀着卑鄙恶劣的好奇心查了一下意大利面，所能找到的只是它“原为意大利特有”，没有任何记录显示是中国首先发现了它。至于中国推广煤炭的说法，希腊人在公元前371年就有了煤炭，而在英国罗马城镇和堡垒的废墟中发现了可追溯至罗马时代（公元43年至5世纪）的煤渣。

中国孩子们趁宾古乔打盹时用火药搞恶作剧，结果被他们的父亲狠狠地打了屁股；马可把一些火药放进钱包，他和宾吉依然浑身污垢，前往皇宫。

马可将介绍信交给那名士兵，士兵虽看不懂信，但英语说得不错。于是他们得以觐见伟大的忽必烈汗，这位汗王在外貌、举止和谈吐上都与贝尔·利文斯通（Belle Livingstone）如出一辙。

马可对汗王的模仿感到厌倦，溜进了这位大人物的女儿的闺房。（每个人都在公主的领地进进出出，她毫无隐私可言。）库卡钦一寸寸地向上打量，看看她的王子是否到来。来的只是一个打扮得像哥伦布的美国牛仔（是的，他终于洗了澡），但她还是坠入爱河。太晚了，太晚了，她在摇篮里时就已许配给波斯国王。别担心，各位，戈德温先生在这里，一切都会好起来的。

回到汗王面前，马可表现得所罗门般智慧，通过询问每位女子“一只咬人乌龟有多少颗牙齿”并选中那些回答不知道的女子，帮助忽必烈挑选宫廷侍从。但这一场景的历史价值不在于马可的愚钝（我说的是愚钝），而在于这是13世纪中国宫廷中聚集的最有趣的美女群像。其中有一位现代日本人，一位瑞典人，其余则是堪萨斯城小姐、奥尔巴尼小姐、圣安东尼奥小姐等。化妆师甚至都没怎么动手！根据戈德温式的历史，13世纪的中国人民由以下组成：(1) 中国人（军队的大多数），(2) 试图看起来像中国人的美国人，以及 (3) 坦率地表现为美国人的本地人。没有人试图扮演中国人；没有人显得高深莫测。除了试图扮演嘉宝的库卡钦公主和扮演贝尔·利文斯通的忽必烈汗外，没有人试图假装自己是其他人。

下一次马可不敲门就飘进公主的房间时，他向她展示了如何接吻，依据的是1271年威尼斯发展出的最高艺术水平。这在如今是行不通的，不是那种撅嘴的动作。但无论如何，这对推动剧情来说是重磅炸弹，谢天谢地。啊，现任职的邪恶大臣艾哈迈德发现了此事，并影响汗王派遣马可执行一项有去无回的任务。果然，马可和宾吉作为间谍被捕，被带到地方统治者海都（由留着黑人小辫子的费迪南德·戈特沙尔克饰演）面前，并被判处死刑。

且慢！海都的妻子（宾妮·巴恩斯饰）觉得马可很可爱，而海都因惧内而 gladly 饶恕了他，他的妻子不让他与女仆亲热，现在是他的机会！马可必须取悦海都的夫人，否则就被扔进油锅炸死！而他并不想这样做，各位，即使她是一位迷人的金发女郎。他想对库基（Kookie）保持忠诚！

与此同时，忽必烈汗出征征服日本，这与现代新闻兴趣 nicely 挂钩。一场台风在中国海域淹没了中国军队，艾哈迈德夺取王位，并告诉库基她是他的王后。

镜头切回马可。海都的妻子让他独处！她正爬到他身上，做着梅·韦斯特（Mae West）式的匍匐动作！她把他逼到角落，他无路可退，各位，他不想玷污他对库基的爱，但他也不想被深油炸熟。噢——他要放弃了，这个懦夫。他要背叛那个甜美小女孩的信任！但是等等——等等，各位，这是什么发展？万岁——海都的妻子只是想蹭鼻子！她高深莫测！马可终究不必对库基不忠了！

看啊，看啊，这是什么？一只信鹰在海都营地上空盘旋！他们将其射落，发现其腿上绑着一封信。信来自公主，但什么也没写。她有着女子精修学校的口音，但不会写字。上面只写着“公主，她的标记”，但内心是个双关语高手的马可知道这意味着信是给他的。不仅如此，他还知道这意味着她处于危险之中，速来。哦，戈德温先生，这太过分了。他怎么知道这不意味着“黄浦阿姨来吃晚饭，之后我们一起做了软糖”。

不管信上写的是什么，海都不让他走。他必须留下来和海都的妻子蹭鼻子。与此同时——闪回——汗王从战场归来，成了一个破碎的老人。淹没在中国海域的不是他，只是他的军队。而现在——现在，嘿嘿——他必须签署文件，将王国和女儿转让给艾哈迈德，否则秃鹫将被释放，去啄食被锁链束缚在邪恶喙下的可怜库基！

“老爹”能做什么？他签了字，

由 D.S. Pitts 制作。转呈者

《购物新闻》（SHOPPING NEWS）是一家美国机构，于1934年9月由国际代理公司（International Agencies, Inc.）负责人 Robert D. CHISHOLM 先生创立，是一份每周发行的广告报纸，其主要内容致力于刊登女性感兴趣的项目。

除了该出版物刊登的文章和广告材料外，还有一页或多页用于刊登简短段落或“简讯”，这些内容虽然具有幽默性质，但 invariably 具有诽谤性或丑闻性。

从所附注册表格中包含的细节可以看出，《购物新闻》被描述为在上海美国总领事馆注册。然而，调查显示事实并非如此；同样，国际代理公司也未在当地美国当局注册。

该报的编辑部位于南京路233号540室。

Chisholm，在上海熟称为“Don” Chisholm，是特别分部档案 D. 2310 的主题对象，该档案随函附上以供参考。另附《购物新闻》样本一份。

C. 18/11

D.C.（特别分部）。

（印：SMP 特别分部 1937年11月18日）

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE

Some 16 workers employed by the Russian Daily News submitted a demand on March 20 to the management for an increase of 50% in wages to those who earn $450.00 or more per month, and 60% to those who earn less than $450.00. Two of the workers representatives, namely Tong King Kung (唐金根) and Doong Wen Ping (董文炳), called at the office of the Division at 10 a.m. on March 22 requesting mediation. They stated that the workers employed by the Epoch Magazine Co., to which the Daily News is affiliated, were much better paid. A worker in the Epoch Magazine Co., could earn at least $580.00 per month, while the lowest wage in their own press was only $360.00. They were advised, as requested by the management, to negotiate direct with their employer first in order to maintain amicable relationship with their employer.

On April 12, the Section was informed by the workers that no settlement had so far been reached.

Mr. Serebrikoff, manager of the press, was interviewed in the Division Office on April 15 by appointment. He explained that the press had no connection whatsoever with the interests of the Epoch Magazine Co., and owing to poor business, the press could not afford to grant any increase on the workers wages.

Negotiations with the management were resumed on April 19. After mediation, the management agreed to effect 40% increase to those workers whose basic pay is above $250 per month, and to grant more substantial increase to those whose basic pay is below $250, but no increase is to be made on the rice allowance. The workers were satisfied, and the dispute was therefore settled.

(Henry Chiu)

劳资纠纷

《俄罗斯日报》雇用的约16名工人于3月20日向管理层提出要求，月薪在450.00美元或以上者加薪50%，月薪低于450.00美元者加薪60%。3月22日上午10时，两名工人代表，即唐金根（Tong King Kung）和董文炳（Doong Wen Ping），前往本分局办公室请求调解。他们表示，《俄罗斯日报》所属的《时代杂志公司》（Epoch Magazine Co.）雇员工资要高得多。《时代杂志公司》的一名工人每月至少可赚取580.00美元，而他们报社的最低工资仅为360.00美元。应管理层要求，建议他们先与雇主直接谈判，以维持与雇主的良好关系。

4月12日，工人们通知本股，迄今尚未达成和解。

4月15日，经预约，印刷厂经理Serebrikoff先生在本分局办公室接受了问询。他解释说，该印刷厂与《时代杂志公司》的利益没有任何关联，且由于生意不佳，印刷厂无力承担增加工人工资的费用。

4月19日，与管理层的谈判恢复。经调解，管理层同意给基本工资每月超过250美元的工人加薪40%，并给基本工资低于250美元的工人更大幅度的加薪，但米贴不予增加。工人们表示满意，因此纠纷得以解决。

(Henry Chiu)

SUBJECT: A Booklet Entitled "Sleepless Nights"

With reference to the attached letter from
Mr. V. Chilikin, the booklet in question is a
translation from a monthly magazine in the English
language "Far Eastern Review", No.8, 1941, which
has ceased publication since the outbreak of the
Pacific War in December 1941.

The booklet is entitled "Sleepless Nights" and
is written by Mitsudzira Sarizawa. It describes
the personal impression of a young Japanese, who
joined a special detachment of the Japanese Imperial
Army in 1937 and proceeded to Shanghai where he was
employed unloading war material from Japanese transports
on the Whangpoo River.

Nothing objectionable was found in this booklet.

K. S. Alyoji

主题：一本名为《不眠之夜》的小册子

参照附呈的V. Chilikin先生的来信，有关小册子系译自英文月刊《远东评论》（Far Eastern Review）1941年第8期，该杂志自1941年12月太平洋战争爆发以来已停刊。

该小册子题为《不眠之夜》，作者为Mitsudzira Sarizawa。书中描述了一名年轻日本人的个人印象，他于1937年加入日本帝国陆军的一个特别分队，随后前往上海，受雇在黄浦江上从日本运输船上卸载军用物资。

在该小册子中未发现任何不妥之处。

SUBJECT: Letter from Mr. Chilikin, the editor of

Reference to the attached letter of Mr. V. Chilikin,
re a bomb attack which is being planned on the "Russian
Daily News" premises situated at 615-622 Avenue Foch,
enquiries indicated the following:-

Mr. V. Chilikin was communicated with by telephone
and stated that the Russian who had furnished the infor-
mation named himself as Kirichko. The Complainant
described the man as follows:- age about 40, oval face,
clean shaven, pale complexion, slim built, about 5'8" in
height, wearing an old Khaki watchman's uniform. The
man stated he was unemployed at present, and formerly
worked as a private watchman with the China Printing and
Finishing Company, and that he was living in the
Salvation Army's shelters. He requested the complainant
some money for information, and was told by the former
to see him at 3 p.m. on the same date, but failed to
come. The Salvation Army's Shelter was communicated
with, but nothing was known there about the above
described man. The China Printing and finishing Co.,
however, replied that they had in their company a private
watchman named Kirichko, but the man in question
terminated his service about 4 months ago, and nothing
was known regarding his present whereabouts. Sub-Inspr.
Kourjansky, i/c of Russian Watchmen's Section, Police
Headquarters, was also communicated with, but no such a
person was registered in the said office.

Mr. Chilikin when interviewed stated that he is of
the opinion that this was not a genuine case, but a mere
attempt to gain some "easy money". In view of the
fact that the reward was not paid at the spot, the
informer was afraid to call again at 3 p.m., thinking
that the complainant might have informed the police.
It should also be mentioned that Mr. Chilikin
formerly had numerous complaints of similar nature made
to Chengtu Road Station, and was usually provided with
a C.P.C. at the entrance to the Newspaper office, 620
Avenue Foch. As soon as C.P.C. was being withdrawn by
Officer i/c of the Station, after an interval of two to
three weeks, another complaint was usually reported such
as intimidation by telephone, suspicious visitors etc.
It should also be recalled that Mr. Chilikin recently
applied for the renewal of a licence to carry firearms,
which was refused, and apparently is now trying his best
to show the Police the extreme necessity to carry a
pistol.

STATEMENT

ON OCTOBER 4TH AN UNKNOWN TO ME RUSSIAN MALE CAME INTO MY
OFFICE ASKING FOR A JOB. ON BEING QUESTIONED ABOUT HIS FORMER EM-
PLOYMENT, HE REVEALED THAT HE WORKED AS A WATCHMAN IN HONGKEW FOR
LUN CHONG'S (CHINA PRINTING AND FINISHING COMPANY). HIS REFERENCES
GAVE HIS NAME AS KIRKITCH OR KIRKOSH LIVING IN THE SALVATION
ARMY.

HE ASKED FOR THE PROPRIETOR AND WHEN I TOLD HIM IT WAS I,
HE ASKED ME HOW MUCH I WOULD PAY FOR INTERESTING INFORMATION. ON BEING
TOLD THAT IT WOULD DEPEND ON HOW TRUE HIS STATEMENT WOULD BE,
HE TOLD ME THAT A BOMB ATTACK IS BEING PLANNED ON OUR NEWSPAPER.
HE TOLD ME THAT TODAY (SUNDAY) A MEETING IS BEING HELD AT TRETIA-
KOFF'S IN HONGKEW AT WHICH IT WILL BE DECIDED WHO WILL THROW THE
BOMB AND WHEN.

I ASKED THE MAN TO COME AND SEE ME AT THREE O'CLOCK BUT HE
DID NOT COME.

陈述书

10月4日，一名我不认识的俄罗斯男子进入我的办公室求职。当被问及以前的工作经历时，他透露曾在虹口为伦昌（中国印刷整理公司）担任守夜人。他的推荐信显示其姓名为KIRKITCH或KIRKOSH，居住在救世军。

他要求见业主，当我告诉他我就是业主时，他问我愿意为有趣的情报支付多少钱。当被告知这将取决于他的陈述有多真实时，他告诉我有人正策划对我们的报社进行炸弹袭击。他告诉我，今天（星期日）在虹口的TRETIAKOFF处正在举行会议，会上将决定由谁投掷炸弹以及何时投掷。

我让该男子三点钟来见我，但他没有来。

Station Censorship Office, Sp. Branch No. Date 15-9-43.

SUBJECT: "Glory to Russian Country and her defender glorious Red Army", a pamphlet by V. Jiganoff, published by newspaper "Daily News".

The following information can be furnished regarding the subject:-

On the 1-9-43, the editor of the Daily News, Mr. Chilikin, sent to this Office proofs of an article written by V. Jiganoff and entitled "Glory to Russian Country and her defender glorious Red Army", for the preliminary censorship.

This was usual practice of the editor to send articles or cuttings from Moscow papers for preliminary censorship. The undersigned complied with the request of the editor and the proofs were returned. Later the editor informed the undersigned that the proofs of the said article would be sent in usual manner in three copies for final approval and then to be published in his paper. Lately, two days ago, it was found out that the above mentioned article was published in Russian unofficially as a pamphlet and sold for $2.00 a copy in the 8th Administrative District, contrary to the existing Press regulations.

The contents of the pamphlet can be summarized as follows:-

The author exposes the split existing amongst the Russians in Shanghai over current war events in which Russia is actually involved.

The author states that he is unable to understand those Russians, who are of pro-German attitude and calls them poor defeatists. At the same time he insists that according to his knowledge, the majority of Russians

主题：V. Jiganoff（音译）所著、由《每日新闻》报出版的小册子《荣耀归于俄罗斯及其光荣的捍卫者红军》。

关于上述主题，可提供如下信息：

1943年9月1日，《每日新闻》编辑 Chilikin 先生（音译）将 V. Jiganoff（音译）撰写的一篇题为《荣耀归于俄罗斯及其光荣的捍卫者红军》的文章校样送交本办公室进行预审。

该编辑通常会将文章或从莫斯科报纸上剪下的资料送交预审。签署人应编辑之请求办理了此事，并将校样退回。随后，编辑通知签署人，该文章的校样将按惯例一式三份送来以供最终批准，然后在其报纸上发表。最近，即两天前，发现上述文章以俄语非正式地作为小册子出版，并在第八行政区以每本2.00美元的价格出售，此举违反了现行的新闻法规。

该小册子的内容可概括如下：

作者揭露了在上海的俄罗斯人之间因俄罗斯实际卷入的当前战争事件而存在的分裂。

作者表示，他无法理解那些持亲德态度的俄罗斯人，并称他们为可怜的失败主义者。同时，他坚持认为，据他所知，大多数俄罗斯人

在本科接受审查之物系作为小册子发售者，故认为如此分配
若在本局管辖区内发现有售卖之事实，则予以没收为宜。

SUBJECT: Meeting of the Association of Central European Attorneys-at-Law in Shanghai

1. Time and Date of meeting: 7.30 p.m. to 9 p.m. 22-4-43
2. Place: 416/22 Tongshan Rd Jewish Gemeinde premises
3. Nature of meeting: ordinary meeting of members
4. Responsible person; Dr. R. B. Michaelis, chairman, 1074 B'well Rd.
5. Object: to discuss current matters
6. Number of persons attending: 13
7. Agenda: Discussion of matters of interest to lawyers with regard to the Proclamation of Febr. 18th
8. Enquiry and comment:

Before the discussion was opened, Dr. Leidert, the Hon. secretary, who had been asked by Dr. Michaelis to preside over the meeting, welcomed the persons attending and read out the minutes of the last meeting.

Dr. Leidert then read a letter which had been received from the S.A.C.R.A. in answer to the Associations query concerning applications for permits for lawyers. The S.A.C.R.A. letter said that applications should be made individually and not through the Association. Thereafter the date for the next meeting was fixed for May 10th, 1943. The discussion was then opened and the following points were mentioned:

1. S.M.C. prosecutions for selling houses at prices exceeding the actual value of fixtures and furniture and charging of rent higher than permitted by the S.M.C. It was stated that lately there had been but few prosecutions but one case was cited where the chief tenant was fined 1.900,- by the S.M.C. for charging excessive rent only one month ago.

2. The S.A.C.R.A. now actively promoting the exchange of residences. It was said that the S.A.C.R.A. is in possession of lists of Japanese residing in the designated area who are willing to exchange their residences. These addresses are given to stateless refugees who can go there and begin negotiations.

3. The next point discussed was the question of stateless refugees owning property outside the designated area after May 18th, 1943. Particularly the question whether or not stateless refugees will be able to remain lessees of houses outside the designated area. According to the opinion of several lawyers present, the leasehold of premises and the subsequent subletting at fixed rents does not constitute a business and it might therefore be possible to continue the lease. On the other hand one case was mentioned where the realty owning company had demanded from the lessee that he brings the consent of the Muirhead Rd Office before they would renew his contract.

4. The status of the Aryan wife married to a non-aryan stateless refugee now who wants to be divorced. The question arises that she may divorced and recognized as German by the German authorities yet if such

3. 会议性质：会员常规会议
4. 负责人：R. B. Michaelis 博士，主席，地址：百老汇路1074号。
5. 目的：讨论当前事项
6. 出席人数：13人
7. 议程：讨论律师界关注的有关2月18日公告的事项
8. 查询与评论：

在讨论开始之前，受 Michaelis 博士委托主持会议的荣誉秘书 Leidert 博士（音译）欢迎了与会人员，并宣读了上次会议的纪要。

随后，Leidert 博士宣读了一封来自 S.A.C.R.A.（音译）的回信，答复了该协会关于律师许可证申请的咨询。S.A.C.R.A. 的信中表示，申请应个人单独提出，而非通过协会提出。此后，确定下次会议日期为1943年5月10日。随后展开讨论，提及了以下几点：

1. 工部局对以超过固定装置和家具实际价值的价格出售房屋以及收取高于工部局允许租金的行为提起诉讼。据称，最近此类诉讼很少，但举出一个案例，即首席承租人仅在一个月前就因收取过高租金被工部局罚款1,900元。

2. S.A.C.R.A. 目前正积极促进住房交换。据悉，S.A.C.R.A. 掌握着居住在指定区域内的日本人名单，这些人愿意交换住房。这些地址提供给无国籍难民，他们可以前往那里并开始谈判。

3. 接下来讨论的问题是1943年5月18日之后无国籍难民在指定区域外拥有财产的问题。特别是无国籍难民是否能够继续作为指定区域外房屋的承租人的问题。根据在场几位律师的意见，房屋租赁及随后以固定租金转租不构成商业行为，因此可能可以继续租赁。另一方面，提到一个案例，其中房地产拥有公司要求承租人在续签合同前获得缪尔黑德路办公室的同意。

4. 嫁给非雅利安无国籍难民的雅利安妻子目前的身份，她现在希望离婚。出现的问题是，她可能会离婚并被德国当局承认为德国人，但如果这样的

5. Actual cases of the exchange of houses and
the practices followed. The obligation of the chief-
tenant to accomodate as many of his old subtenants as
possible.

Comment
The above mentioned points which were discuss-
ed during the above meeting are of particular interest
to lawyers because their clients expect them to know
the answers to all these questions. In order to safe-
guard their clients from infringing the regulations
of the Proclamation and also in order to upkeep the
reputation of the lawyer's profession they are exchang-
ing their experiences with actual cases. in this manner
they believe to obtain the best conception of the way
in which the Authorities want the Proclamation to be
carried out. From point 8/3 it appears that some doubt
exists in refugee circles regarding the retention of
property outside the designated area after May 18th .
The Proclamation mentions "residences and businesses"
but not "property" and this is probably the reason why
this point was mentioned. The lawyers' interest in
housing matters is also due to the fact that some of
them have not found lodgings yet inside the area. Those
who have done so were very much envied by their colle-
gues because May 18th draws closer and closer and the
finding of quarters has remained very difficult.

D. J. Ullaci

O i/c Foreign Affairs Section
C & S Branch

评论
上述会议上讨论的上述几点
对律师特别感兴趣，因为他们的客户期望
他们知道所有这些问题的答案。为了保护
他们的客户不违反公告的规定，同时也为了
维护律师职业的声誉，他们正在交流
实际案例的经验。他们认为通过这种方式
可以最好地理解当局希望如何执行
公告。从第8/3点来看，难民圈中对5月18日
之后保留指定区域外的财产存在某些疑虑。
公告提及“住所和商业”，但未提及“财产”，
这可能是提及这一点的原因。律师对住房
 matters 的兴趣也源于以下事实：他们中的一些人
尚未在区域内找到住处。那些已经找到住处的人
受到了同事们的极大羡慕，因为5月18日越来越近，
而寻找住所仍然非常困难。

Further to the attached file and acting on instructions
of the D. C. (Special Branch) appended thereon, Mr. Fang Fu-an
(房福安), editor of the China News and Views Digest, Apartment
32, No.176 Route Dufour, French Concession, was given a

University, Peiping. He came to Shanghai about eight years ago.

SPECIAL BRANCH）

Reference the attached letter on the subject of
the "China News and Views Digest" written by Mr. Fang
Fu An, it has been learned that this concern was
established on September 22, 1936, at 504 Avenue du Roi
Albert, French Concession by Mr. Fang Fu An, proprietor,
with Mr. Cecil Frank Glass, British South African subject
as editor. Registration with the French Police, of this
translation and news service, was effected on October 9,
1936, since which time a daily news service has been
operated by the concern, a copy of the news and translation
manuscript being regularly supplied to the Political Section,
French Police.

Mr. Fang Fu An is not known to have any strong
political leanings but Mr. C.F. Glass was known to
entertain Communist (Trotsky clique) sympathies
(Vide File D.2771 (S.B.)). The latter person left
Shanghai for New York on April 18, 1937 in possession
of an U.S.A. Non-immigration visa No.434. He is believed
to be still in U.S.A. and is stated to have obtained an
extention to his visa which will permit of his remaining
in U.S.A. a further six months.

Mr. Fang Fu An is well known to newspaper editors
and the managers of major news agencies locally. His
translation and news service is reputed to be fairly
good while he is described as being smart in appearance
and very 'cock-sure'.

（批：S.I.

2/4）

D. S. I. Logan
C. B.

CHINA NEWS AND VIEWS DIGEST
April 1, 1938.

CHINESE ATTACK WESTERN SUBURB OF TSINAN.
--
JAPANESE SUFFER HEAVY CASUALTIES IN SHANTUNG DRIVE
HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---In an enveloping attack on the western
suburb of Tsinan, the capital of Shantung, a mobile column operating
in the right wing of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway yesterday succeeded
in wiping out more than 200 Japanese troops stationed there,
according to military advices just received here.
Severe fighting was raging north of Taierchwang, the terminus
of the Tsinpu Railway spur line, last night, when Japanese troops
launched a pincer movement to cut the rear of the Japanese. Over 2000
Japanese are reported to have killed during the engagement.
Meanwhile, the Chinese forces are attacking the Japanese
positions at Yihhsien northwest of Taierchwang, in two routes.
The Japanese units north of the city are reported to have already
been surrounded by the Chinese defenders, who are now outside the
city walls.
At Linchen sector the both forces are still facing each other,
but communications between Linchen and Hanchwang have been
interrupted by the Chinese.
Japanese troops operating on both banks of the Yi River, north
of Lingyi are reported to have been completely routed by the Chinese
who have crossed the Yichi in hot pursuit of the retreating Japanese
forces.-- Morning Edition of Ta Mei Wan Pao, April 1.
-- -- --
IMPORTANT SHANSI TOWNS RECOVERED
LOYANG, Mar. 31.--Hohsien and Chaochen, important town on the
Tungou Railway, have been recaptured by Chinese forces operating in
southern Shansi, according to a military report reaching here today.
Severe fighting is stated to be in progress at Hungtung, south
of Chaochen.--Morning Edition of Ta Mei Wan Pao, April 1.
-- -- --

1938年4月1日。

中国军队进攻济南西郊。
--
日军在山东攻势中遭受重大伤亡
徐州，3月31日电。---据此处刚收到的军事消息，昨日在津浦铁路右翼作战的一支机动纵队，对山东省会济南西郊实施包围攻击，成功歼灭驻守该地的200多名日军。
昨晚，津浦铁路支线终点站台儿庄以北激战正酣，当时日军发动钳形攻势以切断其后路。据报道，在此次交战中有超过2000名日军被杀。
与此同时，中国军队正分两路进攻台儿庄西北的义县日军阵地。据报道，城以北的日军部队已被中国守军包围，后者目前位于城墙之外。
在林城地区，双方仍处于对峙状态，但林城与韩庄之间的通讯已被中国军队切断。
据报道，在临沂以北沂河两岸作战的日军已被中国军队彻底击溃，中国军队已渡过沂河，猛烈追击撤退的日军。--《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。
-- -- --
山西重要城镇收复
洛阳，3月31日电。--据今日到达此处的军事报告称，在晋南作战的中国军队已收复同蒲铁路上的重要城镇霍县和赵城。
据悉，赵城以南的洪洞地区正在进行激烈战斗。--《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。
-- -- --

April 1, 1938.    Chinese News --2

FIGHTING AT TAIECHWANG REACHES TEMPORARY END

    HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---After a sanguinary combat started on the
night of Mar. 30, military operations at the Taierchwang sector are
considered to have reached a temporary conclusion.
    Japanese troops operating on the northwest of Taierchwang are
stated to have been completely annihilated, while the fate of their
remnants now hiding out in the outskirts of the town are doomed,
as the Chinese forces are now engaged in "mopping" operations.
    Meanwhile, gunfire is no longer audible Taierchwang and its
environs. The total of Japanese casualties during the battle of
Taierchwang is said to have exceeded 1000. Many Japanese have taken
prisoner, and the booty included 17 tanks. --Hua Mei Wan Pao
Morning Edition, April 1.

-- -- --

ANOTHER TOWN IN SHANTUNG RECAPTURED

    HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---Japanese troops operating around Tsining,
south of Chufu in southern Shantung, have recaptured Changhokou,
states a brief message reaching here from the front. No details are
yet available.--Morning Edition of Ta Mei Wan Pao, April 1.

-- -- --

ANTI-AIR RAID "TUNNEL" PLANNED IN CHUNGKING

    CHUNGKING, Mar. 31.---A million dollar anti-air raid "tunnel"
is being planned here by local residents. Half of the fund required
for the construction purpose is said to have been subscribed
by local gentry and business leaders, while the remaining portion
is to be subsided by the government.---Morning edition of Ta Mei
Wan Pao, April 1.

-- -- --
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。    中国新闻 --2

台儿庄战斗暂时结束

    徐州，3月31日电。---经过3月30日晚开始的惨烈战斗后，台儿庄地区的军事行动被认为已暂时结束。
    据悉，在台儿庄西北作战的日军已被彻底歼灭，而目前躲藏在城镇郊区的残部命运已定，因为中国军队正在进行“扫荡”行动。
    与此同时，台儿庄及其周边地区已听不到枪声。据说台儿庄战役中日军的伤亡总数已超过1000人。许多日军被俘，战利品包括17辆坦克。 --《华美晚报》4月1日晨版。

-- -- --

山东又一城镇被收复

    徐州，3月31日电。---据从前线到达此处的简短消息称，在鲁南曲阜以南的济宁地区作战的日军已重新占领长沟口。目前尚无详细细节。--《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。

-- -- --

重庆计划修建防空“隧道”

    重庆，3月31日电。---当地居民正在此处规划一项价值百万美元的防空“隧道”。据悉，建设所需资金的一半已由当地士绅和商业领袖认购，其余部分将由政府补贴。---《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。

-- -- --

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938.    Chinese News - 3

CHINESE DESTROY COMMUNICATION LINES NEAR TAIAN

HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---Reports from Chinese sources state that
Chinese troops operating at T-wenkou, south of Taian on the Tsinpu
Line, crossed the Wen river on Mar. 29 and succeeded in destroying
two bridges and about 700 meters of the railway tracks northeast
of Taian.---Morning Edition of Ta Mei Wan Pao, April 1.

JAPANESE RETREATING TOWARD LAI TsO

HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---Hotly pursued by Chinese forces, Japanese
troops stationed northwest of Lingyi, strategic town in southeastern
Shantung, are now retreating toward Lai tso.---Morning Edition of
Ta Mei Wan Pao, April 1.

1,000 JAPANESE SOLDIERS KILLED BY BIG SWORDS

HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---Over 1,000 out of 5,000 Japanese soldiers
from Yihhsien were killed by hand grenades and big swords on
Tuesday when they launched a second attack against the Chinese
forces at Taierhchwang, north of Hsuchow, according to belated
reports reaching here.

Following Serious hand-to-hand fighting at the western and
northwestern outskirts of Taierhchwang city, according to the reports,
the Japanese suffered heavy losses. A Chinese soldier named
Ho Tze-hou killed thirteen Japanese soldiers by his big sword,
another soldier by the name of Wang Chia-shang killed nine, Chang
Shao-min killed five while the others killed an average of one and
half.

Yesterday the Chinese troops captured Sanlichuan, Pangchiao and
Nanpao, outside of Taierhchwang, while the Japanese troops retreated
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。    中国新闻 - 3

中国军队破坏泰安附近的通讯线路

徐州，3月31日电。---据中方消息来源报道，在津浦线上泰安以南的T-wenkou（音译）作战的中国军队于3月29日渡过汶河，成功破坏了泰安东北的两座桥梁和约700米的铁轨。---《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。

日军向莱佐（Lai Tso，音译）撤退

徐州，3月31日电。---在中国军队的猛烈追击下，驻扎在鲁东南战略重镇临沂西北的日军正向莱佐（Lai tso，音译）撤退。---《大美晚报》4月1日晨版。

1000名日本士兵死于大刀之下

徐州，3月31日电。---据此处收到的迟报称，周二，来自义县的5000名日军中的1000多人在对徐州以北台儿庄的中国军队发动第二次进攻时，死于手榴弹和大刀之下。

据报道，在台儿庄城西和西北郊区的激烈肉搏战后，日军遭受重创。一名名叫何子厚（Ho Tze-hou，音译）的中国士兵用大刀杀死了13名日本士兵，另一名名叫王嘉尚（Wang Chia-shang，音译）的士兵杀死了9人，张绍民（Chang Shao-min，音译）杀死了5人，其他人平均每人杀死1.5人。

昨天，中国军队占领了台儿庄外的三里川、庞桥和南堡，而日军撤退

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938.    Chinese News - 4

to the east of the railway line.--Ta Mei Wan Pao, March 31.

** ** **

JAPANESE AMMUNITION STORED AT HSINHSIANG
CHENGCHOW, Mar. 31.---Hsinhsiang, important railway town
on the Peiping-Hankow line, is reported to be one of the important
depots of the Japanese troops, where large quantities of foodstuffs
as well as ammunition are stored.
About 2,000 Japanese soldiers are stationed there where
strong defence works have been built both near the airdrome and at
the railway station to stop any Chinese attack.--Ta Mei Wan Pao,
March 31.

** ** **

SPECIAL TAX ON NATIVE PRODUCTS FROM JAPANESE OCCUPIED AREAS TO
BE COLLECTED

HONGKONG, Mar: 31.---In an attempt to stop the Japanese from
absorbing the Chinese legal tender notes from the interior, the
Kwangtung Provincial Government has decided to collect special
taxes on imports of native products produced in the various
areas now occupied by the Japanese troops.
Pear from Tientsin, soy-beans from Manchuria and wine from
Linfeng and other products will have to pay special import taxes
beginning from April 1.--Ta Mei Wan Pao, March 31.

** ** **

KWANGTUNG BOMBED BY JAPANESE PLANES;
GERMAN CONSULATE-GENERAL BOMBED IN HAINAN

CANTON, Mar. 31.---A fleet of 28 Japanese planes in seven
squadrons bombed Pakong, Yingtak, and other cities along the Canton-
Hankow Railway line today. Over 20 bombs were dropped from these
planes.
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。    中国新闻 - 4

至铁路线以东。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

** ** **

日军弹药储存在新乡
郑州，3月31日电。---据报道，平汉铁路上的重要铁路城镇新乡是日军的重要仓库之一，那里储存着大量的食品以及弹药。
约有2000名日军驻扎在那里，并在机场附近和火车站建立了坚固的防御工事，以阻止任何中国军队的攻击。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

** ** **

将对来自日军占领区的土特产征收特别税

香港，3月31日电。---为了阻止日本人吸收内地的中国法币，广东省政府决定对目前被日军占领的各个地区生产的土特产进口征收特别税。
从4月1日开始，天津的梨、满洲的大豆以及临丰（Linfeng，音译）的酒和其他产品必须缴纳特别进口税。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

** ** **

广东遭日机轰炸；
海南德国总领事馆被炸

广州，3月31日电。---今天，由七个中队组成的28架日机编队轰炸了广汉铁路沿线的琶岗（Pakong，音译）、英德和其他城市。这些飞机投下了20多枚炸弹。

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938.    Chinese News - 5

At Whampoa and Shihto near Canton, the Japanese planes
dropped over ten bombs. Little damage was done to the Chinese
positions.
    When staging an aerial raid over Haikow on Hainan Island
yesterday, four Japanese planes dropped a number of bombs hitting
directly the former German Consulate-General. The building was
completely destroyed. One Japanese warship is now anchored off
Haikow.--The Life Daily News, April 1.
                        ***
CHINESE PLANES ACTIVE OVER YIHSIEN
    HANKOW, Mar. 31.---Chinese planes are reported to be very
active in South Shantung, and that 40 Chinese planes subjected
Yihsien, northwest of Taierhchwang and northeast of Hanchwang,
to a series of terrific bombing today.--The Life Daily News, Apr. 1.
                        ***
VOLUNTEERS ACTIVE IN MANCHURIA
    HSUCHOW, Mar. 31.---Over 70 per cent of the Japanese troops in
the northeastern provinces have been sent to North China and serious
anxiety is felt by the authorities there because of the growing
activities of the anti-Japanese volunteers.
    In an attempt to suppress these volunteers, new troops are
being trained by the Japanese in the area.
    In view of this situation, despite the defeats of the Japanese
troops on the northern sector of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway front,
no Japanese reinforcement has been sent south from Manchuria since
March 21. -- Hwa Mei Wan Pao, Morning Edition, April 1.
                        ***
CHEN CHI-TANG TO BE APPOINTED CHAIRMAN OF FUKIEN
    HONGKONG, Mar. 31.---General Chen Chi-tang, former Commander of
Kwangtung troops, will soon be appointed Chairman of the Fukien
Provincial Government, to succeed Mr. Chen Yi, according to well-
informed circles.
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。    中国新闻 - 5

在广州附近的黄埔和石角（Shihto，音译），日机投下了十多枚炸弹。中国阵地受损轻微。
    昨天在海南岛海口上空进行空袭时，四架日机投下数枚炸弹，直接击中前德国总领事馆。该建筑被完全摧毁。一艘日本军舰目前停泊在海口外海。--《立报》，4月1日。
                        ***
中国飞机在义县上空活跃
    汉口，3月31日电。---据报道，中国飞机在鲁南非常活跃，今天40架中国飞机对台儿庄西北、韩庄东北的义县进行了一系列猛烈轰炸。--《立报》，4月1日。
                        ***
义勇军在满洲活动频繁
    徐州，3月31日电。---东北省份超过70%的日军已被派往华北，由于反日义勇军活动日益增多，当地当局感到严重焦虑。
    为了镇压这些义勇军，日军正在该地区训练新部队。
    鉴于这种情况，尽管日军在津浦铁路前线北段遭遇失败，但自3月21日以来，没有日军增援部队从满洲南下。 -- 《华美晚报》4月1日晨版。
                        ***
陈济棠将被任命为福建省主席
    香港，3月31日电。---据消息灵通人士称，前粤军司令陈济棠将军将很快被任命为福建省政府主席，接替陈仪先生。

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938. Chinese News - 6

This action will be taken by the Central authorities because of
the importance of Fukien in the entire scheme of national defence.
Fukien is particularly important from the military point of view
because of its geographical position.

It may be recalled that General Chen who returned recently from
an extensive investigation tour in Europe, has contributed $7,000,000
to the war-chest.--Shanghai Daily News, April 1.
***

INTERNATIONAL FINANCIAL SYNDICATE TO BE ORGANIZED?

SHANGHAI, -- Well-informed circles state that an international
financial syndicate will be organized in Shanghai in the near future,
because of the financial instability in the city.

The syndicate will have control of cash reserves as well as
foreign exchange of the National Government and will make use of the
large quantities of silver now stored in America.

The visit of the British financial adviser attached to the British
Embassy here to Japan is to sound out the opinion of the Japanese
authorities regarding this matter.--Shanghai Daily News, April 1.
***

CHINESE IN AMERICA CONTRIBUTE US$400,000 FOR PURCHASE
OF AIRPLANES

HONGKONG, Mar. 31.---Six Chinese fliers returned here from America
and another 30 will return next month to join the Chinese air force.

The six fliers including Messrs. Chen Zuo-kwang and Kwong Shun-
hsiang, declared that Chinese in America have contributed US$400,000
for the purchase of airplanes for the Chinese air force.--
Ta Mei Wan Pao, March 31.
***
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。 中国新闻 - 6

中央当局采取这一行动是因为福建在整个国防计划中的重要性。从军事角度来看，福建因其地理位置而尤为重要。

值得一提的是，陈将军最近从欧洲广泛考察归来，已向战争基金捐款700万美元。--《上海日报》，4月1日。
***

将组建国际金融辛迪加？

上海，-- 消息灵通人士称，由于本市金融不稳定，不久将在上海组建一个国际金融辛迪加。

该辛迪加将控制国民政府的现金储备以及外汇，并将利用目前存储在美国的大量白银。

附属于英国驻华大使馆的英国财务顾问访问日本，旨在探询日本当局对此事的意见。--《上海日报》，4月1日。
***

在美华人捐款40万美元购买飞机

香港，3月31日电。---六名中国飞行员从美国返回此处，另有30人将于下月回国加入中国空军。

包括陈作光（Chen Zuo-kwang，音译）和邝顺祥（Kwong Shun-hsiang，音译）先生在内的六名飞行员宣布，在美华人已为中国空军购买飞机捐款40万美元。--
《大美晚报》，3月31日。
***

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938.    Chinese news - 7

SINO-BRITISH BOXER INDEMNITY COMMISSION GRANTS EDUCATIONAL SUBSIDIES

HANKOW, March 31 - The Sino-British Boxer Indemnity Fund Commission has decided to allot $500,000 as subsidies to the Provisional Universities at Sian and Changsha, it is learned from educational circles here today.
It has also been decided by the commission to grant $50,000 to the Medical College in Kweichow and $85,000 to the various universities in frontier provinces as a fund for professors. -- Wen Hui Pao, April 1.
* * * * *

CHINESE SOLDIERS BURNED TO DEATH BY JAPANESE DISGUISED AS FARMERS

KINGHWA, March 31 - Eight Chinese soldiers were recently burned to death at a village near Fuyang, south of Hangchow, by Japanese troops disguised as Chinese farmers, states a message from Chinese sources.
With a view to preventing possible attacks of Chinese guerillas, Nipponese troops now building defence works near Fuyang are stated to have resorted to the tactics of disguising themselves as Chinese farmers.
-- Wen Hui Pao, April 1.
* * * * *

JAPANESE RECEIVE ALLOTMENT OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE

SHANGHAI - If it is for legitimate purpose, even the Japanese will receive allotments of foreign exchanges from the Central Bank of China, according to well-informed banking circles.
The Japanese banks applied last week with the Central Bank of China a sum of £500,000 of foreign exchange and they were granted with £15,000.
It is generally believed that the Central Bank of China will allot more foreign exchange this week for Shanghai. The amount applied this week exceeds £2,000,000.
It may be recalled that £452,000 was allotted to Shanghai in the first week after the introduction of the new measures of control and £450,000 in the second week. -- China Evening News, March 31.
* * * * *
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日。    中文新闻 - 7

中英庚款委员会发放教育补助

汉口，3月31日——据本地教育界人士今日获悉，中英庚子赔款基金委员会已决定拨款50万美元，作为西安和长沙临时大学的补助金。
该委员会还决定向贵州医学院拨款5万美元，并向边疆各省的各大学拨款8.5万美元，作为教授基金。——《文汇报》，4月1日。
* * * * *

中国士兵被伪装成农民的日军烧死

金华，3月31日——据中方消息来源称，近日在杭州以南的富阳附近的一个村庄，八名中国士兵被伪装成中国农民的日军烧死。
据悉，为防止中国游击队可能发动的袭击，目前正在富阳附近修筑防御工事的日军采取了伪装成中国农民的战术。
——《文汇报》，4月1日。
* * * * *

日本人获得外汇配给

上海——据消息灵通的银行界人士称，如果是用于合法目的，即使是日本人也能从中国银行获得外汇配给。
日本各银行上周向中国银行申请了50万英镑的外汇，获准1.5万英镑。
人们普遍认为，中国银行本周将为上海配给更多外汇。本周申请的金额超过200万英镑。
回顾一下，在实施新的管制措施后的第一周，上海获配45.2万英镑，第二周获配45万英镑。——《China Evening News》（英文《中国晚报》），3月31日。
* * * * *

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938    Chinese News - C

VICE-MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS VISITS CANTON
CANTON, Mar. 31.---Mr. Lu I-so-fu, Vice-Minister of Communications, has arrived here to confer with the railway officials for the purpose of improving the regular freight traffic along the Canton-Kowloon and Canton-Hankow Railways.
Because of the large demand of rolling stocks for military purposes, large quantities of goods are stored in Canton without any chance of being transported to Hankow in the near future.
As a result of the discussions between Mr. Lu and the railway officials here, it is expected that more rolling stocks will be made available for the transportation of freight.--Ta Mei Wan Pao, Mar. 31.

***

KWANGSI TRAINS 5,000,000 SOLDIERS
CANTON, Mar. 31.---As many as 5,000,000 soldiers, including 1,000,000 women soldiers, will be trained by the authorities in Kwangsi Province.
Already, Kwangsi has trained 1,500,000 soldiers in five groups. The fifth group of soldiers, who just completed their training will not be dissolved according to instructions received by the Kwangsi authorities from Hankow. It is reported that this group will soon be sent to the front.--Ta Mei Wan Pao, March 31.

***

CHINESE MOBILE UNITS ACTIVE NEAR TSINGTAO
TIENSIN, Mar. 31.---Chinese mobile units attacked Anchiu, 80 miles northwest of Tsingtao on Monday, according to belated reports reaching here.
These mobile units engaged the Japanese in a series of fightings on Monday night and retreated the next day when large Japanese reinforcements were rushed to the region.
Many parts of the Tsinan-Xiaochow railway and the East Shantung Highway have been destroyed by the mobile units, disrupting greatly
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日    中文新闻 - C

交通部次长视察广州
广州，3月31日。---交通部次长卢作孚先生已抵达此地，与铁路官员会商，旨在改善广九铁路和粤汉铁路沿线的定期货运交通。
由于军事用途对机车车辆的需求量大，大量货物堆积在广州，近期无法运往汉口。
经过卢先生与本地铁路官员的讨论，预计将有更多的机车车辆用于货物运输。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

***

广西训练500万士兵
广州，3月31日。---广西当局将训练多达500万名士兵，其中包括100万名女兵。
目前，广西已分五批训练了150万名士兵。根据广西当局从汉口收到的指示，刚完成训练的第五批士兵将不予解散。据报道，这批士兵不久将被派往前线。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

***

中国机动部队在青岛附近活动
天津，3月31日。---根据迟至此处才收到的报道，中国机动部队于周一袭击了位于青岛西北80英里的安丘。
这些机动部队在周一晚间与日军进行了一系列战斗，次日当大批日军增援部队 rushed 至该地区时撤退。
机动部队破坏了津浦铁路（原文为Tsinan-Xiaochow railway，指济南-小段或相关路段，此处依原文直译或按当时语境理解，但通常指胶济线或周边，原文写Tsinan-Xiaochow，暂译为济南-小周铁路或保留原意，考虑到OCR可能有误，Tsinan即济南，Xiaochow可能是Zhoucun周村或Xuzhou徐州之误，但依规则不脑补，故直译）和山东东部公路的许多路段，严重扰乱了

April 1, 1938    Chinese News - 9

Japanese communication from Tsingtao to South Shantung, where serious
fighting is in progress.--China Evening News, March 31.
***

CANTON MAYOR CALLS ON H. H. KUNG
    CANTON, Mar. 31.--Mr. Tseng Yang-fu, Mayor of Canton and
concurrently Commissioner of Finance for Kwangtung, is visiting
Hankow, arriving there on March 26.
    In Hankow, Mr. Tseng is discussing with Dr. H.H. Kung, President
of the Executive Yuan and concurrently Minister of Finance, regarding
the financial situation in Kwangtung.
    Following the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities, according to
Mr. Tseng, little revenue has been realized in Kwangtung and deficit
of the province has increased to $8,000,000.
    Mr. Tseng is reporting also to Dr. Kung on the financial situation
in Kwangtung caused by the sharp increase of the value of Hongkong
notes in the past few days.--Ta Mei Wan Pao, March 31.
***
page_data.zh:
1938年4月1日    中文新闻 - 9

日军从青岛到鲁南的通讯，那里正在进行激烈的战斗。--《China Evening News》（英文《中国晚报》），3月31日。
***

广州市长拜访孔祥熙
    广州，3月31日。--广州市长兼广东省财政厅长曾养甫先生正在访问汉口，于3月26日抵达那里。
    在汉口，曾先生正与行政院院长兼财政部长孔祥熙博士讨论广东省的财政状况。
    据曾先生称，自中日敌对行动爆发以来，广东省收入甚微，该省赤字已增至800万美元。
    曾先生还向孔博士报告了过去几天港元币值急剧上涨造成的广东省财政状况。--《大美晚报》，3月31日。

TRANSLATIONS FROM JAPANESE NEWSPAPERS        April 1, 1938.

PEACE TALK RUMOURED AGAIN BY JAPANESE PRESS

    SHANGHAI - While the Sixth Kuomintang Congress is being held in
Chungking, serious disputes between the high Chinese military officers
and political officials are reported.

    The political science group, including General Chang Chun, vice-
President of the Executive Yuan, General Ho Ying-chin, Minister of
War, Mr. Wang Ching-wei, Chairman of the Central Political Council,
and Dr. H. H. Kung, President of the Executive Yuan and concurrently
Minister of Finance, are in favor of an early conclusion of the present
war. The other group including General Chen Chen, vice-Minister of
War, the Whampoa military officers and the Communists are insisting
on a protracted war with Japan.

    At present, it seems that the political science group in favor of
peace is gaining in strength and these people are of opinion that time
has come for the negotiating of peace with Japan.

    Among the peace terms, it is reported that China will recognize
the "Manchukuo" as well as the independence of Inner Mongolia. Indemnities
will also be paid by China. During the peace negotiations, no third
power intervention will be tolerated by the Japanese. -- Shanghai Nippo,
March 31.

                * * * * *
page_data.zh:
日文报纸译文        1938年4月1日。

日媒再次谣传和谈

    上海 - 据报道，当国民党第六次全国代表大会在重庆召开时，中国高级军事将领和政治官员之间发生了严重争执。

    包括行政院副院长张群将军、军政部长何应钦将军、中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生、行政院院长兼财政部长孔祥熙博士在内的“政学系”派别，主张尽早结束目前的战争。另一派别包括军政部次长陈诚将军、黄埔军校军官以及共产党人，坚持要与日本进行持久战。

    目前，主张和平的“政学系”似乎势力正在增强，这些人认为与日本进行和平谈判的时机已经到来。

    据报道，在和谈条件中，中国将承认“满洲国”以及内蒙古的独立。中国还将支付赔款。在和平谈判期间，日本不容忍任何第三国干预。 -- 《Shanghai Nippo》（《上海日报》），3月31日。

PRESS COMMENTS April 1, 1938

SHANGHAI CAPITALISTS SHOULD DEVELOP INTERIOR PROVINCES
(Wen Hui Pao, March 31 )

No country can,writes the Wen Hui Pao in an editorial this morning,
maintain its independence by sheer luck. At the present time of unpreceden-
ted crisis,it is all the more important to strengthen the foundations of
our nation.

As a result of the present hostilities, industry and commerce
in the port cities have been to a large extent destroyed. There is no
reason why Chinese industrialists and businessmen should cling to Shanghai
and refuse to leave for the interior.

Development of China's Northwest and Southwest are important
tasks. With vast natural resources, improved communications and stable
political conditions in the Southwest,special attention should be paid
to this region. This is the time for firm determination and a resolve
to undergo whatever hardships may be incurred in industrialising the
Southwest.For the developmentof industry, capital is needed. According
to investigations made by the Central Government, the Southwest is rich
in mineral as well as in agricultural products. Only capital is needed
to develop these resources. Having no other possibility of investing
their capital at the present time, it is the duty of Shanghai financiers
to assist the Government and to finance productive enterprises in the
Southwest.

Instead of investing in Shanghai in the past few years,
Chinese financiers should have invested in the southwestern provinces
for the development of industry,agriculture and mines. They should be
satisfied with a lower rate of interest and make it possible for farmers
and industrialists to make full use of the money under generous terms.
If loans are secured on machines ,farms or mines, there is no danger
whatsoever for the financiers to lose their money. Instead of investing
it individually, they would do far better to organise and to invest
collectively.
page_data.zh:
报刊评论 1938年4月1日

上海资本家应开发内地省份
（《文汇报》，3月31日）

《文汇报》在今早的一篇社论中写道，没有任何国家能单凭运气维持其独立。在目前前所未有的危机时刻，加强我们国家的基础尤为重要。

由于目前的敌对行动，港口城市的工商业在很大程度上遭到破坏。中国实业家和商人没有理由固守上海，拒绝前往内地。

开发中国西北和西南是重要的任务。西南地区拥有广阔的自然资源、改善的交通和稳定的政治局势，应特别关注该地区。现在是下定决心，决心承受工业化西南过程中可能产生的任何艰难困苦的时候了。为了发展工业，需要资本。根据中央政府的调查，西南地区矿产和农产品丰富。只需要资本来开发这些资源。由于目前没有其他投资资本的可能性，上海金融家有责任协助政府，并为西南地区的生产性企业提供资金。

中国金融家在过去几年里本应将资本投资于西南省份，以发展工业、农业和矿业，而不是投资于上海。他们应满足于较低的利率，并以优惠的条件使农民和实业家能够充分利用资金。如果贷款以机器、农场或矿山为抵押，金融家根本没有损失资金的危险。与其单独投资，他们不如组织起来集体投资会更好。

page_data.en:

    To develop the interior means developing China's lifeline. It is
the only chance for the financiers to revive their business. Financial
syndicates should be organized on scientific lines and investments should
be made only after examinations have been carried out by specialists
employed by these syndicates. It is to be hoped that scientific manage-
ment can be introduced and that, with the assistance of China's financiers
in Shanghai, our lifeline can be developed and our strength of resistance
increased, the paper concludes.

            * * * * *

        AMERICA'S FAR EASTERN POLICY
          (Ta Kung Pao, March 20)

    Commenting on America's policy in the Far East, Professor Chang
Chun-fu writes:
    "The United States of America, as the sponsor of the Washington
Conference of 1921, has contributed greatly toward the stabilization of
the general situation in the Far East for ten years. After the Mukden
Incident in September 18, 1931, the American Government wanted very
much to maintain both the letter and spirit of the Nine-Power Treaty,
but she was forced to adopt a laisser faire policy as Great Britain refused
to support her strong action. As a result all what the American Government
has done is to adhere to the policy of non-recognition of the changed
situation in East Asia created by force. President Roosevelt has continued
to pursue this policy on the one hand and concentrated his efforts to
build strong armies and navies on the other .
    "Over 90 per cent of the American people are sympathetic to China's
cause, but because of their bitter experiences in Europe during the World
War, they are eager to maintain peace by adopting the so-called isolationist
policy. They hope their Government will not involve herself in the Far
Eastern conflict.
    "In the past forty years, it must be noted, the United States of
America has paid more attention to the Far East than to Europe. During
this period, she has never been neutral in her dealings with the Far East.
Being one of the important powers in the Pacific, it is absolutely

    开发内地意味着开发中国的生命线。这是金融家复兴业务的唯一机会。应按科学方式组织金融辛迪加（财团），投资仅应在这些辛迪加聘用的专家进行检查后进行。本报总结道，希望能引入科学管理，并在上海金融家的帮助下，开发我们的生命线，增强我们的抵抗力量。

            * * * * *

        美国的远东政策
          （《大公报》，3月20日）

    张君劢教授在评论美国在远东的政策时写道：
    “作为1921年华盛顿会议的发起国，美利坚合众国为远东总体局势的稳定做出了巨大贡献，历时十年。在1931年9月18日沈阳事变之后，美国政府非常希望维护《九国公约》的字面和精神，但由于英国拒绝支持其强硬行动，它被迫采取放任政策。结果，美国政府所做的一切只是坚持不承认武力造成的东亚局势变化的政策。罗斯福总统一方面继续推行这一政策，另一方面集中精力建立强大的陆海军。
    “超过90%的美国人民同情中国的事业，但由于他们在世界大战期间在欧洲的痛苦经历，他们渴望通过采取所谓的孤立主义政策来维持和平。他们希望他们的政府不要卷入远东冲突。
    “必须指出，在过去四十年里，美利坚合众国对远东的关注多于对欧洲的关注。在此期间，她在处理远东事务时从未保持中立。作为太平洋的重要强国之一，美国绝对

page_data.en:
April 1, 1938. Comments - 5.
impossible for America to keep aloof from the developments on this coast
of the ocean. This situation is well realized by those Americans who are
well acquainted with the conditions in the Far East.
"Outwardly, it appears that there are in America two schools of
thought vis-a-vis the China situation. A closer examination of the
situation will, however, show us that both of the two schools of thought
are based on a common ground. That is both of them are sympathetic to
China's cause and hope that China will emerge victorious. The isolationists
want to avoid war at all costs. They would remain indifferent toward
whatever actions Japan may take in the future. The other group, who is
better acquainted with the situation in China, believes that it is their
duty to assist China, despite the possible danger of plunging their
country into a major war. It must also be pointed out that this school
is equally eager to maintain world peace.
"Theoretically speaking," Professor Chang continues, "the latter
school of thought will eventually triumph, because it has its convictions
that are derived from historical facts, while the former is based on
personal sentiments. The latter school is composed of historians,
statesmen and specialists, whereas the former is composed of men on the
street. Any change of American policy, however, depends upon the progress
of the Chinese armed resistance, the development of European events and
American internal problems.
"Personally," Professor Chang concludes, "I believe whatever America
may do, she will try to preserve peace both in America and in the Far
East. She will uphold righteousness and justice. It is yet not impossible
that America will find a way to achieve this aim in the near future."

CHINA NEWS AND VIEWS DIGEST
No. 811, April 20, 1939

TENSION GROWS IN CANTON AS CHINESE DRAW NEARER

HONGKONG, April 19 - The tension in Canton grows, as Chinese are rapidly closing in on the city, according to reports received here today.

Evacuation of Japanese forces from the city is reported to have begun. Japanese wounded soldiers and heavy pieces are being transported to places of safety along the Pearl River.

Troops under Generals Teng Lung-kwang and Li Cheng-chiu have reached the suburbs of Canton, where fierce fighting is in progress.

The Japanese are reported to be preparing for a desperate stand in Canton. Huge quantities of explosives and sulfur are being piled up in the business centers ready to set the city afire before they evacuate.

Meanwhile, strict precautions are being taken by the concession authorities in Shamen for preventing the entry of Japanese troops when they retreat in disorder.

Local observers believe that the recapture of Canton is only a matter of time. -- Wen Hui Pao, April 20.
* * *

GUERILLAS ACTIVE OUTSIDE GREAT WALL

HONGKONG, April 19 - Following a thorough reorganization under the direction of the central military authorities, Chinese volunteers operating outside the Great Wall have resumed their activities with added zest and renewed vigor, according to information from foreign sources.

On April 15, it is stated, the guerillas succeeded in cutting off the Tao-Ngang line on the border of Heilungkiang and Liaoning provinces in Manchuria and briefly occupied Ngang-ngang-chi in Heilungkiang. Traffic between Tsitsihar and Taonan is still under suspension.

Guerilla warfare is reported to be raging at various points on the South Manchurian, Chinese-Eastern and Peiping-Liaoning Railways.

It is further learned that with a view to making contacts with the volunteers, heavy Chinese regular forces are being dispatched to the Northeast. Large quantities of arms supplies are said to have been conveyed to the volunteers last month.

《中国新闻与观点文摘》
第811期，1939年4月20日

随着中国军队逼近，广州局势日益紧张

香港，4月19日——据今日在此收到的报道，随着中国军队迅速向该市逼近，广州的紧张局势日益加剧。

据报道，日军撤离该市行动已经开始。日本伤兵和重型装备正沿珠江被运往安全地带。

邓龙光将军和李成九将军麾下的部队已抵达广州郊区，激烈的战斗正在进行中。

据报道，日军正准备在广州作垂死挣扎。大量炸药和硫磺正堆积在商业中心，准备在撤离前放火焚烧城市。

与此同时，沙面租界当局正采取严格预防措施，以防止日军溃退时进入该地。

当地观察家认为，收复广州只是时间问题。——《文汇报》，4月20日。
* * *

长城以外游击队活动频繁

香港，4月19日——据来自外国方面的消息，在中央军事当局的指导下经过彻底重组后，在长城以外活动的中国义勇军以更加饱满的热情和 renewed vigor 恢复了活动。

据悉，4月15日，游击队成功切断了满洲黑龙江与辽宁边境的道昂线（Tao-Ngang line），并短暂占领了黑龙江的昂昂溪（Ngang-ngang-chi）。齐齐哈尔与洮南之间的交通仍处于中断状态。

据报道，南满铁路、中东铁路和平宁铁路沿线多处地点游击战正激烈进行。

另悉，为了与义勇军取得联系，中国正规军主力正被派往东北。据说上月已向义勇军运送了大量武器补给。
