No. 70. (501) DAILY WAR NEWS March 25, 1943

Nazi Attempts to Cross Donets River Foiled
SOUTH WESTERN FRONT, March 23. — The front of the Donets River bend, near Chuguyev, and the area south of it have been turned into a scene of sun-
German motorized infantry, supported by tanks, attempted to reach the river. The enemy's efforts to drive a wedge into the Soviet defence lines cost him very dearly.
The Red Army units frequently wrest the initiative from the enemy and hurl him back, despite the numerical superiority of the hitlerites. The fighting for a populated place which repeatedly changed hands was of especial violence. At first the Germans used the tactics of massed tank blows, but having sustained heavy losses from the Soviet artillery and anti-tank rifle fire they proceeded to act in smaller groups, consisting of 15 to 25 tanks.
The Soviet anti-tank riflemen, tankmen, the artillery and infantry everywhere meet the enemy with a hurricane fire, hurling him back to his initial lines. The other day the cavalrymen of our N unit distinguished themselves.
The Germans brought into action considerable numbers of tanks and about a regiment of infantry and attempted to pierce the Soviet defence line and to seize the river-crossing. After long artillery preparations several groups of German tanks rushed out towards the Soviet defence lines. Automatic riflemen rode on all tanks, while trucks with infantry followed at some distance behind. As a result of the Soviet artillery fire, and of the accurate shots of our anti-tank riflemen, the Germans lost 19 tanks and turned tail. The German infantrymen were unable to keep pace with the hurriedly retreating tanks, got stuck in the muddy road, and were overtaken there by the Soviet cavalrymen. Our mounted cavalrymen, with glittering sabers fell upon the Germans and cut their retreat. Not a single hitlerite escaped their punishing blades. Over an enemy infantry battalion was wiped out in the field amidst the motionless bodies of disabled German tanks.—(TASS.)

"Home Army" Formed in Holland
STOCKHOLM, March 23. — The formation in Holland of a "Home Defence Army" for the "defence of the country from enemies" was announced in Hague. This army will be subordinated to the Imperial SS Headquarters. All men from 18 to 50, possessing the required "morale" are to be drafted for service with this army. All R.C. soldiers, as the order emphasizes, must take an oath of allegiance to Hitler, which serves to confirm that the Dutchmen are actually called up to serve in the German armed forces.
Commenting on this order the "Deutsche Zeitung in Niederlanden" states, that the Dutchmen must assume certain tasks in the defence of the country, which hitherto were entrusted exclusively to the German occupation troops. At the same time, according to the newspaper, the new army is called upon to prevent anarchy in the country.—(TASS.)

Stalin Prizes Awarded to Scientific Workers
MOSCOW, March 24. — The decisions of the Council of the People's Commissars of USSR have been made public regarding the awards of Stalin Prizes for outstanding scientific achievements,
for radical improvements in technology and industrial production, made in 1942.
The first prizes, of 200,000 rubles each, in physics and mathematics have been awarded to Pavel Alexandrov, correspondent member of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR, for scientific studies in mathematics, published in 1941-1942, and to the member of the Academy of Sciences, Peter Kapitsa, for the discovery and study of the superfluidity of liquid helium.
In the field of technical sciences, the first prizes were awarded to Leonid Leibenzon, correspondent member of the Academy, for his studies of the theory of elasticity and of oil industry mechanics, and to member of the Academy Mikhail Pavlov, for his well-known works on the technology of pig-iron smelting.
In the chemical sciences the first prize was awarded to Alexander Nesmeyanov, correspondent member of the Academy, for his studies of metal-organic combinations.
In geology and geography, the first prizes were awarded to Feodosiy Krasovsky, correspondent member of the Academy, for his scientific work entitled "High Geodesy" and to member of the Academy Vladimir Obruchev, for geological explorations of the Donets Basin area, summed up in his book "The Geology of the USSR."
In biological sciences first prizes were awarded to Peter Zhukovsky, member of the All-Union Lenin Academy of Agricultural Sciences, for his work "Botany" and for the discovery of new varieties of wheat and rye, and for developing of hybrids by crossing plants of high economic value, to Vladimir Engelgardt, professor of the Institute of Biochemistry under the Academy of Sciences of the USSR, and to Militza Liubimova, staff member of the same institute, for studies of the muscular system.
In agricultural sciences the first prizes were awarded to member of the Academy Trofim Lysenko, Vassily Mossolov, member of the All-Union Lenin Agricultural Academy, and to a group of scientific workers, for the scientific development and introduction in the agriculture of the method of using tops of potatoes for plantings.
In the medical sciences the first prizes were awarded to Lieutenant-General of the Medical Service Prof. Victor Sheitunenko, and to Professors of the Military Medical Academy, Alexei Maxim-
menkov and Andrei Vishnevsky, for their scientific work "An Atlas of the Nervous and Venous Systems."
In the military sciences, second prizes of 100,000 rubles each were awarded to Professor Leonid Goncharov, for his scientific work "The Use of Artillery in Action", to Lieutenant-General, Professor Nikolai Drozdov, for the development of methods of designing guns, and for studies in the field of ballistics.
In historical and philologic sciences the first prizes were awarded to Isaak Mintz, correspondent member of the Academy, to Professors Georgyi Alexandrov, and Petr Pospelov, to member of the Academy Yemelyan Yaroslavsky, for the second volume of his scientific work "The History of the Civil War in the USSR", and to member of Academy Evgeny Tarle, for his book "The Crimean War."
In the philosophic sciences first prizes were awarded to Professors Georgyi Alexandrov and Bernard Bykhovsky, to member of the Academy Mark Mitin, to correspondent member of the Academy Pavel Yudin, to Professors Traktenberg and Valentin Asmus, for a three-volumed study "The History of Philosophy."
For many years of outstanding activities in the field of science, first prizes were awarded to members of the Academy Boris Asafyev, to Academician Vladimir Komarov, member of the Presidium of the Georgian Academy of Sciences, Semen Dzhanashvili, to Director of the Institute of Speech and Thought, and member of the Academy Boris Grekov, to members of the Academy Ivan Meshchaninov and Vladimir Mikhaylevitch, to Director of the Institute of Combustible Minerals under the Academy of Sciences of the USSR and member of the Academy Sergei Numetkin, to members of Academy Alexander Porai-Koshitz, Nikolai Chizhevsky, and Klavdy Shengier.
The second prizes of 100,000 rubles each were awarded to members of the Academy Alexander Arbuzov and Alexei Borisyak; to Major-General of Artillery Prof. Mikhail Vasiliev; to F. Vladimir Vetchinkin of the Central Institute of Aerodynamics, named after Zhukovsky, to members of Academy Vladimir Petrov, Alexei Terpigorev, and Evgeny Chudakov; to Major General of Engineering Troops Prof. Victor Yakovlev, to Professors Yefim Lisitsyn, Ivan Yakushev, members of the All-Union Lenin Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and others.—(TASS.)

Allies Advance in Tunisia
LONDON, March 24. — The Reuter's Agency reports that the 8th British Army, developing its attacks against the enemy positions, advances toward the sea in the direction of Gabes, thus menacing the rear of the German-Italian troops.
The Algiers Radio states that battles are in progress in front of Gabes, between the hilly area of Matmata and the sea. The tank units of the British 8th Army are attacking the German Army.
American and French forces are continuing to advance from Gafsa to the Bay of Gabes.—(TASS.)

Italy's Naval Forces to Stay in Home Waters
GENEVA, March 23. — Commenting on the official reports about Admiral Denits' Rome visit, the local political circles are very sceptical as regards the naval co-operation. The reports received in the past few weeks from well informed sources stress the continued aggravation of the dispute between the chief Axis partners regarding the use of the Italian Navy, and more specifically of the submarine fleet on various theatres of war.
The German insistent demands for detailing strong Italian naval forces for operations in the Atlantic Ocean and in the northern seas, encountered a vigorous opposition of the naval circles of Rome, and has become a subject of long and fruitless discussions between the Italians and the Germans.
Under various pretexts the Italians stubbornly defended the principle of "local operations" of the navy, as opposed to the doctrine of "total submarine war", as proclaimed by Denits.
The rumours of Denits' impending visit to Italy for the "settlement of problems of first rate importance" have long been current in Rome. It is now stated, that the recent Italian denial of the differences between the Italian and German naval staffs was published under the direct pressure of the Germans, since the rumours about these differences reached the general public.
According to the most recent reports from Rome, in the course of his talks with Riccardi, Denits presented to Italy a virtual ultimatum, demanding of a wide use of the Italian submarine and surface fleets, and urging immediate action in view of the heavy losses sustained by the German navy in the Atlantic.
However, the point of view of the prominent representatives of the Italian naval circles, after the Denits-Riccardi negotiations, in essence does not differ from the former attitude of the Italian Naval Ministry, and manifestly runs in opposition to the official communique. These circles state that Italy must do her utmost for the preservation of her naval forces "which will be of very big importance for her national policy."
It is rumoured that in view of the failure of the Rome negotiations, Denits, on behalf of the German Government, has invited Riccardi to visit Berlin.—(TASS.)

纳粹强渡顿涅茨河企图受挫
西南战线，3月23日电。——在丘古耶夫附近的顿涅茨河弯曲部前线及其以南地区，已变成一片烈日炙烤下的战场。
德军摩托化步兵在坦克支援下，试图抵达河边。敌人企图楔入苏联防御线的努力使其付出了极其惨重的代价。
尽管希特勒分子在数量上占优势，红军部队仍经常从敌人手中夺取主动权并将其击退。对一个多次易手的居民点的争夺尤为激烈。起初，德军采用大规模坦克突击的战术，但在遭受苏联火炮和反坦克步枪火力的沉重损失后，他们转而采取由15至25辆坦克组成的小组行动。
苏联反坦克枪手、坦克兵、炮兵和步兵 everywhere 以暴风骤雨般的火力迎击敌人，将其打回原出发阵地。日前，我军N部队的骑兵表现英勇。
德军投入了大量坦克和约一个团的步兵，企图突破苏联防御线并夺取渡口。经过长时间的炮火准备后，几群德军坦克向苏联防御线冲去。每辆坦克上都载有自动步枪手，而载有步兵的卡车则跟随在后方一定距离处。由于苏联炮兵的火力以及我军反坦克枪手的准确射击，德军损失了19辆坦克并狼狈逃窜。德军步兵无法跟上匆忙撤退的坦克，被困在泥泞的道路上，并在那里被我军骑兵追上。我军骑兵马刀闪闪，扑向德军并切断了其退路。没有一个希特勒分子能从他们惩罚性的刀锋下逃脱。在一个步兵营的敌军被歼灭在战场上，周围横陈着瘫痪的德军坦克的静止躯体。——（塔斯社。）

荷兰组建“本土军队”
斯德哥尔摩，3月23日电。——海牙宣布在荷兰组建一支用于“保卫国家免受敌人侵害”的“本土防卫军”。这支军队将隶属于帝国党卫队总部。所有18至50岁、具备所需“士气”的男子均将被征召入伍。正如命令所强调的，所有罗马天主教士兵必须宣誓效忠希特勒，此举证实荷兰人实际上是被征召服役于德国武装部队。
《荷兰德意志报》在评论此命令时指出，荷兰人必须承担某些此前完全由德国占领军负责的国防任务。同时，据该报称，新军队旨在防止国内出现无政府状态。——（塔斯社。）

科学工作者获颁斯大林奖金
莫斯科，3月24日电。——苏联人民委员会关于颁发1942年在杰出科学成就、技术和工业生产根本改进方面获得斯大林奖金的决定已公布。
物理学和数学领域的一等奖（各20万卢布）授予苏联科学院通讯院士帕维尔·亚历山德罗夫（Pavel Alexandrov），以表彰其1941-1942年发表的数学科学研究；以及授予科学院院士彼得·卡皮察（Peter Kapitsa），以表彰其发现和研究液氦的超流动性。
在技术科学领域，一等奖授予科学院通讯院士列昂尼德·莱本宗（Leonid Leibenzon），以表彰其对弹性理论和石油工业力学的研究；以及授予科学院院士米哈伊尔·巴甫洛夫（Mikhail Pavlov），以表彰其在生铁冶炼技术方面的著名著作。
在化学科学领域，一等奖授予科学院通讯院士亚历山大·内斯梅亚诺夫（Alexander Nesmeyanov），以表彰其对金属有机化合物的研究。
在地质学和地理学领域，一等奖授予科学院通讯院士费奥多西·克拉索夫斯基（Feodosiy Krasovsky），以表彰其题为《高等大地测量学》的科学著作；以及授予科学院院士弗拉基米尔·奥布鲁切夫（Vladimir Obruchev），以表彰其对顿涅茨盆地地区的地质勘探，这些成果汇总在其《苏联地质学》一书中。
在生物科学领域，一等奖授予全苏列宁农业科学院院士彼得·茹科夫斯基（Peter Zhukovsky），以表彰其著作《植物学》、发现小麦和黑麦的新品种以及通过杂交具有高经济价值的植物开发杂交种；授予苏联科学院生化研究所教授弗拉基米尔·恩格尔加特（Vladimir Engelgardt）；以及授予该研究所工作人员米利察·柳比莫娃（Militza Liubimova），以表彰其对肌肉系统的研究。
在农业科学领域，一等奖授予科学院院士特罗菲姆·李森科（Trofim Lysenko）、全苏列宁农业科学院院士瓦西里·莫索洛夫（Vassily Mossolov）以及一组科学工作者，以表彰其在农业中科学开发和引入利用马铃薯茎叶进行种植的方法。
在医学科学领域，一等奖授予医务中将维克多·谢伊图年科（Victor Sheitunenko）教授，以及军事医学院教授阿列克谢·马克西缅科夫（Alexei Maximmenkov）和安德烈·维什涅夫斯基（Andrei Vishnevsky），以表彰其科学著作《神经和静脉系统图集》。
在军事科学领域，二等奖（各10万卢布）授予列昂尼德·贡恰罗夫（Leonid Goncharov）教授，以表彰其科学著作《火炮在作战中的使用》；授予少将、教授尼古拉·德罗兹多夫（Nikolai Drozdov），以表彰其发展火炮设计方法以及在弹道学领域的研究。
在历史和语文学领域，一等奖授予科学院通讯院士伊萨克·明茨（Isaak Mintz）、格奥尔基·亚历山德罗夫（Georgyi Alexandrov）教授和彼得·波斯佩洛夫（Petr Pospelov）教授；授予科学院院士叶梅利扬·雅罗斯拉夫斯基（Yemelyan Yaroslavsky），以表彰其科学著作《苏联内战史》第二卷；以及授予科学院院士叶夫根尼·塔尔勒（Evgeny Tarle），以表彰其著作《克里米亚战争》。
在哲学科学领域，一等奖授予格奥尔基·亚历山德罗夫（Georgyi Alexandrov）教授和伯纳德·贝霍夫斯基（Bernard Bykhovsky）教授、科学院院士马尔克·米京（Mark Mitin）、科学院通讯院士帕维尔·尤金（Pavel Yudin）、特拉赫滕伯格（Traktenberg）教授和瓦伦丁·阿斯穆斯（Valentin Asmus）教授，以表彰其三卷本研究著作《哲学史》。
鉴于在科学领域多年的杰出活动，一等奖授予科学院院士鲍里斯·阿萨菲耶夫（Boris Asafyev）、科学院院士弗拉基米尔·科马罗夫（Vladimir Komarov）、格鲁吉亚科学院主席团成员谢苗·贾纳什维利（Semen Dzhanashvili）、言语与思维研究所所长兼科学院院士鲍里斯·格列科夫（Boris Grekov）、科学院院士伊万·梅夏尼诺夫（Ivan Meshchaninov）和弗拉基米尔·米哈伊列维奇（Vladimir Mikhaylevitch）、苏联科学院可燃矿物研究所所长兼科学院院士谢尔盖·努梅特金（Sergei Numetkin）、以及科学院院士亚历山大·波赖-科希茨（Alexander Porai-Koshitz）、尼古拉·奇热夫斯基（Nikolai Chizhevsky）和克拉夫季·申吉尔（Klavdy Shengier）。
二等奖（各10万卢布）授予科学院院士亚历山大·阿尔布佐夫（Alexander Arbuzov）和阿列克谢·博里西亚克（Alexei Borisyak）；炮兵少将、教授米哈伊尔·瓦西里耶夫（Mikhail Vasiliev）；茹科夫斯基中央空气流体动力学研究院的弗拉基米尔·韦特钦金（F. Vladimir Vetchinkin）；科学院院士弗拉基米尔·彼得罗夫（Vladimir Petrov）、阿列克谢·特尔皮戈列夫（Alexei Terpigorev）和叶夫根尼·丘达科夫（Evgeny Chudakov）；工程兵少将、教授维克多·雅科夫列夫（Victor Yakovlev）；叶菲姆·利西岑（Yefim Lisitsyn）教授、伊万·亚库舍夫（Ivan Yakushev）教授（全苏列宁农业科学院院士）等。——（塔斯社。）

盟军在突尼斯推进
伦敦，3月24日电。——路透社报道，英国第8集团军在加强对敌方阵地的攻击，向加贝斯方向朝海岸推进，从而威胁德意军队的后方。
阿尔及尔广播电台称，在马特马塔丘陵地区与海岸之间的加贝斯前方正在进行战斗。英国第8集团军的坦克部队正在进攻德军。
美法军队正继续从加夫萨向加贝斯湾推进。——（塔斯社。）

意大利海军力量将留守本国水域
日内瓦，3月23日电。——当地政治界对有关邓尼茨海军上将访问罗马的官方报道持非常怀疑态度，尤其是在海军合作方面。过去几周从消息灵通人士处收到的报道强调，轴心国主要伙伴之间关于意大利海军、特别是潜艇舰队在各战区的使用问题上的争端持续加剧。
德国坚持要求抽调强大的意大利海军力量在大西洋和北部海域作战，遭到了罗马海军界的强烈反对，并成为意德之间长期且毫无结果的讨论主题。
意大利人以各种借口顽固地捍卫海军“局部作战”的原则，这与邓尼茨所宣称的“全面潜艇战”学说相对立。
关于邓尼茨即将访问意大利以“解决头等重要性问题”的传闻在罗马流传已久。现在据悉，此前意大利否认意德海军参谋部之间存在分歧的声明是在德国的直接压力下发布的，因为有关这些分歧的传闻已传至公众耳中。
根据来自罗马的最新报道，在与里卡尔迪（Riccardi）的会谈中，邓尼茨向意大利提出了事实上的最后通牒，要求广泛使用意大利的潜艇和水面舰队，并鉴于德国海军在大西洋遭受的重大损失，敦促立即采取行动。
然而，在邓尼茨-里卡尔迪谈判后，意大利海军界重要代表的观点本质上与意大利海军部以前的态度并无不同，且明显与官方公报相悖。这些圈子表示，意大利必须竭尽全力保存其海军力量，“这对其国家政策至关重要。”
有传闻称，鉴于罗马谈判失败，邓尼茨代表德国政府邀请里卡尔迪访问柏林。——（塔斯社。）

SUBJECT: S.M. Lehem

Soloman. M. Lehem, British-Jew, was born at Aden on May 5th, 1911. Until August 1940 he was the owner of an import and export business at Aden. He arrived in Shanghai on August 25th 1940. From February to July 1941 he was employed with the Mercury Press on the publication of the Dollar Directory. He offered to purchase the business of the Dollar Directory from the Mercury Press but they were not willing to sell outright and he was made a partner in the concern for which he put up the sum of $4,000. The Mercury Press, however, became displeased with Mr. Lehem's work, or rather his lack of work, and released him at the end of his six month's contract, The $4,000 being returned to him.

S.M. Lehem is understood to be quite sound financially. He is married and is a cousin of Mr. Razon of Razon's Trading Company.

He is registered at H.B.M. Consulate and holds a British Aden Passport No.640.

There is nothing known or recorded to Mr. S.M. Lehem's detriment in S.M.P. records.

Lehem，英籍犹太人，1911年5月5日出生于亚丁。直至1940年8月，他在亚丁拥有一家进出口商行。他于1940年8月25日抵达上海。1941年2月至7月期间，他受雇于 Mercury Press，参与《美元行名录》（Dollar Directory）的出版工作。他曾提出从 Mercury Press 购买《美元行名录》的业务，但对方不愿 outright 出售，于是他成为该公司的合伙人，出资4,000美元。然而，Mercury Press 对 Lehem 先生的工作，或者更确切地说是他的无所事事感到不满，并在其六个月合同期满时解除了与他的关系，4,000美元已退还给他。

REPORT

Section 4 Crime
& Special Branch
Station........................................ File No.................... Date April 13th, 1943.

SUBJECT: Application for re-registration of the
"Shanghai Medical Journal".

With reference to the attached application regard-
ing the re-registration of the "Shanghai Medical Journal"
(monthly magazine), I beg to state the following:-

Mr. F. Bury (former publisher) intended to transfer
the said publication to Mr. G. Poliak, a partner of
the "Zenith Agencies". Reasons for the transfer given
by Mr. Bury were that owing to lack of funds he was
no longer able to publish this magazine and therefore
sold it for $1000 to Mr. G. Poliak of the "Zenith
Agencies" who purchased all rights and interests in
respect of the journal from Mr. Bury. However,
on the 1st of April 1943, Mr. Bury died and Mr. G.
Poliak applied to continue publishing this journal.

Mr. G. Poliak, Russian Emigrant, is the partner
of "Zenith Agencies", 181, Kiangse Road, Room 1003
Tel. No. 19733 (paper printing and advertising) regis-
tered with the Russian Emigrants Committee. He was
born on November 26th 1908 in Chita (Russia) and
arrived in Shanghai in 1915 and has never been known
to interest himself in political matters. Hence he
is not likely to misuse the magazine. At present,
he is residing at 71 Route Kaufmann Merchant.

The said journal is published in English, German,
and Chinese and is to be distributed free of charge.
The first copy of the "Shanghai Medical Journal" was
published on 1st January 1940. (S.M.P. Registration

P. T. O.

鉴于所附关于《上海医学杂志》（月刊）重新注册的申请，谨陈述如下：

F. Bury 先生（前出版人）拟将该出版物转让给“Zenith Agencies”的合伙人 G. Poliak 先生。Bury 先生给出的转让原因是，由于资金短缺，他已无法继续出版该杂志，因此以1000美元的价格将其出售给“Zenith Agencies”的 G. Poliak 先生，后者从 Bury 先生处购买了该期刊的所有权利和权益。然而，1943年4月1日，Bury 先生去世，G. Poliak 先生申请继续出版该期刊。

G. Poliak 先生，俄裔流亡者，系“Zenith Agencies”（江西路181号1003室，电话19733，从事纸张印刷及广告业务）的合伙人，已在俄侨委员会注册。他于1908年11月26日出生于赤塔（俄国），1915年抵达上海，从未被发现对政治事务感兴趣。因此，他不太可能滥用该杂志。目前，他居住在考夫曼商人路71号。

Freights vergas Wall Street 


The real present antithogis is between Wall 
Street and the ocean freight market, because the latter is 
the tangible barometer of the state of international trade, 
particularly in the primary products. Wall Street currently 
collapsing is not consonant with the ocean freight merket 
currently booming; remains to be sesn which of them will 
disprove the other. The worst one can say of the freight 
markets 1s that they look too true to be good, yet true they 
dindubitably are. Just to think of how the owners bowed down 
year after year to anyone who made a noise like a potential 
charterer - and now the biggest international wheat houses 
are bidding 34s. Ode for Febd-March (new-crop) space from the 
Plate, only to find the owners fallinz over themselves backwards. 
There are less than a dozen unfixed ships committed to arrive 
in the Plate this yeare 


Action is equal and opposite to reaction: it 
is because of the years and years when snipping was driven to 
the wall of the breaker's yard that there 1s now not enough 
space to go round. When Lord Craigmyle says that it is as 
certain as anything in this world that the present freight boom 
will not endure for the 15 or 20 years ordinarily needed to 
amortize the cost of a new vessel, it is almost equally certain 
that it will endure =- and very likely accentuate - for the 
next 15 or 20 weeks, a period which mey be of more immediate 
importance.

Agents, Room 44a, 89 Foochow Road. He is a registered 
British subject and nothing is known to his detriment 
at the British Consulate-General. 

In its first issue which appeared on June 10, 
1938, the paper contained the following paragraph: - 

“tWe shall support no party, be the agent 
of no faction or coterie, and care nothing for 
any election, or any candidate from president 
down to consulate.’ This was the policy of 
James Gordon Bennett, founder of the 'New York 

E Herald.' We cannot do better than attempt a 
modest emlation of this policy." 

A few months ago, it was reported that the paper 
received a subsidy from the Japanese but no confirmation 
was obtained. 

The circulation of the paper is very poor and 
only about 1,000 copies per issue are being printed 
at the "China Press" for which the "Evening Echo" 

' {) pays about $2,600 per mensem to the “China Press."

a journalist, $94.18 as 12 days salary in arrears and 
$31.25 as court and lawyer's fees. Mr. Steiner stated 
in Court that he had resigned owing to the poor working 
conditions and also because he had heard that the paper 
was being subsidized by the Japanese.

CRIME-RIDDEN SHANGHAI ‘ 


HE approach of the old Chinese New Year, now known 
. as the Spring Festival, is generally accompanied by an 
increase of crime. It‘is the most important day settlement 
day of the year and consequently many are forced to dis- 
honest, to say nothing’ of desperate, remedies in order to 
meet their commitments. 


762" 


Nowadays there are many factors contributing to an. 


exacerbation nf crime; come Sf them are polivical and are 
concerned with the current hostilities, while others may be 
described as economic. Searcely a day passes without at 
least one—and generally several—armed rubberies, hold-ups 
and shootings, which are keeping both the Settlement and 
the Concession police extremely busy. 


There is much want in this city and those who are hun- 
gry become desperaté, committing acts in their extremity 
which would never occur in more normal times. Together 
with the tens of thousands of refugees now being harbour- 
ed in Shanghai have come many criminal characters, while 
there is reason to believe that not a few guerillas as well 
as soldiers who were formerly fighting with the Chinese 
armies, but who have been cut off from their units, have 
been forced through privation to seek a means of keeping 
body and soul together by joining the ranks of Shanghai’s 
underworld. 


It can he easily understood that, owing to the severe 
fighting in the areas surrounding Shanghai large quantities 
of fireavins have fpund their way into the city, many of 
which were doubtless picked up from the corpses of dead 
soldiers, and these have found their way, together with 
large quantities of small-arms ammunition, into the hands 
of gangsters. Periods of warfare are the cause of large 
numbers of men becoming familiar with the use of firearms 
and the development of a psychosis which holds life cheap, 
so that they will take desperate risks with their own in the 
hope of securing a few dollars. It was only a day or two 
ago that a gangster met his death at the hands of the Set- 
tlement police in a running street fight after he had at- 
tempted to rob a blind fortune-teller. 


Such men can be hired for a few dollars to commit 
political assassinations and many such have occurred in re- 
cent months, chiefly of thoue who have accepted.ofics. under 
the Ta Tao Government. % 23 

Assassinations perpetrated by crazed fanatics for poli- 
tical reasons are despicable enough, but it: is impossible to 
find words to express sufficient contempt for those who com- 
mit such acts for money. 


This city has always been a happy hunting ground for 
gamblers who have never found any lack of amenities for 
indulging their weakness, and present conditions-lend them- 
selves to an increase of such activities. “Easy money” in- 
variably attracts large numbers of the worst elements with 
the result that even the fortunate minority who leave a 
“gambling-joint” with more in their pockets than. when 
they entered are by no. means sure of: getting their:cash’ or 
their persons safely home.’ A 


Allegations have been.made of failure of the various 
authorities responsible for the maintenance of law and order 
to co-operate, but such are the present abnormal conditions 
in and around Shanghai that it is, surprising that such a 
large percentage: of those’ committing: offences: against. the 
law. are brought so swiftly to justice, )

HE EVENING ECHO makes its first appearance today 

and we trust that those Shanghailanders who scan its 

modest four pages for the first time will remember that the 
acorn came before the oak. 


We also derive considerable solace and encouragement 
from the reflection that the great James Gordon Bennett, 
founder of the New York Herald, started his paper (for 
which he charged one cent) in a cellar and was editor, 
publisher, printer, reporter and salesman. 

He was frequently compelled in the last capacity to 
combine it with that of fistic handyman, as a.number of his 
readers were unable to appreciate his frequent very out- 
spoken and pungent comments. concerning their real or 
fancied moral obliquities. These encounters in the journalis- 
tic cause usually occurred in the streets, so Bennett gained 
plenty of free publicity. 

We trust, however, that we shall be spared this last, |! 
but not least, important pkase of his many-sided activities. | 

Bennett fixed the policy of his paper from the very 
beginning and adhered to it to the day of his death. It was 
as follows: 

“We shall support no party, be the agent of no faction 
or coterie, and care nothing for any election, or any 
candidate from president down to constable.” 

We cannot do better than attempt a modest emula- 
tion of this policy. = ; 

We propose strictly to eschew all political matters, but 
shall not -hesitate to take a strong view, when we-consider | 
it necessary, on matters concerning the public welfare of this 
city, among whose residents. we trust we shall have a 
steadily increasing number of readers. 

We were born in difficult times and no part. of.the world 
is now free from anxiety. He would be a bold man who 
ventured to predict what lies in store for the human race 

!} during the next few years or even months. ; 
: Here, for the past ten months, we have been in the 
midst of an undeclared war, with its inevitable concomitants 
of trade paralysis and yncertainty, but Shanghai has 
weathered many crises in_the past, always shewing 
= powers of resiliency and recuperation, and his-|: 


cet te 


tory has an uncanny habit of repeating itself. 
Wars do not last forever and sooner or later the fabric of 

‘}our commerce will again be found licking its wounds and 
those wounds will not prove fatal; they will, as always in 
the past, heal. . 

We have endeavoured to attune the rates of the EVEN. 
ING ECHO to the times and are confident that they will 
make their appeal to the Shanghai public. : 

We trust that we may merit the very encouraging sup- 
‘port Which we have so far beén accorded, both from. those 
who have already enrolled themselves as subscribers, and 
from advertisers.

My dear Mr. f&hillips, 

I veg to draw your attention to an article published on 
Page 83 of the June 2lst issue of the China Weekly Review. You 
will notice that the article contains utterly false and most 
derogatory references to our Imperial Family. 

, You will be informed that some time ago our Consul- 
General requested the Chairman of the Municipal Council to take 
steps against the "Parade" which also contained slanderous 
remarks regarding our Imperial Family. I need not dwell upon 
how inimical these articles are to friendly relations between 
various communities here, but I would like to remind you how 
sensitive our people are toward any reference to our Imperial Family. 

Apart from the legal question of the right of the 
Municipal Council to control the publication in the International 
Settlement, or of the extraterritorial character of the weekly 
magazine in question, I am convinced that something can be done 
regarding such a publication for the greater cause of tranquility 
in this international community. 

I should be very grateful if you would find it possible 
to take a statesmanlike view of the situation, and adopt any 
measure that may effectively withhold the above-mentioned issue 
of the magazine from circulation and warn the editor against a 
repetition. 

I remain,

OVER THE COFFINS OF WHITE RENEGADES WHO RAISED

Recently, the English Telegraph Agency - Reuter printed a 
report from their correspondent in the Japanese-Nongolian 


frontier:- 
seccceee"l HAVE SEEN COVFINS COVERED WITH WHITE MATERIAL WITH

THEIR OWN BLOOD". This short report started gossip among 
Russian emigrants in the Far East and words of bitter condemna- 
tion of those fascists fighting in the ranks of the Japanese 
Army could be heard everywhere in town. This is how the ; 
emigrants by an overwhelming majority are expressing their 
opinion on the story. 

It is obvious that we agree with those opinions. We, by no 
means hate the Japanese, but our relations towerds them are 
the same as they are to the Chinese, the “nglish, the Germans 
and the French, i.e. absolutely indifferent, but in the same 
time we are citizens who love our mother-country and its 
happiness comes first with us before anything else. 

This is perfectly netural and is understood by everyone, but 

a war has broken out and the army of my country has clashed 
with the Japanese army on the field of battle. I, according 
to special circumstances, am living on the enemy side. What 
dest I do? First and foremost is to keep outwardly indiffer- 
ent, but it is impossible to keep silent the voice of true 
blood. 

There is no one to believe that Russian emigrants are indiff”

ent inwardly to the present military action and an overyw>

majority, no matter what their feelings are towards the! exis,

rule in their mother-country, feel sorry for every defea arg 


| 


happy at every success. 

But there is unhealthy, cemetry like atmosphere amongst the 
Russian emigrants which is reflected in a new kind of living 
creature. Ugly vampires who keep themselves alive by sucking 
the blood of their brothers. And yet they do not know how much 
ef that trothers blood they heve spilled in cells of Harbin 


prisons. And in the ranks of tne rannion they are fighting 
ageinst the Red Army - the thirst for Russian blood attrects unw 


to the front. 


Of course, these pitiful individuals ere not an asset to the 
Japanese Army, but the mere fact of their presence in the enemy 
ranks (and that presence is absolutely voluntary), raises in 

us a feeling of high indignation. 

We are sure that the Japanese have the same feeling of contempt 
and squeamishness towards those renegades and consider them 
mercenaries, who crawl on their paunch in front of their masters 
or hateful degenerates with crooked brains. 

The Japanese people in general are healthy people and a 
patriotic feeling is cultivated amongst them, so it is only 
natural to suppose that the above feelings are general amongst 
them. 

We, the Russian emigrants, can only clench our teeth and whisper:- 


- Disgrace, Disgrace.
